{{nihongo|'''Juri Ueno'''|上野 樹里|Ueno Juri|born 25 May 1986}} is a Japanese actress. She first gained recognition in the 2004 film ''[[Swing Girls]]'' where she was a recipient of Newcomer of the Year prize at the [[Japanese Academy Awards]]. Ueno achieved mainstream success for playing the title role in the live-action adaptations of manga ''[[Nodame Cantabile]]'' for which she won Best Lead Actress at the 51st Television Drama Academy Awards in 2007. She further gained acclaim with her role in the television series ''[[Last Friends]]'' for which she won Best Supporting Actress at the Nikkan Sports Drama Grand Prix<ref name="last_friends_award">{{cite web|url=http://www.tokyograph.com/news/id-3529|title=Drama Grand Prix: "CHANGE" and "Last Friends" win for Fuji TV|publisher=Tokyograph|access-date=21 March 2015}}</ref> and the 57th Television Drama Academy Awards in 2008.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blog.television.co.jp/drama/academy/2008/08/post_304.html|title=Best Supporting Actress|language=ja|publisher=Television Drama Academy Awards|access-date=21 March 2015|archive-date=9 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140809212646/http://blog.television.co.jp/drama/academy/2008/08/post_304.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Career==
Ueno made her television debut in 2002 at the age of 16 in the [[NHK]] series ''Seizon'' before making her first film major appearance in 2003 in ''Chirosoku no Natsu'' which won her the Sponichi Grand Prize New Talent Award at the [[Mainichi Film Awards]] along with her performance in the 2004 film, ''[[Swing Girls]]''. ''Swing Girls'' proved to be a breakthrough when she received critical acclaim and awards for Best Newcomer at the [[Yokohama Film Festival]] (she was also honored for her performance in ''Joze to Tora to Sakana Tachi'') and the [[Japan Academy Prize (film)|Japanese Academy Awards]].

In 2004, Ueno took on a supporting role in [[Tokyo Broadcasting System|TBS]]'s romance drama, ''[[Orange Days (TV series)|Orange Days]]'', and co-starred in 2005 with [[Takuya Kimura]] in [[Fuji TV]]'s romantic comedy ''[[Engine (TV series)|Engine]]'' as Misae Hoshino. She also appeared with [[Kazuya Kamenashi]] in the special television movie of ''[[Kindaichi Case Files|Kinda'ichi Shōnen no Jikenbo]]'' the same year taking over the role of Miyuki Nanase from [[Anne Suzuki]].

Ueno's popularity rose further when she was cast as Megumi Noda ("Nodame") in the 2006 live-action television adaptation of the popular [[manga]] ''[[Nodame Cantabile]]''. Co-starring opposite [[Hiroshi Tamaki]], the series' 11-episode run was a success with an average viewership rating of 18.79% with the season finalé garnering 21.7% of the viewership share for its time slot. Ueno's portrayal as the eccentric and disorganized but yet extremely affable and talented pianist won her "Best Lead Actress" at the 51st Television Drama Academy Awards while the show won "Best Drama". The show was also recognized overseas at the 2nd Seoul Drama Festival where it was awarded "Best Miniseries". Ueno and Tamaki reprised their roles in 2007 in the two-part special, ''Nodame Cantabile Shinshun Special in Europe'', which chronicles their individual struggles to achieve success on Europe's storied classical music stage whilst being away from each other.

In 2008, Ueno reunited with ''Nodame'' co-stars [[Eita Nagayama|Eita]] and [[Asami Mizukawa]] in Fuji TV's drama, ''[[Last Friends]]'', as Ruka Kishimoto, a talented [[motocross]] racer with a hidden secret she cannot discuss with friends or family. Taeko Asano, the [[screenwriter]] of ''Last Friends'' praised Ueno's acting of Ruka, stating that Ueno is a "natural genius" and that she became "the character itself".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tokyowrestling.com/articles/2008/06/last_friends_4.html |title=日本初レズビアン＆クィアカルチャーWebマガジン｜TokyoWrestling.com |publisher=Tokyowrestling.com |access-date=2015-03-27 |archive-date=2017-03-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170313041629/http://www.tokyowrestling.com/articles/2008/06/last_friends_4.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> Ueno won "Best Supporting Actress" at the 12th Nikkan Sports Drama Grand Prix and The 57th Television Drama Academy Awards for her role.<ref name="last_friends_award"/> She was recognised as "Best Student Voice Actress" at the 2008 MTV Student Voice Awards for her role in ''Wanko''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tokyograph.com/news/id-3707|title=Student Voice Awards: Oguri wins again|publisher=Tokyograph|access-date=21 March 2015}}</ref>

The Japanese version of ''[[Vogue (magazine)|Vogue]]'' named her as one of the "Women of the Year 2008".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tokyograph.com/news/id-4091|title=Aoi Miyazaki, Juri Ueno named Vogue's Women of the Year|publisher=Tokyograph|access-date=21 March 2015}}</ref>

On 9 December 2008, it was announced that she would reprise her role as "Nodame" in a new ''Nodame Cantabile'' two-movie sequel slated for release in 2010,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tokyograph.com/news/id-4158|title=Two "Nodame Cantabile" films planned for 2010|publisher=Tokyograph|access-date=21 March 2015}}</ref> with filming to start in May 2009.<ref>[http://www.sanspo.com/geino/news/081210/gnj0812100506016-n2.htm] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081212051927/http://www.sanspo.com/geino/news/081210/gnj0812100506016-n2.htm|date=December 12, 2008}}</ref>

On 25 January 2010, it was announced that Ueno would be the lead in the 2011 NHK Taiga drama ''[[Gō (TV series)|Gō]]'' based on an original script by ''[[Atsuhime (drama)|Atsuhime]]'' writer {{nihongo|Kumiko Tabuchi|田渕 久美子|Tabuchi Kumiko}}.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tokyograph.com/news/id-5730|title=Juri Ueno to lead 2011 taiga drama|publisher=Tokyograph|access-date=21 March 2015}}</ref> with filming starting in August 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://contents.oricon.co.jp/news/movie/73446/|title=2011年度NHK大河主演に上野樹里 "先輩"福山雅治からのエールに歓喜|date=17 February 2010 |language=ja|publisher=[[Oricon]]|access-date=21 March 2015}}</ref> The series is Ueno's first role in a historical drama. ''Gō'' is NHK's 50th Taiga drama, and only its 10th drama with a woman as the main character. On April 15, 2010, Ueno took the role of "Haru" in the spring J-Drama [[Sunao ni Narenakute]] which tells a story of the blossoming friendship between five people through [[Twitter]], along with [[Eita Nagayama|Eita]]], [[Hero Jaejoong]], [[Megumi Seki]] and [[Tetsuji Tamayama]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://wwwz.fujitv.co.jp/sunao/index.html |title=Ueno Juri with Eita, Jaejoong, Megumi and Tetsuji |publisher=FujiTv.co.jp |access-date=21 March 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121225044842/http://wwwz.fujitv.co.jp/sunao/index.html |archive-date=25 December 2012 }}</ref>

On 11 September 2010, Ueno guest starred in the Korean variety show [[Munhwa Broadcasting Corporation|MBC]]'s ''[[We Got Married]]'' Season 2 while promoting ''[[Nodame Cantabile - The Movie]]'' and paid a visit to [[Girls' Generation|SNSD]]'s [[Seohyun]] and [[CN Blue]]'s [[Jung Yong-hwa]]. In 2013 she returned to acting with a leading role in the romance film ''[[Girl in the Sunny Place]]'' opposite actor [[Jun Matsumoto]] which was based on the best selling novel of the same name.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.shinchosha.co.jp/book/135361/|title=越谷オサム『陽だまりの彼女』｜新潮社|publisher=Shinchosha.co.jp|access-date=2015-03-27|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150303202800/http://www.shinchosha.co.jp/book/135361/|archive-date=2015-03-03}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.ameba.jp/20131007-21/ |title=愛される女優・上野樹里の魅力とは？ 「陽だまりの彼女」現場に有名監督たちが陣中見舞い - Ameba News [アメーバニュース] |publisher=News.ameba.jp |date=1994-12-01 |access-date=2015-03-27}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tokyohive.com/article/2013/10/ueno-juri-talks-about-matsumoto-jun-and-hidamari-no-kanojo |title=Ueno Juri talks about Matsumoto Jun and 'Hidamari no Kanojo' |publisher=Tokyohive.com |date=2013-10-12 |access-date=2015-03-27}}</ref> The film opened in Japanese theaters on October 12 and was a commercial success topping the box office and grossing ¥763 million after eight days.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.filmbiz.asia/news/domestic-films-lead-japan-box-office |title=Domestic films lead Japan box office |publisher=Filmbiz.asia |date=2013-10-23 |access-date=2015-03-27}}</ref>

In 2014 she starred in the [[Tokyo Broadcasting System|TBS]] revenge drama ''Alice no Toge'' as Mizuno Asumi a young woman who becomes a doctor at the hospital her father was treated at in order to get revenge on those responsible for his death.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://crazy9drama.wordpress.com/2014/04/06/drama-news-ueno-juri-seeks-revenge-in-alice-no-toge/ |title=[Drama News] Ueno Juri Seeks Revenge in Alice no Toge | A Dramatic Life |publisher=Crazy9drama.wordpress.com |date=2014-04-06 |access-date=2015-03-27}}</ref> This was followed by another leading role in the [[Tokyo Broadcasting System|TBS]] television drama ''Ouroboros'' based on the manga of the same name and opposite actors [[Toma Ikuta]] and [[Shun Oguri]]. This marks her first time starring in a detective drama.<ref name="tokyohive1">{{cite web|url=http://www.tokyohive.com/article/2014/11/ueno-juri-to-take-on-her-first-detective-role-in-drama-ouroboros |title=Ueno Juri to take on her first detective role in drama 'Ouroboros' |publisher=Tokyohive.com |date=2014-11-16 |access-date=2015-03-27}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://aramajapan.com/news/tvmovie/dramas/ueno-juri-joins-oguri-shun-and-ikuta-toma-in-ouroboros/13273/ |title=Ueno Juri joins Oguri Shun and Ikuta Toma in "Ouroboros" |publisher=Aramajapan.com |date=2015-01-31 |access-date=2015-03-27}}</ref> and she joined alongside Korean singer [[T.O.P]] for romantic [[Web series|Web drama]] titled ''Secret Message''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.soompi.com/2015/03/30/bigbangs-t-o-p-to-star-alongside-juri-ueno-in-new-drama/|title = BIGBANG's T.O.P to Star Alongside Juri Ueno in New Drama| date=31 March 2015 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://kpopherald.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=201509161623379678411_2|title='Secret Message' starring T.O.P and Juri Ueno will premiere in November |date=16 September 2015 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.kpopstarz.com/articles/241226/20150916/big-bang-top-secret-message.htm|title=T.O.P's Japanese-Korean Series 'Secret Message' to Hit the Web in November|date=16 September 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.allkpop.com/article/2015/09/title-and-tentative-airing-date-for-ueno-juri-and-tops-web-drama-series-finally-revealed|title = Title and tentative airing date for Ueno Juri and T.O.P's web drama series finally revealed!}}</ref>

In 2021, Ueno starred in 'Is Love Sustainable?'

== Personal life ==
Ueno married [[Triceratops (band)|Triceratops]] band member Sho Wada on May 26, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ueno Juri and TRICERATOPS' Wada Sho tie the knot|url=http://www.tokyohive.com/article/2016/05/ueno-juri-and-triceratops-wada-sho-tie-the-knot|website=Tokyo Hive}}</ref>

charter members to support JKT48. She is also a former member of the sub-unit [[French Kiss (band)|French Kiss]].{{cite web|url=http://mv.avex.jp/french-kiss/profile/ |title=Profile | フレンチ・キス |publisher=Mv.avex.jp |date=n.d.|access-date=November 13, 2011}} == Career == [[File:Aki Takajo.jpg|thumb|left|Takajō at J!-ENT Live, Los Angeles, in 2011]] Takajō auditioned for [[AKB48]] and was chosen in the group's sixth generation, also known as the third generation of Kenkyusei (trainees). She debuted on August 23, 2008, in the concert "Live DVD wa Derudarou kedo, Yappari Nama ni Kagiruze". On October 19, she substituted for [[Haruna Kojima]] on the Team A Fifth Stage, "Renai Kinshi Jorei". On December 29, Takajō was promoted to AKB48's Team A; she only spent 71 days from theater debut to full member, and it was the fastest promotion in AKB48 history at the time, until [[Rion Azuma]] from [[SKE48]] was promoted in 2013. {{citation needed|date=November 2013}} Takajō's first A-side with AKB48 was in 2010 for the single "[[Ponytail to Shushu]]". In the 2010 AKB48 general elections, she placed 13th and landed a spot on the title track for "[[Heavy Rotation (song)|Heavy Rotation]]". She and AKB48 members [[Yuki Kashiwagi]] and [[Asuka Kuramochi]] formed a sub-unit, "[[French Kiss (band)|French Kiss]]" and the group released the single "Zutto Mae Kara" which peaked at number five on the Oricon charts. On August 24, 2012, the first day of its Tokyo Dome concert series, AKB48 announced a reorganization of its teams. Takajō and [[Haruka Nakagawa]] were sent to Jakarta to help AKB48's sister group [[JKT48]].{{cite web |url=http://www.akb48.co.jp/news/detail.php?id=7929 |title= Reformation of AKB48 in Tokyo Dome Concert |date=August 24, 2012 |language=ja}}{{cite web | url = http://www.crunchyroll.com/anime-news/2012/08/24/akb48-announces-tectonic-line-up-shift | title = AKB48 Announces Tectonic Line-Up Shift | date = August 24, 2012 | last = Green | first = Scott | work = Crunchyroll }} On April 28, 2013, it was announced that she would hold a concurrent position in AKB48 Team B.{{cite web|url=http://natalie.mu/music/news/89690|script-title=ja:AKB48、夏に5大ドーム公演決定＆新たなグループ兼任発表|access-date=June 7, 2015|publisher=Natasha, Inc.|language=ja}} On February 24, 2014, during the Grand Reformation Festival, it was announced that she was released from her concurrent positions in JKT48. In 2015, she was transferred to AKB48 Team K.{{cite web|url=http://www.tokyohive.com/article/2015/03/akb48-announces-reshuffling-of-personnel-kawaei-rinas-graduation|title=AKB48 announces reshuffling of personnel + Kawaei Rina's graduation|access-date=June 7, 2015|work=Tokyohive|publisher=6Theory Media, LLC}} On December 15, 2015, at the group's ''AKB48 Kōhaku Uta Gassen'' event, she announced that she would be leaving the group. On February 23, 2016, AKB48 gave her a graduation ceremony.{{Cite web|url=http://lifestyle.sindonews.com/read/1083974/157/aki-takajo-umumkan-tanggal-konser-terakhir-bersama-akb48-1455016662|title = Aki Takajō Umumkan Tanggal Konser Terakhir Bersama AKB48}} She officially graduated from AKB48 on May 1, 2016. She left Watanabe Productions and became a freelancer the next day, May 2.{{cite web|url=https://www.oricon.co.jp/news/2071080/full/|script-title=ja:元AKB48高城亜樹が所属事務所を退社 5月からフリー転向|access-date=August 22, 2018|publisher=oricon ME inc.|language=ja |date=May 2, 2016 }} On November 20, 2017, she announced her affiliation with the film production company and talent agency Is.Field.{{cite web|url=https://mdpr.jp/news/detail/1729260|script-title=ja:元AKB48高城亜樹、所属事務所移籍を発表 卒業後初のファンイベント開催|access-date=May 7, 2021|publisher=modelpress|language=ja |date=March 21, 2017 }} On October 3, 2025, '''Park Sang-hyun''' ({{Korean|hangul=박상현}}; born October 7, 1990),<ref name="천둥 박상현" /><ref name="Park Sang Hyun Thunder" /><ref name="Russell2014">{{cite book|author=Mark Russell|title=K-Pop Now!: The Korean Music Revolution|page=64|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=etDZAwAAQBAJ|date=April 29, 2014|publisher=Tuttle Publishing|isbn=978-1-4629-1411-1}}</ref> known professionally as '''Thunder''' ({{Korean|천둥||'''Cheondung'''}}), is a South Korean singer, songwriter, actor and model. He is a former member of South Korean boy band [[MBLAQ]]. On December 16, 2014, it was announced that he had departed from the group to focus on studying music.<ref name="withdrawn">Cheondung's Departure from MBLAQ [http://mwave.interest.me/enewsworld/en/article/83204/lee-joon-and-cheon-dung-release-official-statement-on-ending-promotions-as-mblaq "Lee Joon and Cheon Dung Release Official Statement on Ending Promotions as MBLAQ"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141216082504/http://mwave.interest.me/enewsworld/en/article/83204/lee-joon-and-cheon-dung-release-official-statement-on-ending-promotions-as-mblaq |date=December 16, 2014 }}, ''[[Mnet (TV channel)|Mwave]]'', December 16, 2014. Retrieved on December 16, 2014.</ref> He signed with Mystic Entertainment's music label APOP on February 11, 2015<ref name="천둥, 미스틱엔터테인먼트 에이팝과 전속 계약…윤종신 품으로" /><ref name="Naver" /> and released his debut extended play on December 7, 2016.

==Life and career==
===1990–2008: Early life and career beginnings===
Park Sang-hyun was born in Busan, South Korea, but grew up in the Philippines. He has two elder sisters, [[Sandara Park|Sandara]] and Durami. Aside from his native [[Korean language|Korean]], he is also fluent in English and [[Tagalog language|Tagalog]], and can speak conversational [[Standard Mandarin|Mandarin]] and Japanese.

His eldest sister, Sandara, achieved nationwide fame in the Philippines in 2004 after becoming the runner-up on the first season of ''[[Star Circle Quest]]'', a talent search reality competition. He first appeared on national television when he attended the finale with his mother. Later on, as his sister began her hectic activities as a celebrity, a crew from one of South Korea's biggest television agencies recorded her daily life in the documentary ''My Name Is Sandara Park''. This marked Thunder's first ever appearance on South Korean television.

Sandara's eventual decision to pursue activities in their home country led to their family's return to South Korea in 2007. By this time, Thunder had finished secondary education in the Philippines. It was later on revealed in a magazine interview that he had originally decided to pursue a professional career as a soccer player, specifically as a midfielder. He gave up and instead started auditioning for entertainment agencies, one of which was [[JYP Entertainment]]. He had taken dancing workshops offered by Sandara's home network back in the Philippines.

Thunder eventually became a trainee under [[LOEN Entertainment]], where he met [[IU (entertainer)|IU]]. He appeared in IU's debut music video for her song "Lost Child" and was also seen in a couple of videos with her wherein they sing [[Big Bang (South Korean band)|Big Bang]]'s "Lies" and [[Super Junior]]'s "Sorry Sorry."

===2015–present: Return to acting and ''Thunder''===
In 2015, he was cast in the role of Kang Hyun-seo in the MBC drama ''[[Make a Woman Cry]]''. Starting with this drama, he is being credited by his birth name (except for music-related projects). In 2016, he made a cameo appearance on another MBC drama, ''[[Woman with a Suitcase]]'', as Cheondung, a lawyer interviewing for the same job as Ma Seok-woo (played by Lee Joon).

On November 23, 2016, Mystic Entertainment revealed that Thunder would release new music in December. His self-titled debut extended play as a solo artist was released on December 7, 2016, and featured guest appearances by [[Goo Hara]], [[Basick]] and Giantpink. Thunder participated in writing and composing all five tracks. The music video for the promotional single "Sign" features his sister Sandara.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.soompi.com/2016/12/06/watch-thunder-makes-first-solo-comeback-two-years-sign-mv-featuring-sandara-park/|title=Watch: Thunder Makes First Solo Comeback In Two Years With "Sign" MV Featuring Sandara Park|work=Soompi|date=December 6, 2016|accessdate=December 7, 2016}}</ref>

{{Short description|Norwegian actress (born 1985)}}[[File:Heidi Ruud Ellingsen Drømmerollen finale 2007 Gimme Gimme Jan Erik Teigen Fremover.jpg|thumb|Ellingsen performing in the finale of ''Drømmerollen'' (2007). Photo: Jan Erik Teigen/Fremover]]'''Heidi Ruud Ellingsen''' (born 26 July 1985) is a Norwegian musical theatre performer, actress and singer. She is known for leading roles in stage productions and for appearances in television and film.

She gained wider attention in 2007 after winning the [[NRK1]] television competition ''[[Drømmerollen]]'',<ref>{{Cite web |last=Riise |first=Hege Bakken |date=2007-11-20 |title=Heidi vant drømmerollen |url=https://www.nrk.no/kultur/heidi-vant-drommerollen-1.4096106 |url-status=live |access-date=2026-03-01 |website=NRK |language=nb-NO}}</ref> which led to her casting as Kathy Selden in ''[[Singin' in the Rain]]'' at [[Oslo Nye Teater]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2008-01-21 |title=Velkommen til pressevisning på singin' in the rain |url=https://oslonye.no/velkommen-tilpressevisning-pa-singin-in-the-rain/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181222173441/https://oslonye.no/velkommen-tilpressevisning-pa-singin-in-the-rain/ |archive-date=2018-12-22 |access-date=2008-01-21 |website=Oslo Nye |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==

Ellingsen grew up in Narvik. During her youth she attended [[Narvik kulturskole]], the municipal school of music and performing arts, where she studied dance, singing and violin. She participated in several stage productions during this period.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Teigen |first=Jan Erik |date=2006-06-19 |title=Pangstart for Heidi |url=https://www.fremover.no/kulturliv/pangstart-for-heidi/s/1-55-2155652 |url-status=live |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=Fremover}}</ref>

She later studied musical theatre at [[Bårdar Akademiet]] in Oslo from 2004 to 2006.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Leinslie |first=Elisabeth |date=2026 |title=Heidi Ruud Ellingsen |url=https://sceneweb.no/nb/artist/18332/Heidi_Ruud%20Ellingsen |url-status=live |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=Sceneweb}}</ref>

== Career ==

=== Breakthrough ===

In 2006, Ellingsen made her professional stage debut in ''[[Fiddler on the Roof]]'' at [[Oslo Nye Teater]]. The following year she competed in the televised talent competition ''[[Drømmerollen]]'' on NRK1 and won the title role in ''[[Singin' in the Rain]]''. The production premiered at Oslo Nye Teater in January 2008.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rogne |first=May Synnvøe |date=2007-12-28 |title=Synger i regnet |url=https://www.aftenposten.no/kultur/i/Kp50E/synger-i-regnet |url-status=live |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=Aftenposten}}</ref>

=== Stage career ===
Following her breakthrough, she appeared in several Norwegian musical and theatre productions. She played the title role in ''[[Sol av Isfolket]]'', based on [[Margit Sandemo]]’s ''The Legend of the Ice People'',<ref>{{Cite web |last=Berg |first=Inger-Mari |date=2010-07-16 |title=Sol trollbandt publikum |url=https://www.nrk.no/innlandet/sol-trollbandt-publikum-1.7212015 |url-status=live |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=NRK}}</ref> and later appeared as Cosette in ''[[Les Misérables]]''<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kleve |first=Marie L. |date=2009-01-21 |title=Begynner å grine hver gang jeg ser «Les Miserables» |url=https://www.dagbladet.no/kultur/begynner-a-grine-hver-gang-jeg-ser-les-miserables/65305665 |url-status=live |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=Dagbladet}}</ref> and in ''[[Spring Awakening (musical)|Spring Awakening]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Horne |first=Anders |date=2010-02-01 |title=Får skryt etter premieren |url=https://www.fremover.no/kulturliv/far-skryt-etter-premieren/s/1-55-4837476 |url-status=live |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=Fremover}}</ref>

From 2010 to 2015, she was a member of the ensemble at [[Det Norske Teatret]], where she performed in several productions, including ''The Secret Garden'' (''Den hemmelege hagen''), ''Enron'', ''Tonje Glimmerdal'', and ''Fiddler on the Roof''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Redaksjon |date=2026-03-02 |title=Heidi Ruud Ellingsen |url=https://www.detnorsketeatret.no/skodespelarar/heidi-ruud-ellingsen |url-status=live |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=Det Norske Teateret}}</ref>

She has played leading roles in productions such as:

* ''[[Mary Poppins (musical)|Mary Poppins]]'' at [[Folketeatret]] (2015)<ref>{{Cite web |last=Redaksjon |date=2016-04-12 |title=Vinnere av Musikkteaterprisen 2015 |url=https://scenekunst.no/sak/vinnere-av-musikkteaterprisen-2015/ |url-status=live |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=Scenekunst.no A/S}}</ref>
* ''[[Flashdance]]'' at [[Chateau Neuf]] (2018)<ref>{{Cite web |last=Redaksjon |date=2018-02-01 |title=Musikalen FLASHDANCE |url=https://neuf.no/arrangementer/musikalen-flashdance-18 |url-status=live |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=Chateau Neuf}}</ref>
* ''[[Moulin Rouge!]]'' at Chateau Neuf (2023)<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nystøyl |first=Karen Frøsland |date=2023-08-31 |title=Heftig hitparade |url=https://www.nrk.no/anmeldelser/anmeldelse_-_moulin-rouge_-the-musical_-pa-chateau-neuf-1.16533744 |url-status=live |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=NRK}}</ref>

She has also performed as Solveig in ''[[Peer Gynt]]'' at [[Gålå]] and appeared in several large-scale outdoor historical productions.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Klævahaugen |first=Ingunn |date=2025-06-04 |title=Hele familien står sammen på scenen: – Endrer litt DNA |url=https://www.gd.no/hele-familien-star-sammen-pa-scenen-endrer-litt-dna/s/5-18-2284017 |url-status=live |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=Gudbrandsdølen Dagningen}}</ref>

=== Film and television ===

Ellingsen played Oda in the NRK drama series ''[[Hjem]]'' (2012).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eide |first=Tonje |date=2012-12-21 |title=Hjem fra Vestfossen for siste gang |url=https://www.nrk.no/buskerud/hjem-fra-vestfossen-for-siste-gang-1.10850676 |url-status=live |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=NRK Buskerud}}</ref> She also appeared in the Swedish-American television series ''[[100 Code]]'' (2015).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Steen |first=Thea |date=2014-10-17 |title=I all hemmelighet har hun spilt inn en internasjonal tv-serie |url=https://www.dagbladet.no/kultur/i-all-hemmelighet-har-hun-spilt-inn-en-internasjonal-tv-serie/60976997 |url-status=live |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=Dagbladet}}</ref>

In 2019, she co-hosted [[Melodi Grand Prix 2019]] on NRK1 alongside [[Kåre Magnus Bergh]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sand |first=Camilla |date=2018-12-06 |title=Leder Melodi Grand Prix 2019 |url=https://www.nrk.no/presse/leder-melodi-grand-prix-2019-1.14326497 |url-status=live |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=NRK presse}}</ref>

In 2023, she portrayed [[Svarta Bjorn|Svarta Bjørn]] in the historical drama film ''[[Sulis 1907]]''. The same year, she appeared in the film ''[[Konvoi]]'', for which she was nominated for the [[Amanda Award]] for Best Supporting Actress in 2024.<ref name=":0" />

=== Voice acting ===

Ellingsen has also worked as a voice actor, including roles in the Norwegian-language versions of animated films such as ''[[Ice Age: Continental Drift]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Redaksjon |date=2026-03-02 |title=Norske stemmer i Istid 4: Kontinenter på avveie |url=https://dubbet.no/film/ice-age-continental-drift |url-status=live |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=Dubbet}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Ellingsen's partner is the actor [[Mads Ousdal]]. They have two children, the first born in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mads Ousdal og Heidi Ruud Ellingsen har blitt foreldre |url=https://www.vg.no/rampelys/i/g5xw9/mads-ousdal-og-heidi-ruud-ellingsen-har-blitt-foreldre}}</ref>

== Awards and nominations ==

* 2015 – Musical Theatre Prize (Musikkteaterprisen)
* 2018 – Musical Theatre Prize (Musikkteaterprisen)
* 2008 – Narvik Municipal Culture Prize
* 2024 – Nominated for the [[Amanda Award]] for Best Supporting Actress for ''Konvoi''<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Redaksjon |date=2024-06-01 |title=Her er årets Amanda-nominasjoner |url=https://montages.no/2024/06/her-er-arets-amanda-nominasjoner-dag-johan-haugerud-krig-og-dokumentarer-leder-an/ |url-status=live |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=Montages}}</ref>

A member of the [[Peruvian Aprista Party]] (APRA), he is currently a member of the party's National Political Commission and was the party's presidential nominee for [[2026 Peruvian general election|2026 presidential election]].{{cite news|title=Enrique Valderrama será el candidato presidencial del APRA en las Elecciones 2026|url=https://larepublica.pe/politica/2025/12/01/enrique-valderrama-sera-el-candidato-presidencial-del-apra-en-las-elecciones-2026-69192|access-date=2 January 2026|work=La República|date=2 December 2025|language=es|quote=With 100 percent of the records processed, the list headed by Enrique Valderrama (List 7) defeated the list led by Javier Velásquez Quesquén (List 13) in the party’s internal election. He became a fully registered member in 2010. That same year, he was selected as a candidate for the Lima Metropolitan Council in the 2010 municipal election; however, the party's electoral list, headed by [[Carlos Roca (politician)|Carlos Roca]] as mayoral nominee, was ultimately withdrawn.{{cite news|url=https://www.diariocritico.com/noticia/213481/noticias/carlos-roca-caceres-sera-el-candidato-del-apra-a-la-alcaldia-de-lima.html|title=Carlos Roca Cáceres será el candidato del Apra a la alcaldía de Lima|work=Diariocrítico|date=15 June 2010|access-date=2 January 2026|language=es|quote=The election of Carlos Roca Cáceres cleared up the uncertainty that had been hanging over the Aprista Party headquarters on Alfonso Ugarte Avenue for several days. In the days leading up to the election, former Labor Minister Susana Pinilla and Foncodes Executive Director Carlos Arana had been touted as future candidates, both of whom had the support of President Alan García.}}{{cite news|url=https://rpp.pe/politica/actualidad/partido-aprista-retira-candidatura-de-carlos-roca-a-la-alcaldia-de-lima-noticia-285338|title=Partido Aprista retira candidatura de Carlos Roca a la Alcaldía de Lima|work=RPP Noticias|date=4 August 2010|access-date=2 January 2026|language=es|quote=The Peruvian Aprista Party (PAP) decided to withdraw Carlos Roca's candidacy for metropolitan mayor of Lima. According to a statement from the National Political Commission, the ruling party will not participate in the electoral process for the mayoralty of Lima. The statement also thanked Roca Cáceres and the candidates for councilors for having assumed such party responsibility.}} From 2011 to 2012, Valderrama served as General Secretary of the Aprista University Command at the [[Pontifical Catholic University of Peru]], where he was then studying law.{{cite web|author=|url=https://www.gatoencerrado.net/store/noticias/96/96049/detalle.htm|title=Los Pulpines del APRA|publisher=Gato Encerrado|date=11 January 2016|accessdate=23 January 2023|language=es}} After an extended interruption in his studies, during which he worked in the social housing sector, he completed his law degree in 2022 at the [[University of San Martín de Porres]]. He is currently pursuing a master's degree in financial markets at the [[International University of La Rioja]]. In July 2021, Valderrama was appointed by party leader [[César Trelles]] as a member of the party's National Political Commission.{{cite web|author=|url=https://infogob.jne.gob.pe/Politico/FichaPolitico/pitter-enrique-valderrama-pe%C3%B1a_historial-partidario_aEcgCC5qfUgc6+@0ElOxMA==cC|title=POLÍTICOS - PITTER ENRIQUE VALDERRAMA PEÑA|publisher=Jurado Nacional de Elecciones|date=|accessdate=23 January 2023}} He was subsequently identified by commentators as part of a new generation of party leaders associated with efforts to renew the organization.{{cite news|last=Redacción Canal N|url=https://canaln.pe/actualidad/video-enrique-valderrama-lo-principal-este-momento-construir-unidad-apra-n453764|title=Enrique Valderrama: Lo principal en este momento es construir la unidad del APRA|work=Canal N|date=21 October 2022|access-date=23 January 2023|language=es}}{{cite news|url=https://larepublica.pe/politica/2025/03/30/elecciones-2026-el-apra-busca-resurgir-entre-dudas-viejas-caras-y-nuevos-liderazgos-hnews-2765728|title=Elecciones 2026: el APRA busca resurgir entre dudas, viejas caras y nuevos liderazgos|work=La República|date=31 March 2025|access-date=9 July 2025|first=Mauricio|last=Muñoz|language=es|quote=Enrique Valderrama is one of the youngest figures in the star party. At 36, the activist will be under 40 on election day. Valderrama has been seen participating in political activities in districts such as Comas and San Juan de Lurigancho. '''Nathaniel Schatzline''' (born November 19, 1991)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://thetexan.news/directory/house/nate_schatzline/|title=Rep. Nate Schatzline|access-date=July 18, 2026|website=[[The Texan (website)|The Texan]]}}</ref> is an American politician and pastor serving as the senior advisor to the [[Governor of Texas]] since 2026. A member of the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]], he served in the [[Texas House of Representatives]] from 2023 to 2026.

==Early life and career==
Schatzline's parents, Karen and Patrick Schatzline, co-founded the [[evangelicalism in the United States|evangelist]] organization Remnant Ministries International.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://raisetheremnant.com|title=PAT & KAREN: EVANGELISTS, AUTHORS, AND COACHES|access-date=July 18, 2026|website=Remnant Ministries International}}</ref> He graduated from the [[Southwestern Assemblies of God University]] with a [[Bachelor of Arts]] and from [[Liberty University]] with a [[Master of Arts]] in [[political science]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-announces-senior-staff-leadership-additions|title=Governor Abbott Announces Senior Staff Leadership Additions|date=July 2, 2026|access-date=July 18, 2026|website=[[Governor of Texas]]}}</ref>

Schatzline worked as a pastor at a church in [[Modesto]], [[California]]. He was an [[adjunct professor]] at SEU-NorCal, a satellite campus in Modesto of [[Southeastern University]], lecturing [[microeconomics]] classes in a [[megachurch]] in 2019. He moved to [[Fort Worth]] in June 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.star-telegram.com/opinion/bud-kennedy/article257381622.html|title=Listerine and sanitizer? This whole Fort Worth-area Texas House race needs a scrubbing|first=Bud|last=Kennedy|date=January 21, 2022|access-date=July 18, 2026|website=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]]}}</ref>

He is the director of operations of The Justice Reform, an anti-[[human trafficking]] nonprofit that operates under Mercy Culture Church in Fort Worth.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |last=Brindley |first=Emily |date=November 9, 2022 |title=Live updates: Candidates leading in Fort Worth-area's state House and Senate races |work=Fort Worth Star-Telegram |url=https://www.star-telegram.com/news/politics-government/election/article268092372.html |access-date=2023-03-01}}</ref>

==Political career==
===Texas House of Representatives===
A [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]], Schatzline was elected during the [[2022 Texas House of Representatives election]], defeating Democrat KC Chowdhury in [[Texas's 93rd House of Representatives district|District 93]].<ref name=":1" /> He campaigned on [[Conservative Christianity|Christian conservative]] values, and supported securing the Mexican border, law enforcement, and lowering taxes.<ref name=":1" /> Schatzline supports the Constitutional right to keep and bear arms, and restrictions on [[abortion]], with exceptions when the mother's life is at risk.<ref name=":1" /> He opposes [[critical race theory]].<ref name=":1" /> Schatzline currently served on the corrections and human services committee.

In February 2023, Schatzline authored bill HB 1266 to restrict [[drag performance]]s by amending the Texas business and commerce code.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Abrams |first=Cameron |date=2023-02-06 |title=Rep. Schatzline Introduces Bills to Ban Child Gender Modification, Raise Age of Consent in Texas |url=https://thetexan.news/rep-schatzline-introduces-bills-to-ban-child-gender-modification-raise-age-of-consent-in-texas/ |access-date=2023-03-01 |website=The Texan |language=en-US}}</ref> A month later, ''[[NBC News]]'' reported on a video showing Schatzline had previously dressed in women's clothing and performed for a school theatre project.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/nbc-out/out-politics-and-policy/video-appears-show-texas-drag-bill-author-dressed-drag-rcna72950|title=Video appears to show Texas drag bill author dressed in drag|first=Matt|last=Lavietes|date=March 1, 2023|access-date=July 18, 2026|website=[[NBC News]]}}</ref>

On May 27, 2023, Schatzline voted against the [[Impeachment of Ken Paxton|impeachment]] of [[Texas Attorney General]] [[Ken Paxton]].<ref>Astudillo, Carla and Chris Essig. [https://www.texastribune.org/2023/05/27/ken-paxton-texas-house-impeachment-vote/ Ken Paxton was impeached by the Texas House. See how each representative voted.], ''[[Texas Tribune]]'', May 27, 2023.</ref>

In 2025, Schatzline authored a bill to make bookstores liable for selling books that contain obscene content.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2025 |title=Book bans aren't stopping at libraries—now Texas is targeting bookstores |url=https://www.chron.com/politics/article/texas-bookstores-obscene-books-20290932.php |work=Houston Chronicle}}</ref>

Schatzline announced he would not seek re-election to a third term in 2026, instead joining the National Faith Advisory Board, which works with the  White House under [[Donald Trump]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=O'Bar |first1=Mary Elise |title=Texas Rep. Nate Schatzline to Not Seek Re-election, Joins National Faith Advisory Board |url=https://thetexan.news/elections/2026/texas-rep-nate-schatzline-to-not-seek-re-election-joins-national-faith-advisory-board/article_8458dec8-b7ef-448e-9e1f-989aeab16f25.html |access-date=14 March 2026 |work=The Texan |date=October 27, 2025}}</ref> [[Fort Worth]] city councilman Alan Blaylock won the Republican nomination to succeed Schatzline.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hovland |first1=Addie |title=Republican Nominees Secured for Key Open Seats in Texas Legislature |url=https://texasscorecard.com/state/republican-nominees-secured-for-key-open-seats-in-texas-legislature/ |access-date=14 March 2026 |work=Texas Scorecard |date=March 4, 2026}}</ref> 

He resigned from the chamber in July 2026 after being appointed a senior advisor on election integrity to [[Texas Governor|governor]] [[Greg Abbott]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Guo |first1=Kayla |last2=Serrano |first2=Alejandro |title=Rep. Nate Schatzline resigns from Texas House to lead 'election integrity' policy in Gov. Abbott’s office |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2026/07/02/texas-nate-schatzline-appointed-greg-abbott-governors-office-election-adviser/ |access-date=9 July 2026 |work=[[The Texas Tribune]] |date=July 2, 2026}}</ref> Although reported that Schatzline was a frontrunner to be nominated [[Secretary of State of Texas]], Abbott ultimately appointed his legislative director [[Robert Howden (politician)|Robert Howden]] after incumbent secretary of state [[Jane Nelson]] reportedly pushed against Schatzline's appointment.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.democracydocket.com/news-alerts/texas-appoints-new-secretary-of-state-ahead-of-2026-midterm-elections/|title=Texas appoints new secretary of state ahead of 2026 midterm elections|date=July 17, 2026|access-date=July 18, 2026|website=[[Democracy Docket]]|first=Jen|last=Rice}}</ref>

'''Jamalcolm "Jay" Liggins''' (born 26 April 1996) is an American [[American football|football]] [[defensive back]] for the [[Paris Musketeers]] of the [[European League of Football]] (ELF). He played [[college football]] at [[Dickinson State University|Dickinson State]].

==Youth and college career==
Liggins attended [[Bismarck High School]] in North Dakota's capital city. He had also competed in track and field (long jump and triple jump) in high school and college, earning All-American honors. On the football team, he excelled as a senior and became a first-time starter for the Demons and was subsequently selected to the All-Region Team.<ref name="TDP">{{cite web |author1=Meaghan MacDonald |title=Bismarck’s Sease, Liggins sign with DSU. |url=https://www.thedickinsonpress.com/sports/bismarcks-sease-liggins-sign-with-dsu |website=thedickinsonpress.com |publisher=[[The Dickinson Press]] |access-date=11 March 2023}}</ref> As a result, he participated in the North Dakota Shrine Bowl in April 2014.<ref>{{cite web |title=Prep football N.D. Shrine Bowl. |url=https://www.grandforksherald.com/sports/prep-football-shrine-bowl |website=grandforksherald.com |publisher=[[Grand Forks Herald]] |access-date=11 March 2023}}</ref>

In 2014, Liggins committed to [[Dickinson State University]] in of the [[National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics]] (NAIA).<ref name="TDP"/> He sat out his first year as a redshirt. In the following years, he won the conference four times with the Blue Hawks. In 2019, they advanced to the quarterfinals of the NAIA playoffs but were eliminated. During his collegiate career, Liggings was selected to the All-Conference team multiple times and was also named to the Second Team in 2017 and the All-American First Team in 2018.<ref>{{cite web |title=2017 Associated Press NAIA All-America Team, List. |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/college-football/2017-associated-press-naia-all-america-team-list |website=FOXsports.com |access-date=11 March 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=2018 NAIA Football All-America Teams Unveiled. |url=https://www.naia.org/sports/fball/2018-19/releases/20181212squqd |website=NAIA.org |access-date=11 March 2023}}</ref> In addition, he was a finalist for the prestigious [[Cliff Harris#Cliff Harris Award|Cliff Harris Award]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Jay Liggins Nominated for Cliff Harris Award. |url=https://www.playnorthstar.com/article/4753 |website=playnorthstar.com |access-date=11 March 2023 |archive-date=January 24, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230124133344/https://www.playnorthstar.com/article/4753 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In March 2019, he attended the [[Pro Day]] at [[North Dakota State University]] and was also named to the All-Conference Team that year.

===North America===
On April 28, 2019, Liggins was signed by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] as an undrafted free agent.<ref>{{cite web |title=I'm ready to go - Bismarck grad, DSU football alum inks deal with Eagles |url=https://www.thedickinsonpress.com/sports/im-ready-to-go-bismarck-grad-dsu-football-alum-inks-deal-with-eagles |website=thedickinsonpress.com |publisher=The Dickinson Press |author=Shelby Reardon |access-date=11 March 2023}}</ref> He appeared in two games during the preseason, recording four tackles, one tackle for loss, and one pass breakup. He was released by the Eagles in mid-August.<ref>{{cite web |title=Eagles release CB Jay Liggins; Make Brett Toth signing official |url=https://theeagleswire.usatoday.com/2019/08/16/eagles-release-cb-jay-liggins-make-brett-toth-signing-official/ |website=theeagleswire.usatoday.com |access-date=11 March 2023}}</ref> Liggins was on the spring 2020 squad of the [[St. Louis BattleHawks]] of the [[XFL (2020)|XFL]], but was released before the start of the season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jay Liggins to play in XFL for BattleHawks |url=https://www.kfyrtv.com/content/sports/Jay-Liggins-to-play-in-XFL-for-BattleHawks-567337111.html |website=kfyrtv.com |access-date=11 March 2023}}</ref> On February 20, 2020, Liggins was signed by the [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) and released on July 30, 2021.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Jake Wright |title=Liggins signs with CFL. |url=https://www.thedickinsonpress.com/sports/liggins-signs-with-cfl |website=thedickinsonpress.com |publisher=The Dickinson Press |access-date=11 March 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Blue Bombers Transactions |url=https://www.bluebombers.com/transactions/ |website=bluebombers.com |access-date=11 March 2023}}</ref> He did not appear in any regular season games for the CFL team.

===Europe===
Liggins was signed by the Bern Grizzlies for the 2022 Swiss [[Nationalliga A (American football)]] season and won the Swiss Bowl championship with them.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jay Liggins wird neuer Cornerback der Bern Grizzlies |url=https://www.grizzlies.ch/post/jay-liggins-wird-neuer-cornerback-der-bern-grizzlies |website=grizzlies.ch |access-date=11 March 2023 |language=DE |archive-date=January 24, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230124133335/https://www.grizzlies.ch/post/jay-liggins-wird-neuer-cornerback-der-bern-grizzlies |url-status=dead }}</ref> On 4 August, Liggins was introduced by the [[Raiders Tirol]] of the [[European League of Football]] (ELF) as a new signing midway through the 2022 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Schaffer und Liggins kommen: RAIDERS Tirol verstärken sich mit ehemaligen NFL-Spielern |url=https://www.raiders.at/football/schaffer-und-liggins-kommen-raiders-tirol-verstaerken-sich-mit-ehemaligen-nfl-spielern/ |website=raiders.at |access-date=11 March 2023 |language=DE}}</ref> In the remaining four games of the regular season, he recorded nine tackles, two interceptions, and eight pass break-ups. He reached the semifinals with the Raiders, where they lost to the Hamburg Sea Devils. In November 2022, Frankfurt Galaxy announced the signing of Liggins for the 2023 ELF season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://europeanleague.football/news/frankfurt-galaxy-sign-former-raiders-tirol-defensive-back-jamalcolm-liggins-340|title=Frankfurt Galaxy sign former Raiders Tirol defensive back Jamalcolm Liggins|website=europeanleague.football|first=Tim|last=Hanswillemenke|date=November 23, 2022|access-date=July 15, 2025}}</ref> He was named a 1st team ELF all star for the 2023 season.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Daniel MacKenzie |title=ELF: Frankfurt Galaxy shore up secondary with Tony Anderson & Jamalcolm Liggins |url=https://www.americanfootballinternational.com/elf-frankfurt-galaxy-shore-up-secondary-with-tony-anderson-and-jamalcolm-liggins/ |website=AmericanFootballInternational.com |access-date=11 March 2023}}</ref> He resigned with the team on December 18, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://frankfurt-galaxy.eu/re-signed-jamalcolm-liggins/|title=Re-Signed Jamalcolm Liggins|website=frankfurt-galaxy.eu|date=December 18, 2023|access-date=July 15, 2025}}</ref> On May 12, 2025, Liggins signed with the [[Paris Musketeers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://europeanleague.football/news/paris-musketeers-sign-db-jamalcolm-liggins-3207|title=Paris Musketeers sign DB Jamalcolm Liggins|website=europeanleague.football|first=Felix|last=Pahl|date=May 12, 2025|access-date=July 15, 2025}}</ref>

==Private life==
Liggins has ten siblings. He grew up in Memphis, Tennessee and moved with his mother and siblings to Bismarck, North Dakota at the age of eleven.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Zach Berman |title=The other Eagle from Bismarck: The improbable journey of cornerback Jay Liggins, Carson Wentz’s crosstown rival. |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1111931/2019/08/02/the-other-eagle-from-bismarck-the-improbable-journey-of-cornerback-jay-liggins-carson-wentzs-crosstown-rival/ |website=theathletic.com |publisher=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=11 March 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author1=Dustin Monke |date=March 23, 2019 |title=Opportunity of a lifetime: DSU CB Jay Liggins hoping for shot at the NFL. |url=https://dustinmonke.com/2019/03/23/opportunity-of-a-lifetime-dsu-cb-jay-liggins-hoping-for-nfl-opportunity/ |access-date=11 March 2023 |website=dustinmonke.com}}</ref> Initially, he sought a career in the U.S. military.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Adrian Franke |title=Draft 2019 Sleeper - Keelan Doss, Jamalcolm Liggins und Co. |url=https://www.spox.com/de/sport/ussport/nfl/1904/Artikel/draft-sleeper-kandidaten-doss-jennings-anderson.html |website=spox.com |access-date=11 March 2023 |language=DE}}</ref>

'''Guillaume Cliche-Rivard''' is a Canadian politician, who was elected to the [[National Assembly of Quebec]] in the [[2023 Saint-Henri—Sainte-Anne provincial by-election]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Québec solidaire victorious in byelection, capturing Montreal Liberal stronghold |url=https://globalnews.ca/news/9547238/quebec-byelection-montreal-march-13-2023/ |date=March 13, 2023 |access-date=March 14, 2023 |website=[[Global News]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Political career ==
Cliche-Rivard unsuccessfully contested [[Saint-Henri–Sainte-Anne]] in the [[2022 Quebec general election]]. [[Quebec Liberal Party#Party leaders|Leader]] of the [[Quebec Liberal Party]] [[Dominique Anglade]] resigned following the election, and Cliche-Rivard was elected in the by-election that followed.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Richer |first=Jocelyne |date=November 17, 2022 |title=Élection dans Saint-Henri–Sainte-Anne: Guillaume Cliche-Rivard de nouveau candidat pour QS |language=fr-CA |work=[[La Presse (Canadian newspaper)|La Presse]] |url=https://www.lapresse.ca/actualites/politique/2022-11-17/election-dans-saint-henri-sainte-anne/guillaume-cliche-rivard-de-nouveau-candidat-pour-qs.php |access-date=February 24, 2023}}</ref>

'''Shannon Berry''' ([[Port Hedland, Western Australia]], 27 July 1999) is an Australian television actress. She played Dot Campbell on two seasons of [[Prime Video]] series ''[[The Wilds (TV series)|The Wilds]]''.

==Early life==
Berry was brought up in [[Perth, Western Australia]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.themudmag.com/post/shannon-berry-shines-on-amazon-s-the-wilds|website=themudmag|accessdate=17 May 2023|title= Shannon Berry Shines on Amazon's The Wilds|date=5 January 2022}}</ref> She was born in [[Port Hedland, Western Australia|Port Hedland]], and spent her early childhood in the [[Pilbara]] before moving to [[Dianella, Western Australia|Dianella]] at eight years-old.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Playing a teen mum 'life changing' for Perth starlet|first=Jacqui|last=Bahr|website=The West Australian|date=4 July 2017|url=https://thewest.com.au/entertainment/tv/playing-a-teen-mum-life-changing-for-perth-starlet-ng-b88513878z|accessdate=17 May 2023}}</ref>  She first started acting while in primary school at [[John Septimus Roe Anglican Community School]] and attended [[Mount Lawley Senior High School]] until 2016. Shortly afterwards she moved from Perth to pursue acting jobs in [[Melbourne]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://thewest.com.au/entertainment/celebrity-gossip/perth-teen-quits-school-to-join-offspring-ng-ya-111926|accessdate=17 May 2013|title=Perth teen quits school to join Offspring|first=Sue|last=Yeap|website=The West Australian|date=7 July 2016}}</ref>

==Career==
Berry appeared in Australian comedy-drama ''[[Offspring (TV series)|Offspring]]'', for [[Network Ten]], aged sixteen years-old.<ref>{{Cite web|website=News.com.au|first=Colin|last=Vickery|date=12 July 2016|url=https://www.news.com.au/entertainment/tv/shannon-berry-joins-cast-of-offspring-as-rebellious-teen-brody-jordan/news-story/6cf193d7dbc995397734bdeeb1328871|title= Shannon Berry joins cast of Offspring as rebellious teen Brody Jordan|accessdate=17 May 2023}}</ref> She also appeared in [[Geoffrey Wright]]’s reboot of ''[[Romper Stomper (TV series)|Romper Stomper]]'' into a television series for [[Stan (service)|Stan]]. Berry featured as Emme in [[Gale Anne Hurd]] led [[Syfy]] series ''[[Hunters (2016 TV series)|Hunters]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|website=Screen Rant|accessdate=17 May 2023|first=Brynne|last=Ramella|date=15 December 2020|title= The Wilds Season 1 Cast Guide: Where You Recognize The Actors From|url=https://screenrant.com/wilds-amazon-prime-show-cast-character-guide/}}</ref> In 2018,
Berry appeared in her first feature film, opposite [[Jacqueline McKenzie]], called ''The Gateway''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-reviews/gateway-film-review-1093558|website=The Hollywood Reporter|accessdate=17 May 2023|title= The Gateway': Film Review|first=Harry|last=Windsor|date=12 March 2018}}</ref>

Berry played tough [[Texan]] teenager Dot Campbell in [[Amazon Video]] desert island survivalist drama series ''[[The Wilds (TV series)|The Wilds]],'' which ran for two seasons between 2020 and 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/paultassi/2023/01/28/fans-believe-the-last-of-us-has-found-its-abby-actress-for-season-2|website=Forbes|first=Paul|last=Tassi|date=28 January 2023|accessdate=17 May 2023|title= Fans Believe 'The Last Of Us' Has Found Its Abby Actress For Season 2}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thepinknews.com/2023/03/03/the-last-of-us-season-two-shannon-berry-abby/ |accessdate=17 May 2023|website=Pink News|title= The Last of Us fans are convinced The Wilds' Shannon Berry is playing Abby in season 2|date=3 March 2023|first=Charlie|last= Duncan}}</ref> She was cast alongside [[Emilia Jones]] in the [[Susanna Fogel]] directed film ''[[Winner (2024 film)|Winner]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2023/05/winner-shannon-berry-susanna-fogel-biopic-reality-winner-1235366736/|website=Deadline Hollywood|title= 'Winner': Shannon Berry Joins Susanna Fogel's Biopic About Reality Winner|first= Jesse|last=Whittock|date=16 May 2023}}</ref> Berry has a small role which was written specifically for her in Michael Nikou’s Melbourne-filmed independent movie ''Slant''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://glittermagazine.co/2021/02/24/interview-shannon-berry/|website=Glitter Magazine|accessdate=17 May 2023|title= INTERVIEW: Shannon Berry on the Amazon Original Series 'The Wilds,' Strong Female Characters, Fan Theories, Social Isolation, and Self-Love|first=Nikki|last=Fowler|date=24 February 2021}}</ref>

In 2024, she appeared in the Australian mystery thriller television series ''[[High Country (TV series)|High Country]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://if.com.au/high-country-trailer/|accessdate=20 March 2024|title= High Country' (Trailer)|website=IF.com|date=12 February 2024}}</ref>

Berry starred in the 2025 [[Netflix]] miniseries adaptation of [[Jane Harper]]'s [[Jane Harper#The Survivors|novel]], ''The Survivors''.

'''Zachary Dieken''' is an American politician. He currently represents [[Iowa's 5th House of Representatives district|District 5]] in the [[Iowa House of Representatives]]<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Representative Zach Dieken |url=https://www.legis.iowa.gov/legislators/legislator?ga=90&personID=33965 |access-date=2023-07-24 |website=The Iowa Legislature}}</ref> and serves as an Iowa State Patrol Trooper.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Van Aartsen |first=Scott |date=2023-01-13 |title=New State Representative Zach Dieken Tells About His Priorities for 2023 |url=https://kiwaradio.com/local-news/new-state-representative-zach-dieken-tells-about-his-priorities-for-2023/ |access-date=2023-07-24 |website=[[KIWA (AM)|KIWA Radio]] |language=en-US |archive-date=July 24, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230724192118/https://kiwaradio.com/local-news/new-state-representative-zach-dieken-tells-about-his-priorities-for-2023/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In late 2025, he announced he would not be seeking reelection.

== Biography ==

Dieken was born in 1990 in Minneapolis<ref name=":1" /> and graduated from [[George–Little Rock Senior High School]], where he played baseball.<ref>{{cite news |title=Generals swing for fences |url=https://www.dglobe.com/news/generals-swing-for-fences |access-date=June 21, 2026 |work=The Globe |date=July 4, 2007}}</ref> He received a bachelor's degree in sociology and criminal justice from [[Northwestern College (Iowa)|Northwestern College]] in 2012.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Helton |first=Elijah |date=2021-11-23 |title=Open Iowa House seat has first entrant |url=https://www.nwestiowa.com/news/open-iowa-house-seat-has-first-entrant/article_e9125e2e-4cb0-11ec-8bcf-93f1892cefc6.html |access-date=2023-07-24 |website=The N'West Iowa Review |language=en}}</ref> Prior to being elected to the Iowa House of Representatives, Dieken worked as a state patrol trooper and a substitute teacher.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pedley |first=Nick |date=2021-11-18 |title=Another Republican jumps into HD5 race |url=https://www.hartleysentinel.com/story/2021/11/18/news/another-republican-jumps-into-hd5-race/1644.html |access-date=2023-07-26 |website=The Hartley Sentinel-The Everly/Royal News |language=en}}</ref> As of March 2025, media outlets reported that he still served as a state patrol trooper.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Opsahl |first=Robin |title=Iowa Senate sends bill to governor banning open THC drink containers in vehicles |url=https://iowacapitaldispatch.com/briefs/iowa-senate-sends-bill-banning-open-thc-drink-containers-in-vehicles-to-governor/ |access-date=2025-05-14 |website=Iowa Capital Dispatch |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gruber-Miller |first=Stephen |title='That's not already illegal?' Iowa bill would add THC drinks to state's open container law |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/news/politics/2025/01/23/iowa-legislature-bill-would-add-thc-drinks-to-iowa-open-container-law/77906257007/ |access-date=2025-05-14 |website=[[The Des Moines Register]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

Dieken lives in Granville, Iowa.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Breen |first=Matt |date=2022-05-25 |title=Reynolds endorses GOP challenger over incumbent Republican lawmaker in June primary |url=https://www.ktiv.com/2022/05/25/reynolds-endorses-gop-challenger-over-incumbent-republican-lawmaker-june-primary/ |access-date=2023-07-24 |website=[[KTIV]] |language=en}}</ref> He and his wife Megan<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rust |first=Justin |date=2022-03-25 |title=Dieken gives case for District 5 seat |url=https://www.nwestiowa.com/news/dieken-gives-case-for-district-5-seat/article_4cfd43f0-abb0-11ec-8db0-63bfa2d94930.html |access-date=2023-07-24 |website=The N'West Iowa Review |language=en}}</ref> have three children.<ref name="nwiarev2026plans"/>

== Political career ==
Dieken announced his intention to run in the Republican primary to represent the newly created fifth district of the Iowa House of Representatives on November 15, 2021.<ref name=":0" /> He ran as a strong conservative, emphasizing his support for a private school voucher program which incumbent [[Dennis Bush]] opposed.<ref name=":2" /> Since taking office, he has been described as among the most conservative state legislators in Iowa.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cullen |first=Tom |date=2024-03-01 |title=Dieken says governments should ignore new property tax law |url=https://www.chronicletimes.com/stories/dieken-says-governments-should-ignore-new-property-tax-law,98245 |access-date=2024-10-28 |website=The Cherokee Chronicle Times |language=en}}</ref> Dieken received an endorsement from Governor [[Kim Reynolds]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Howell |first=Michael |date=2022-05-25 |title=Gov. Reynolds endorsing another Republican House member's primary challenger |url=https://cbs2iowa.com/news/local/gov-reynolds-endorsing-another-republican-house-members-primary-challenger |access-date=2023-07-24 |website=[[KGAN]] |language=en}}</ref> and won the June 7, 2022 primary with 55.8% of the vote, beating Bush and Tom Kuiper.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Helton |first=Elijah |date=2022-06-07 |title=Dieken, Evans, Wheeler win primaries |url=https://www.nwestiowa.com/news/dieken-evans-wheeler-win-primaries/article_cc5ee512-e6c6-11ec-a0eb-db00372d3df2.html |access-date=2023-07-24 |website=The N'West Iowa Review |language=en}}</ref>

Dieken ran unopposed in the November 8, 2022 general election<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-11-08 |title=Live Iowa State House Election Results 2022 |url=https://www.iowapublicradio.org/political-news/2022-11-08/iowa-house-election-results-2022-live |access-date=2023-07-24 |website=[[Iowa Public Radio]] |language=en}}</ref> and took office January 9, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gruber-Miller |first=Steven |date=2023-01-09 |title=The Iowa Legislature's 2023 session is back in action under GOP control. What to expect. |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/news/politics/2023/01/09/iowa-legislature-2023-session-how-bill-become-law-contact-legislator/69782910007/ |access-date=2023-07-24 |website=[[The Des Moines Register]] |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2024, he won re-election,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Welte |first=Dean |date=2024-11-05 |title=DECISION 2024: Results for races in Northwest Iowa |url=https://www.ktiv.com/2024/11/05/decision-2024-races-watch-northwest-iowa/ |access-date=2025-01-02 |website=[[KTIV]] |language=}}</ref> beating independent candidate Michael Schnoes with 77.8% of the vote.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rust |first=Justin |date=2024-11-05 |title=N'West Iowa election results |url=https://www.nwestiowa.com/news/nwest-iowa-election-results/article_c3b94250-9bf9-11ef-a814-f7a613bcf3e8.html |access-date=2025-01-02 |website=The N'West Iowa Review |language=en}}</ref>

He serves as vice chair of the Environmental Protection committee and as a member of the Agriculture and Public Safety committees.<ref name=":1" /> Dieken has sponsored bills to increase requirements for CO<sub>2</sub> pipeline expansions,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Helton |first=Elijah |date=2023-03-13 |title=Dieken, Evans talk pipeline legislation |url=https://www.nwestiowa.com/news/dieken-evans-talk-pipeline-legislation/article_c7896416-c183-11ed-b1c4-2b8a25962ac5.html |access-date=2023-07-26 |website=The N'West Iowa Review |language=en}}</ref> to amend the Iowa constitution to forbid same-sex marriage,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-03-01 |title=Republican lawmakers propose amendment that would ban gay marriage in Iowa |url=https://www.kcci.com/article/proposed-amendment-would-ban-gay-marriage-in-iowa/43131852 |access-date=2023-07-26 |website=[[KCCI]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kurtz |first=Jake |date=2023-03-02 |title=Dieken co-sponsors House bill banning same-sex marriage |url=https://www.chronicletimes.com/articles/news/dieken-co-sponsors-house-bill-banning-same-sex-marriage/ |access-date=2023-07-26 |website=Cherokee Chronicle Times}}</ref> and to require pre-birth child support.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mackey |first=Mikaela |date=2024-02-24 |title=Pre-Birth Child Support bill |url=https://www.nwestiowa.com/news/pre-birth-child-support-bill/article_1d96770e-d349-11ee-8acf-5f5e93a2b883.html |access-date=2024-10-28 |website=The N'West Iowa Review |language=en}}</ref>

In 2024, Dieken said that cities and counties should set property taxes in defiance of state law, citing the "doctrine of the lesser magistrates."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mohmand |first=Amber |last2=Cullen |first2=Tom |date=2024-03-01 |title=Rep. Dieken: Ignore new property tax lawHe advises cities, counties to set their own tax rates no matter what state thinks |url=https://www.stormlake.com/stories/rep-dieken-ignore-new-property-tax-lawhe-advises-cities-counties-to-set-their-own-tax-rates-no,57840 |access-date=2024-10-28 |website=Storm Lake Times Pilot |language=en}}</ref> This statement was criticized by local government officials and newspapers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mackey |first=Mikaela |date=2024-03-18 |title=Chuck Virgil stands by Dieken's statement |url=https://www.nwestiowa.com/news/chuck-virgil-stands-by-diekens-statement/article_f7786edc-e55f-11ee-8892-5f33720adb7b.html |access-date=2024-10-28 |website=The N'West Iowa Review |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-03-11 |title=Editorial: Dieken's odd advice |url=https://www.nwestiowa.com/opinion/editorial-dieken-s-odd-advice/article_3ecca0ac-dd93-11ee-a326-bb98eb9a55d3.html |access-date=2024-10-28 |website=The N'West Iowa Review |language=en}}</ref> In January 2025, Dieken introduced a bill to better define [[tailgating]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Henderson |first=Kay |date=2025-01-28 |title=Iowa lawmaker introduces bill about tailgating |url=https://www.radioiowa.com/2025/01/28/iowa-lawmaker-introduces-bill-about-tailgating/ |access-date=2025-05-14 |website=Radio Iowa |language=en-US}}</ref>

In December 2025, Dieken announced that he would not be seeking reelection in 2026.<ref name="nwiarev2026plans">{{cite news |title=Dieken will not seek re-election to Iowa House |url=https://www.nwestiowa.com/nwest_iowa_review/dieken-will-not-seek-re-election-to-iowa-house/article_82294378-ecee-42e4-b2dd-6aa178d0eecd.html |access-date=June 21, 2026 |work=N'West Iowa Review |date=January 3, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Zach Dieken not seeking re-election |url=https://www.chronicletimes.com/stories/zach-dieken-not-seeking-re-election,183650 |access-date=June 21, 2026 |work=Cherokee Chronicle Times |date=January 8, 2026}}</ref>

'''Duan Asemota''' (born 29 August 1996) is a Canadian [[Sprint (running)|sprinter]] specializing in the [[100 metres]]. He represented Canada at the [[2024 Summer Olympics]] in [[Paris]], competing in both the 100 metres and the [[4 × 100 metres relay]]. Asemota is a multiple-time national team member and a former [[NCAA]] All-American.

== Early life and education ==
Asemota was born in [[Montreal]], [[Quebec]], and raised in [[Ajax, Ontario]]. He is of Nigerian descent.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nigerians.ca/profiles/duan-asemota|title=Duan Asemota - Nigerian-Canadian Olympic Sprinter|date=5 January 2025|website=Nigerians.ca}}</ref> He began [[track and field]] at the age of eight but focused on sprinting during high school at [[Notre Dame Catholic Secondary School (Ajax)|Notre Dame Catholic Secondary School]]. Asemota was a multi-sport athlete, also playing [[basketball]] for the Durham City Bulldogs and [[association football|soccer]] for Pickering Soccer Club. In 2014, he broke his high school's senior records in both the 100 metres and 200 metres.

After high school, Asemota attended [[Coffeyville Community College]] in Kansas, earning an [[associate degree]] before transferring to [[Ohio State University]], where he majored in [[communication studies]] and competed in [[NCAA Division I]] [[track and field]].

== Collegiate career ==
At Ohio State, Asemota became a First-Team All-American, contributing to the 4×100 metre relay team's school record and second-place finish at the [[NCAA Division I Men's Outdoor Track and Field Championships|2018 NCAA Championships]]. He also earned silver in the 100 metres at the [[Big Ten Conference|2018 Big Ten Championships]] and helped the relay team win the Big Ten title that year.

== International career ==
Asemota made his international debut at the [[2015 Pan American Junior Athletics Championships]] in Edmonton, Alberta. In 2016, he competed at the [[NACAC Under-23 Championships in Athletics|NACAC U23 Championships]] in [[San Salvador]], running 10.87 seconds in the 100 metres preliminaries and helping Canada's 4×100 metre relay team to a fifth-place finish in 40.55 seconds.

In 2019, Asemota finished fifth in the 100 metres at the [[2019 Summer Universiade]] in [[Naples]].

In 2023, he placed fifth in the 100 metres at the [[Canadian Track and Field Championships]], earning a spot on Canada's 4×100 metre relay team for the [[2023 World Athletics Championships]] in Budapest.

== 2024 Summer Olympics ==
At the [[2024 Summer Olympics]] in [[Paris]], Asemota competed in the men's 100 metres, finishing fifth in his heat with a time of 10.17 seconds, narrowly missing advancement to the semifinals. He also participated in the 4×100 metre relay. Asemota later revealed he had been managing a [[Acetabular labrum tear|torn labrum]] and [[sports hernia]] during the Games.<ref>{{cite web |title=De Grasse through to 100m semifinal on second day of track and field at Paris 2024 |url=https://olympic.ca/2024/08/03/de-grasse-through-to-100m-semifinal-on-second-day-of-track-and-field-at-paris-2024/ |website=Olympic.ca |date=3 August 2024 |access-date=11 April 2025}}</ref>

== 2025 Canadian Indoor Championships ==
In March 2025, Asemota won the men's 60 metres at the [[AC Indoor Open|Canadian Indoor Championships]] in [[Toronto]] with a time of 6.70 seconds. He also anchored his club, Speed with Attitude, to gold in the 4×200 metre relay in 1:30.51, setting a new [[championship record]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Canadian Indoor Championships |url=https://worldathletics.org/competition/calendar-results/results/7220336 |website=World Athletics |access-date=11 April 2025}}</ref>

== Coaching ==
Asemota is coached by [[Charles Allen (hurdler)|Charles Allen]], a former Canadian Olympian and current Hub Coach for Sprints and Hurdles (East) with [[Athletics Canada]].

'''Gabrielle Cavassa''' (born July 5, 1994)<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=September 24, 2024 |title=Gabrielle Cavassa |url=https://www.allaboutjazz.com/musicians/gabrielle-cavassa/ |access-date=June 21, 2025 |website=[[All About Jazz]] |language=en}}</ref> is an American [[jazz]] vocalist.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Handy |first=Bruce |date=October 23, 2023 |title=America Sounds Like Emotional Dissonance |url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2023/10/30/america-sounds-like-emotional-dissonance |access-date=December 12, 2025 |magazine=[[The New Yorker]] |via=www.newyorker.com}}</ref>

==Life and career==
Cavassa was born and raised in [[Escondido, California]], and is of Italian descent. She graduated with a Bachelor of Arts in Music from [[San Francisco State University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gabrielle Cavassa |url=https://www.bluenote.com/artist/gabrielle-cavassa/ |access-date=June 21, 2025 |website=[[Blue Note Records]] |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2012, she was a contestant on the [[American Idol season 11|11th season]] of ''[[American Idol]]'', where she performed in the Hollywood rounds before being eliminated.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gabrielle Cavassa |url=https://www.houseofblues.com/neworleans/EventDetail?tmeventid=0&offerid=106192 |access-date=December 12, 2025 |website=House of Blues New Orleans}}</ref>{{Citation needed|date=December 2025}}

In 2017, Cavassa moved to [[New Orleans]], integrating herself into the city's music scene.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Josephson |date=July 8, 2021 |title=Escondido's Gabrielle Cavassa is Co-winner of Sarah Vaughan International Vocal Competition |url=https://www.times-advocate.com/articles/escondidos-gabrielle-cavassa-is-co-winner-of-sarah-vaughan-international-vocal-competition/ |access-date=June 21, 2025 |website=Escondido Times-Advocate|first=Sanford|language=en-US}}</ref> She soon toured with Adonis Rose and the New Orleans Jazz Orchestra, trumpeter [[Irvin Mayfield]], and collaborated with drummer/singer [[Jamison Ross]], who would co-produce her debut album.<ref name=":1" />

After releasing her self-titled debut album, Cavassa won the Sarah Vaughan International Jazz Vocal Competition at the [[James Moody Jazz Festival]] in 2021.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Spargo |first=Tom |date=November 15, 2023 |title=Joshua Redman and Gabrielle Cavassa Beguile at the Barbican |url=https://www.jazzwise.com/review/article/joshua-redman-and-gabrielle-cavassa-beguile-at-the-barbican |access-date=December 12, 2025 |website=[[Jazzwise]]|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=August 30, 2023 |title=Gabrielle Cavassa – Full Set | The OnBeat Sessions |url=https://www.offbeat.com/news/gabrielle-cavassa-full-set-the-onbeat-sessions/,%20https://www.offbeat.com/news/gabrielle-cavassa-full-set-the-onbeat-sessions/ |access-date=December 12, 2025 |website=[[OffBeat (music magazine)|OffBeat]]|language=en}}</ref> Her first, self-titled album was released and self-published on August 21, 2020. Cavassa cites [[Billie Holiday]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alkyer |first=Frank |date=April 1, 2025 |title=Blindfold Test: Gabrielle Cavassa |url=https://downbeat.com/news/detail/blindfold-test-gabrielle-cavassa |access-date=June 21, 2025 |website=[[DownBeat]] |language=en}}</ref> [[Phyllis Hyman]], [[Ornella Vanoni]], and [[Jeff Buckley]] as musical influences.<ref name=":0" />

Cavassa performed on ''[[Where Are We]]'', a 2023 studio album by jazz saxophonist [[Joshua Redman]] and his first to feature vocals.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Baltin |first=Steve |date=January 20, 2023 |title=Artist to Artist Q&A: Gabrielle Cavassa and Sage Bava Riff on the State of Singing Jazz in 2023 |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/stevebaltin/2023/01/20/artist-to-artist-qa-gabrielle-cavassa-and-sage-bava-riff-on-the-state-of-singing-jazz-in-2023/ |access-date=December 12, 2025 |website=[[Forbes]]|language=en}}</ref> She appeared on Redman's subsequent 2025 album, ''[[Words Fall Short]]'', on the track titled "Era's End".

In August, 2024, Cavassa signed to [[Blue Note Records]], and entered the studio to record her label debut.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 25, 2024 |title=Gabrielle Cavassa Signs With Blue Note Records |url=https://www.bluenote.com/gabrielle-cavassa-signs-with-blue-note/ |access-date=June 21, 2025 |website=[[Blue Note Records]] |language=en-US}}</ref>
