Also known as '''Jayy Von Monroe''',<ref name=Hello>{{cite news |title=Hello, Dahli |url=https://www.lascrucesbulletin.com/stories/hello-dahli,2527 |work=[[Las Cruces Bulletin]] |quote=Dahli has more than 73,800 followers on Instagram (@thedahli) and has a following from an earlier incarnation as Jayy Von Monroe of the band Blood on the Dance Floor. |access-date=2024-01-23 |archive-date=2020-02-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200202005117/http://www.lascrucesbulletin.com/stories/hello-dahli,2527 |url-status=live }}</ref> Dahli also became known for being a member of the band [[Blood on the Dance Floor (band)|Blood on the Dance Floor]]. They left the group in 2016 after allegedly being denied HIV medication from [[Dahvie Vanity]], whom Dahli has described as a sexual predator amid multiple misconduct allegations.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2022-02-08 |title=What Jayy Von Has Been Up To Following Abusive Band |url=https://studybreaks.com/culture/music/jayy-von-monroe/ |access-date=2024-01-23 |website=Study Breaks |language=en-us |archive-date=2023-09-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230925125605/https://studybreaks.com/culture/music/jayy-von-monroe/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Early life and career ==
Jeremy Brian Griffis was born in [[Florida]] in August 1991. They began attending punk rock shows at the age of 15 and began their professional career under the stage name Jayy Von Monroe.

== Music career ==
{{Main|Blood on the Dance Floor (band)}}
In 2009, [[Blood on the Dance Floor (band)|Blood on the Dance Floor]] frontman [[Dahvie Vanity]] asked Monroe (who had been a fan of the band before joining) to join the group as Garett Ecstasy's replacement, following Ecstasy's departure after the first rape allegation against Vanity. Many of the songs originally recorded with Ecstasy intended for the upcoming album ''OMFG'' were re-recorded with new vocals by Monroe. The previous concept of the ''OMFG'' album was scrapped, and rebranded as ''Epic'', set for release in 2010. The band went on tour over spring and summer 2010 to promote the release of ''Epic''. With [[Jeffree Star]] they recorded three songs for that album. The collaborations with Jeffree Star were short-lived because like former member Garrett Ecstasy, Star had also accused Vanity of being a pedophile and a predator, claiming to have witnessed questionable behavior. Star later chose to go back on his accusations due to feeling like the band was being [[victimized]]. He was then featured on their 2014 single "Poison Apple", from the album ''[[Bitchcraft (album)|Bitchcraft]]''.<ref name="fight">{{Cite web |title=Jeffree Star and BOTDF at war |url=http://www.absolutepunk.net/showthread.php?t=1872142 |access-date=July 14, 2012 |publisher=AbsolutePunk.net}}</ref> As with the previous conflict with Garrett, the three singles featuring Star's vocals were re-recorded with vocals by Von Monroe, and the original tracks were not featured on the final album.

In October 2010, the album ''[[Epic (Blood on the Dance Floor album)|Epic]]'' charted No. 5 on the Dance/Electronic [[Billboard charts|''Billboard'' chart]].<ref name="amg2">{{Cite web |title=Blood on the Dance Floor |url=http://www.allmusic.com/artist/blood-on-the-dance-floor-mn0002574844 |publisher=[[Allmusic]]}}</ref> The band headlined the Epic Tour and the Epic Tour Part II in support of the album.<ref>[http://www.topspotusa.com/the-epic-tour.html The Epic Tour!!! – Top Spot USA – September 29th 2010] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222194910/http://www.topspotusa.com/the-epic-tour.html|date=February 22, 2014}}. Top Spot USA (September 29, 2010). Retrieved on October 21, 2015.</ref> Even before the release of ''Epic'', recording began for Blood on the Dance Floor's fourth album, ''[[All the Rage!!]]''. The duo collaborated with several artists for the album, including Lady Nogrady, JJ Demon, and Nick Nasty. The album was preceded by several singles to promote the release, including "Yo Ho", and "P.L.U.R.", and "Bewitched", which became the band's most well-known song. The band later embarked on [[Warped Tour 2011]] in June 2011,<ref name="warped">{{Cite web |title=Vans Warped Tour / Bands / June 16th – August 5th / Tickets On Sale Now / Blood on the Dance Floor |url=http://vanswarpedtour.com/band/blood-on-the-dance-floor |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120805020200/http://vanswarpedtour.com/band/blood-on-the-dance-floor |archive-date=August 5, 2012 |access-date=July 14, 2012 |publisher=Vanswarpedtour.com}}</ref> and released the album while on tour.
[[File:Blood_on_the_dance_floor_2011.png|thumb|Monroe performing with [[Blood on the Dance Floor (band)|Blood on the Dance Floor]] in 2011]]
The music video for their hit single from the album ''Bewitched'' featured Nicole "Lady" Nogrady. She later shared that she felt disrespected by the band throughout the album's production and during the music video shoot. Nogrady revealed that she had to directly confront the band to make sure her name was properly credited for her contributions.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 2012 |title=Lady Nogrady Speaks Out |url=http://www.lemonademagazine.net/july2012 |publisher=Lemonade Magazine}}{{dead link|date=August 2023|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> The song was subsequently performed by other female vocalists in place of Nogrady at live shows, and was re-recorded with vocals by Haley Rose for their 2013 acoustic album ''Blood Unplugged''. The album peaked at No. 13 on the ''Billboard'' Top Electronic Albums chart.<ref name="amg2"/> At the end of 2011, the duo headlined the All the Rage Tour and was planning the 'Tis the Season to be Killing Tour.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 4, 2011 |title=Blood on the Dance Floor:. All The Rage [Tour Dates] |url=http://www.eurotrashmusic.co/2011/uncategorized/blood-on-the-dance-floor-all-the-rage-tour-dates/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222143332/http://www.eurotrashmusic.co/2011/uncategorized/blood-on-the-dance-floor-all-the-rage-tour-dates/ |archive-date=February 22, 2014 |publisher=Eurotrash Music}}</ref>

In celebration of Blood on the Dance Floor's fourth anniversary, a digital compilation album titled ''The Legend of Blood on the Dance Floor'' was set to be released on Halloween.<ref name="studio">[http://criticstudio.com/interviews/blood-on-the-dance-floor/ Exclusive Interview: Blood On The Dance Floor] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130909011142/http://criticstudio.com/interviews/blood-on-the-dance-floor/|date=September 9, 2013}}. Critic Studio (January 26, 2012). Retrieved on October 21, 2015.</ref> The compilation's release date was pushed back, originally planned to be released as a CD, it was released as a SoundCloud playlist instead. The compilation features remastered versions of songs from the band's first four albums.{{citation needed|date=August 2025}}

Blood on the Dance Floor's fifth album, ''[[Evolution (Blood on the Dance Floor album)|Evolution]]'', was released on June 19, 2012,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Evolution – Blood on the Dance Floor |url=http://www.allmusic.com/album/evolution-mw0002337839 |publisher=[[Allmusic]]}}</ref> along with a deluxe edition that featured acoustic versions of two songs. Two music videos and four singles were released from the album. The album featured tracks in collaboration with Haley Rose, Amelia Arsenic, Shawn Brandon, Joel Madden of the band [[Good Charlotte]], Elena Vladimirova, and Deuce.<ref name="atrcollabs">{{Cite web |date=October 16, 2011 |title=Blood on the Dance Floor interview w/ Robert Herrera |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n3qKTfawEF0&sns=fb |access-date=July 14, 2012 |publisher=YouTube}}</ref> As a thank you to their fans they released the three-song free EP ''Clubbed to Death!'' on June 20, 2012, for free through an app on [[Facebook]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blood on the Dance Floor – Double Header Review: Evolution and Clubbed To Death |url=http://www.nataliezworld.com/2012/06/blood-on-dance-floor-double-header.html |publisher=Nataliezworld}}</ref> Their sixth EP, ''[[The Anthem of the Outcast]]'', was released on October 30, 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 2012 |title=Blood on the Dance Floor Announce "Anthem of the Outcast" EP Release Date |url=http://www.alterthepress.com/2012/09/blood-on-dance-floor-announce-new.html |publisher=Alter the Press!}}</ref>

Rumors of a breakup in 2013 were proven to be a hoax with Vanity completely denying that the group was disbanding.<ref name="zackrumor">{{Cite web |date=February 19, 2013 |title=Blood on the Dance Floor Not Breaking Up Despite Rumors |url=http://propertyofzack.com/post/43493023308/blood-on-the-dance-floor-not-breaking-up-despite-rumors |publisher=Zack Zarillo}}</ref><ref name="refuse">{{Cite web |date=February 19, 2013 |title=DAMMIT: Blood On The Dance Floor Deny Break Up Rumors; Release New Single |url=http://www.underthegunreview.net/2013/02/19/dammit-blood-on-the-dancefloor-deny-break-up-rumors-release-new-single/ |publisher=Under the Gun Review}}</ref> ''[[Bad Blood (Blood on the Dance Floor album)|Bad Blood]]'' was slated for release in September 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 2013 |title=Blood on the Dance Floor Confirm New Album |url=http://www.alterthepress.com/2013/02/blood-on-dance-floor-confirm-new-album.html |publisher=Alter the Press!}}</ref> On February 18, 2013, the lead single "I Refuse to Sink! (Fuck the Fame)" was released,<ref name="refuse" /> followed by the second single, "Crucified by Your Lies",<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 13, 2013 |title=Blood on the Dance Floor Release New Song; Liken Themselves To Christ & Address Rape Allegations |url=http://www.underthegunreview.net/2013/03/31/blood-on-the-dance-floor-release-new-song-liken-themselves-to-christ-address-rape-allegations/ |publisher=Under the Gun Review}}</ref> and a third, "Something Grimm", on July 2, 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 2013 |title=Blood on the Dance Floor Release New Song "Something Grimm" |url=http://www.alterthepress.com/2013/07/blood-on-dance-floor-release-new-song.html |publisher=Alter the Press!}}</ref>

Andrew "Drew" Apathy joined in early 2014,<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 2014 |title=Id like to announce that @DrewApath... |url=https://www./bloodonthedancefloor/posts/655259394512376 |publisher=Blood on the Dance Floor}}</ref> and a new album, ''Bitchcraft'', was released in June 2014. Their single "We're Takin over!" featuring [[Deuce (singer)|Deuce]] was released February 7.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 2014 |title=Blood on the Dance Floor |url=https://twitter.com/botdfmusic/status/431684761346506753 |publisher=Blood on the Dance Floor}}</ref> They released the album ''Scissors'' in 2016, the band's final release to feature Monroe due to Monroe leaving the group shortly afterward. In 2021 and 2022, Dahli recorded several solo singles.

== Drag career ==
After leaving Blood on the Dance Floor in 2016, they began performing in [[drag (entertainment)|drag]] as Dahli. Their stage name was given to them by their "drag mother", Lady O, in homage to Spanish surrealist artist [[Salvador Dalí]].<ref name="study">{{cite web|url=https://studybreaks.com/tvfilm/jayy-von-monroe/ |title=AFTER BLOOD ON THE DANCE FLOOR, JAYY VON MONROE FINDS REDEMPTION IN DRAG |last=Ventura |first=Illusion |website=studybreaks.com |publisher=Study Breaks Magazine |access-date=September 2, 2025}}</ref> Dahli’s drag aesthetic is often described as a blend of horror, glamour, and punk, frequently featuring intricate makeup and creative concepts.

Dahli gained significant recognition through multiple appearances on the reality competition series ''[[The Boulet Brothers' Dragula]]''. They first competed in Season 2 (2017), where they finished in 7th place. In 2020, they returned for the special ''[[The Boulet Brothers' Dragula|The Boulet Brothers' Dragula: Resurrection]]'', finishing as a runner-up. This performance led to their casting in Season 4 (2021), where they ultimately won the title of "World’s Next Drag Supermonster". Dahli has since appeared as a guest judge on subsequent seasons, including and Season 5.

== Personal life ==
[[File:Chris_Hansen.jpg|thumb|369x369px|Dahli accused [[Dahvie Vanity]] of abuse in an interview with [[Chris Hansen]], who has done multiple other interviews with those, including Damien Leonhardt (formerly known as [[Jessi Slaughter sexual abuse and cyberbullying case|Jessi Slaughter]]), who claim Vanity abused or raped them. Dahli has been criticised for his participation in the harassment against Leonhardt at the time.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Murdock |first1=Sebastian |last2=Cook |first2=Jesselyn |date=March 10, 2020 |title=Chris Hansen To Investigate Alleged Rapist Dahvie Vanity Following HuffPost Coverage |url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/chris-hansen-investigate-dahvie-vanity-huffpost_n_5e67d430c5b6670e72ffbb58 |website=HuffPost}}</ref>]]
Dahli is based in the [[Phoenix, Arizona]] area.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Young |first=Amy |title=The Boulet Brothers' Dragula: Titans Creeps Into Phoenix for a Night of Thrills |url=https://www.phoenixnewtimes.com/arts/boulet-brothers-dragula-titans-creeps-into-phoenix-for-spooky-drag-thrills-15940836 |access-date=2024-01-23 |website=Phoenix New Times |language=en}}</ref> Dahli is [[Non-binary gender|non-binary]].<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1572585144615333891 |user=TheDahli |title=Like If I can live my life fully as a non binary person, why can't my art be as well? |date=2022-09-21 |access-date=2025-03-04}}</ref> They are [[bisexual]] and were diagnosed with [[HIV/AIDS]] while performing with Blood on the Dance Floor, but has since gotten treatment and medication.<ref name="study"/>

In an interview with television journalist [[Chris Hansen]], Dahli accused their former Blood on the Dance Floor bandmate [[Dahvie Vanity]], who has faced multiple allegations of child sexual abuse (including from Damien Leonhardt; formerly known as [[Jessi Slaughter sexual abuse and cyberbullying case|Jessi Slaughter]]), of abuse as well, stating that Vanity forced them to tour without their [[HIV]] medication which caused them to nearly develop [[AIDS]]. Dahli also described Vanity as a sexual predator.<ref name="Huffpost-B">{{Cite web |last1=Cook |first1=Jesselyn |last2=Murdock |first2=Sebastian |date=April 5, 2019 |title=Dahvie Vanity Raped A Child. Police Gave Him A Warning. Now 21 Women Accuse Him Of Sexual Assault. |url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/dahvie-vanity-botdf-sexual-assault_n_5c82afb8e4b0d9361627ca1f |work=Huffington Post}}</ref> Years earlier, Dahli had directly participated in the 2010 cyberbullying of Leonhardt alongside Vanity, initially by releasing a parody of Leonhardt's video with their father, with Dahli in the role of Leonhardt and Vanity in the role of Leonhardt's father. They also released a song, "You Done Goofed", from the album ''[[Epic (Blood on the Dance Floor album)|Epic]]'' about Leonhardt and Vanity's alleged experiences with them, with mocking lyrics including "We watched as the world watched you cry" and "My name and reputation won't be the target of a slut". Vanity intentionally released the song on Leonhardt's 12th birthday, and it resulted in Leonhardt attempting suicide by overdosing. After public opinion began shifting in Leonhardt's favour after revealing their abuse by Vanity in a 2020 interview with Hansen, Dahli has been criticised for their participation in the harassment against Leonhardt at the time.<ref name="CBS News">{{cite news |last1=Hartstein |first1=Jennifer |date=July 22, 2010 |title=Ranting 11-Year-Old Goes Viral |url=http://www.cbsnews.com/video/watch/?id=6702113n&tag=cbsnewsTwoColUpperPromoArea |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100724121153/http://www.cbsnews.com/video/watch/?id=6702113n&tag=cbsnewsTwoColUpperPromoArea |archive-date=July 24, 2010 |access-date=February 13, 2021 |work=[[The Early Show]] |agency=[[CBS News]]}}</ref>

'''D'Andre Sams''' (born March 21, 1992), known professionally as '''ALLBLACK''', is an American rapper. Known for his straightforward flow and gritty lyrics about [[Procuring (prostitution) | pimping]] and street life, Sams emerged as a prominent figure in the [[West_Coast_hip_hop#Bay_Area_Hip-Hop|Bay Area hip-hop]] scene in the late 2010s.<ref name="ringer">{{cite web |last=Murdock |first=Logan |date=October 28, 2020 |title=The New Hype: AllBlack Is Staying True to His Bay Area Roots |url=https://www.theringer.com/music/2020/10/28/21537676/allblack-no-shame-3-interview |website=The Ringer |access-date=September 2, 2024}}</ref><ref name="pitchfork">{{cite web |last=Smith |first=Nadine |date=May 13, 2021 |title=ALLBLACK: TY4FWM Album Review |url=https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/allblack-ty4fwm/ |website=Pitchfork |access-date=September 2, 2024}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Sams was born and raised in the [[San Antonio, Oakland, California | San Antonio]] neighborhood of [[East Oakland]], near [[International Boulevard (Oakland, California) | International Boulevard]], an area commonly known as the "Murder Dubs" due to the rise of drug-related violence in the 1990s.<ref name="hypebeast">{{cite web |url=https://hypebeast.com/2018/6/allblack-interview-2018-trap-black-video |title=ALLBLACK Is Becoming the Bay's Best Rapper |author=Alexis Barnett |website=HYPEBEAST |date=June 11, 2018 |access-date=2024-09-02}}</ref>
<ref name="ringer"/> Sams attended [[Pinole Valley High School]], where he was a standout football player.<ref name="hypebeast"/> After high school, he spent time in [[Santa Barbara, California|Santa Barbara]] and [[Atlanta, Georgia|Atlanta]] from 2011 to 2015, which later influenced his musical perspective and outlook.<ref name="powiss">{{cite web |last=Buford |first=Jayson |date=September 14, 2021 |title='I Was Raised by the Streets, Raised by My Neighbors:' An Interview With ALLBLACK |url=https://www.passionweiss.com/2021/09/14/allblack-interview-ty4fwm-new-album/ |website=Passion of the Weiss |access-date=September 2, 2024}}</ref><ref name="fader">{{cite web |last=Gebreyesus |first=Ruth |date=April 20, 2018 |title=ALLBLACK is carrying on Oakland's complicated rap legacy |url=https://www.thefader.com/2018/04/20/allblack-outcalls-interview |website=The Fader |access-date=September 2, 2024}}</ref>

== Career ==
=== 2015–2017: Career beginnings ===
Sams' entry into music was unplanned. He initially served as a [[hype man]] for [[Berkeley, California | Berkeley]] rapper [[Kossisko]] at [[Roxy Theatre (West Hollywood)|The Roxy Theatre]] in January 2013.<ref name="hypebeast"/><ref name="fader"/><ref name="ringer"/> Encouraged by his mother to write as a way to deal with anger, Sams began writing raps in his early 20s.<ref name="hypebeast"/> His debut project, ''No Shame'', was released in 2015, followed by ''No Shame 2'' in 2016, hosted by prominent Atlanta DJ [[Trap-a-Holics]], known for distributing mixtapes by [[Gucci Mane]] and [[Lil Boosie]].<ref name="ebx">{{cite web |last=Parham |first=Delency |date=March 2, 2016 |title="Allblack finds his purpose" |url=https://eastbayexpress.com/allblack-finds-his-purpose-2-1/ |website=East Bay Express |access-date=September 2, 2024}}</ref><ref name="xxl">{{cite web |last=Seabrook III |first=Robby |date=December 12, 2018 |title=The Break Presents: AllBlack |url=https://www.xxlmag.com/allblack-interview-the-break/ |website=XXL |access-date=September 2, 2024}}</ref><ref name="ringer"/> The latter marked a turning point in his career, showcasing his unique flow that blended Bay Area influences with a [[Detroit drill|Detroit-style]] cadence.<ref name="ringer"/><ref name="hypebeast"/> In 2017, Sams released the "KimSon" EP, which catapulted him to regional stardom in the Bay Area.<ref name="hypebeast"/><ref name="xxl"/><ref name="fader"/>

=== 2018–present: Rising prominence ===
Sams' 2018 project ''Outcalls'' offered a gritty and humanizing view of [[Procuring (prostitution) | pimping]] and [[prostitution]] in the [[San Francisco Bay Area | Bay Area]]. The project featured guest appearances from notable West Coast artists like [[Nef the Pharaoh]], [[Guapdad 4000]], [[P-Lo]], and [[03 Greedo]], and was produced by Japanese-American producer [[DTB (producer)|David Teel]].<ref name="fader"/> The same year, he collaborated with producer [[Kenny Beats]] on the EP ''2 Minute Drills'', which consisted of eight tracks heavily featuring football analogies.<ref name="pitchfork2">{{cite web |last=Pierre |first=Alphonse |date=November 19, 2018 |title=ALLBLACK / Kenny Beats: 2 Minute Drills EP |url=https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/allblack-kenny-beats-2-minute-drills-ep/ |website=Pitchfork |access-date=September 2, 2024}}</ref>

In October 2020, Sams released the EP ''No Shame 3'', featuring collaborations with [[Too Short]], DaBoii of [[SOB X RBE]].<ref name="ringer"/> He performed on [[Jimmy Kimmel Live!]] alongside [[Offset Jim]], [[Blueface]], and [[G-Eazy]].<ref name="ringer"/>

May 2021 saw the release of ''TY4FWM'' (Thank You for Fucking With Me), Sams' debut album featuring production from [[DJ Fresh]] and collaborations with artists such as [[Vince Staples]], [[Drakeo the Ruler]], and [[E-40]].<ref name="pitchfork"/>

== Musical style and themes ==

Sams' lyrics openly discuss his past involvement in [[Procuring (prostitution) | pimping]], which he started as a teenager. Sams describes his music as his "diary" and often draws from his pimping experiences as material in his lyrics, while expressing conflicted feelings about this period of his life.<ref name="fader"/><ref name="pitchfork2"/>

Sams' music is characterized by vivid storytelling, unique slang, extensive [[American football|football]] metaphors, and aggressive delivery.<ref name="hypebeast"/><ref name="ringer"/> Music critics have compared his writing style to [[2Pac | Tupac Shakur]] and [[DMX]].<ref name="xxl"/><ref name="hypebeast"/> His lyrics often deal with themes of trauma, hustling, fatherhood, and his experiences growing up in Oakland, including references to the city's culture of sideshows, parties, and sex work.<ref name="ringer"/><ref name="fader"/><ref name="powiss"/> Sams cites [[Cash Money Records]] artists like [[Lil Wayne]] and [[Juvenile (rapper) | Juvenile]] as major influences, along with [[E-40]], [[3XKrazy]], and classic [[funk]], [[Soul music|soul]], and [[R&B music|R&B]] music.<ref name="powiss"/><ref name="xxl"/> In his personal philosophy, Sams emphasizes principles such as honesty, loyalty, communication, and respect.<ref name="hypebeast"/>

== Personal life ==

Sams' brother and multiple cousins played in the [[National Football League|NFL]], but Sams himself drifted away from football after the death of several close friends in 2010. Sams' grandfather was a member of the [[Black Panther Party]] in the 1960s.<ref name="ringer"/><ref name="hypebeast"/><ref name="powiss"/> Sams has close ties to [[Golden State Warriors]] players, particularly [[Klay Thompson]], who is a fan of his music.<ref name="ringer"/><ref name="powiss"/>

'''Daniel Pérez Otero''' (born February 28, 1990) is a Spanish professional [[basketball]] player for [[Palencia Baloncesto|Palencia]] of the Spanish [[Primera FEB]]. Standing at 6 ft 2 in (1.88 m), Pérez plays as a [[point guard]].

==Early life and youth career==
Born in [[L'Hospitalet de Llobregat]], [[Catalonia]], Pérez started playing basketball in local club C.C.R. Collblanc-Torrassa. He later joined the youth ranks of [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]] at age 13. He would play with Barcelona's junior teams until 2008.<ref name=feb>{{cite web|first=Pablo|last=Romero|title=Dani Pérez, un lugar entre las estrellas |url=https://www.feb.es/2013/11/3/baloncesto/dani-perez-lugar-entre-las-estrellas/50798.aspx|website=feb.es|date=3 November 2013|accessdate=3 June 2025|lang=es}}</ref><ref name=solobasket>{{cite web|title=Regal Barça y Lleida Básquet acuerdan la cesión del base Dani Pérez para convertirse en la primera piedra del nuevo proyecto
 |url=https://www.solobasket.com/liga-endesa/regal-barca-y-lleida-basquet-acuerdan-la-cesion-del-base-dani-perez-para-convertirse-en-la-primera|website=solobasket.com|date=8 August 2008|accessdate=3 June 2025|lang=es}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Still a [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]] player, Pérez joined [[CB Cornellà]] on loan in his first year as a senior, playing in the [[LEB Plata]]. He would remain on loan with Cornellà the following season, playing in the [[LEB Oro]] after the team achieved promotion in the previous season. Pérez would spend a further season on loan with [[CE Lleida Bàsquet]], playing once again in the LEB Oro.<ref name=solobasket></ref>

After his contract with Barcelona expired in July 2011, Pérez joined [[Menorca Bàsquet]] in the [[LEB Oro]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Dino|last=Gelabert-Petrus|title=Dani Pérez, el primero en llegar |url=https://www.menorca.info/deportes/baloncesto/2011/07/09/1405234/dani-perez-primero-llegar.html|website=menorca.info|date=9 July 2011|accessdate=3 June 2025|lang=es}}</ref>

Pérez signed with [[BC Andorra]] of the [[LEB Oro]] in July 2012.<ref>{{cite web|first=R.|last=Mora|title=Dani Pérez, primer fitxatge
|url=https://elperiodic.ad/esports/dani-perez-primer-fitxatge/|website=elperiodic.ad|date=20 July 2012|accessdate=3 June 2025|lang=ca}}</ref> With Andorra, he would lead the [[2012–13 LEB Oro season|2012–13 LEB Oro]] in [[assist (basketball)|assists]].<ref name=fuenla>{{cite web|title=Dani Pérez, nuevo jugador del Fuenla
|url=https://www.baloncestofuenlabrada.com/DetalleNoticia/Article/1826/Dani-Perez-nuevo-jugador-del-Fuenla|website=baloncestofuenlabrada.com|date=3 August 2013|accessdate=3 June 2025|lang=es}}</ref>

After his good performances in the [[LEB Oro]], Pérez signed with [[Baloncesto Fuenlabrada]] in August 2013, finally making his [[Liga ACB]] debut.<ref name=fuenla></ref>

Pérez would return to the [[LEB Oro]] in August 2015, signing for [[Palencia Baloncesto|Palencia]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Adrián|last=Pulleiro|title=Dani Pérez deja la Liga Endesa y firma por el Quesos Cerrato Palencia
 |url=https://www.solobasket.com/competiciones-feb/dani-perez-deja-la-liga-endesa-y-firma-por-el-quesos-cerrato-palencia|website=solobasket.com|date=3 August 2015|accessdate=3 June 2025|lang=es}}</ref> After winning the [[2015–16 LEB Oro season|2015–16 LEB Oro]] championship and achieving promotion with Palencia, Pérez signed with [[Iberostar Tenerife]] in April 2016 to play the final rounds of the [[2015–16 ACB season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=El Iberostar Tenerife ficha a Dani Pérez |url=https://cbcanarias.net/2016/04/14/el-iberostar-tenerife-ficha-a-dani-perez/|website=cbcanarias.net|date=14 April 2016|accessdate=3 June 2025|lang=es}}</ref>

Pérez returned to the [[LEB Oro]] once again, signing with [[Oviedo CB]] in July 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dani Pérez, nuevo timón para el Unión Financiera Oviedo |url=https://www.feb.es/2016/7/11/baloncesto/dani-perez-nuevo-timon-para-union-financiera-oviedo/65437.aspx|website=feb.es|date=11 July 2016|accessdate=3 June 2025|lang=es}}</ref>

In August 2017, Pérez signed with [[Gipuzkoa Basket]] of the [[Liga ACB]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Dani Pérez, primera novedad del Gipuzkoa Basket |url=https://www.acb.com/articulo/ver/133729|website=acb.com|date=3 August 2017|accessdate=3 June 2025|lang=es}}</ref> Pérez player for the Basque team for two seasons, leading the team in [[assist (basketball)|assists]] in both.<ref>{{cite web|title=Acunsa GBC Estadísticas 2017-18|url=https://www.acb.com/club/estadisticas/id/7/temporada_id/2017|website=acb.com|accessdate=3 June 2025|lang=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Acunsa GBC Estadísticas 2018-19|url=https://www.acb.com/club/estadisticas/id/7/temporada_id/2018|website=acb.com|accessdate=3 June 2025|lang=es}}</ref>

===Bàsquet Manresa (2019–2026)===
Pérez signed a three-year contract with [[Bàsquet Manresa]] of the [[Liga ACB]] in June 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dani Pérez, primer reforç per al BAXI Manresa 2019-2020|url=https://www.basquetmanresa.com/noticies/equips/noticies/2019/dani-perez-primer-reforc-al-baxi-manresa-2019-2020/|website=basquetmanresa.com|date=14 June 2019|accessdate=3 June 2025|lang=ca}}</ref> He would set a club record in his first season with the Catalans, recording 16 [[assist (basketball)|assists]] in a home win against [[UCAM Murcia CB|UCAM Murcia]] in November 2019. It was also the 4th highest record in [[Liga ACB]] history.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dentro de un TOP 5 histórico en la era ACB. El partidazo de Dani Pérez con Manresa…|url=https://www.gigantes.com/liga-endesa/dani-perez-manresa/|website=gigantes.com|date=1 December 2019|accessdate=3 June 2025|lang=es}}</ref> He would extend his contract with Manresa for three more years in March 2021.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dani Pérez amplia el seu contracte amb el BAXI Manresa fins el 2024
|url=https://www.basquetmanresa.com/noticies/equips/noticies/2021/dani-perez-amplia-el-seu-contracte-amb-el-baxi-manresa-fins-el-2024/|website=basquetmanresa.com|date=22 March 2021|accessdate=3 June 2025|lang=ca}}</ref> Shortly after, Pérez suffered a [[posterior cruciate ligament injury]] that would sideline him for three months.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dani Pérez estarà 3 mesos de baixa per una lesió al genoll
|url=https://www.basquetmanresa.com/noticies/baxi-manresa/noticias/2021/dani-perez-estara-3-mesos-de-baixa-una-lesio-al-genoll/|website=basquetmanresa.com|date=23 March 2021|accessdate=3 June 2025|lang=ca}}</ref>

Continuing to be an important player for Manresa and becoming the club's all-time leader in [[assist (basketball)|assists]], Pérez signed a 2-year contract extension in April 2024.<ref>{{cite web|title=El BAXI Manresa renova Dani Pérez fins el 2026
|url=https://www.basquetmanresa.com/noticies/teams/news/2024/el-baxi-manresa-renova-dani-perez-fins-el-2026/|website=basquetmanresa.com|date=8 April 2024|accessdate=3 June 2025|lang=ca}}</ref>

In May 2026, Pérez announced he would be leaving Manresa at the end of the [[2025–26 ACB season|2025–26 season]], after having played 275 games for the Catalans. He played his last game on May 29, 2026, in which he received a farewell tribute at the [[Nou Congost]]. It was announced Manresa would retire his number, 55, upon his retirement.<ref>{{cite news|first=Marc |last=Llohis |title=El Nou Congost acomiada "la gran passada" que ha estat Dani Pérez|url=https://www.regio7.cat/basquet-manresa/2026/05/29/nou-congost-acomiada-gran-passada-130820629.html|website=regio7.cat|date=29 May 2026|accessdate=11 June 2026|lang=ca}}</ref>

In July 2026, Pérez returned to [[Palencia Baloncesto|Palencia]] to play in the [[Primera FEB]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Dani Pérez regresa al Súper Agropal Palencia para las dos próximas temporadas|url=https://www.feb.es/2026/7/3/baloncesto/dani-perez-regresa-super-agropal-palencia-para-las-dos-proximas-temporadas/105371.aspx|website=feb.es|date=3 July 2026|accessdate=24 July 2026|lang=es}}</ref>

==National team career==
Pérez has represented [[Spanish Basketball Federation|Spain]]'s youth ranks in several international tournaments, such as the [[2010 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]] with the [[Spain men's national under-20 basketball team|U20 Team]].<ref name=feb></ref>

He made his debut for the senior [[Spain men's national basketball team|Spanish national team]] in 2021, during the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Con Yankuba, Pradilla y Dani Pérez, los debutantes desde 2017 son ya 36
|url=https://www.feb.es/2021/12/1/baloncesto/con-yankuba-pradilla-dani-perez-los-debutantes-desde-2017-son/88718.aspx|website=feb.es|date=1 December 2021|accessdate=3 June 2025|lang=es}}</ref>

Pérez has also represented the [[Catalonia national basketball team|Catalan national team]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Marc|last=Llohis|title=Dani Pérez, base del Baxi i de la selecció catalana de basquetbol: «És destacable que Argentina ens consideri un contrincant de nivell»
|url=https://www.regio7.cat/esports/2023/07/25/dani-perez-base-baxi-seleccio-90285295.html|website=regio7.cat|date=25 July 2023|accessdate=3 June 2025|lang=ca}}</ref>

{{nihongo|'''Kanta Masegi'''|柵木 幹太|Masegi Kanta|February 18, 1998}} is a Japanese [[professional shogi player]] ranked 5-[[Dan (rank)#Modern usage in shogi|dan]].

==Early life and amateur shogi==
Masegi was born in [[Nishio]], [[Aichi Prefecture]] on February 18, 1998.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.shogi.or.jp/player/kanta_masegi|script-title=ja:棋士データベース: 柵木幹太|title=Kishi Dētabēsu: Masegi Kanta|language=ja|trans-title=Professional Shogi Player Database: Kanta Masegi|website=[[Japan Shogi Association]]|access-date=August 25, 2026}}</ref> He learned how to play shogi from his father.<ref name="New4d">{{cite web|url=https://www.shogi.or.jp/news/2023/03/post_2265.html|url-status=dead|script-title=ja:新四段誕生のお知らせ|title=Shinyondan Tanjō no Oshirase|language=ja|trans-title=Announcing the new 4-dans|date=March 11, 2023|website=Japan Shogi Association|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230311141440/https://www.shogi.or.jp/news/2023/03/post_2265.html|archive-date=March 11, 2023|access-date=August 25, 2026}}</ref>

professional [[Yūji Masuda]].<ref name="New4d" /> He was promoted to the rank of apprentice professional 3-dan in April 2016 and qualified to play in the JSA's [[Professional shogi ==Shogi professional==
Masegi was one of the five most recently promoted regular professionals selected to be the for [[Professional shogi player#Women's professionals|women's professional shogi player]] [[Tomoka Nishiyama]] during her best-of-five [[Tomoka Nishiyama#Professional Admission Test|Professional Admission Test]].<ref name="JSA PAT">{{cite web|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line-->|url=https://www.shogi.or.jp/news/2024/08/post_2455.html|url-status=dead|script-title=ja:西山朋佳女流三冠, 棋士編入試験受験へ|title=Nishiyama Tomoka Joryū Sankan, Kishi Hennyūshiken Juken e|language=ja|trans-title=Women's professional 3-crown Tomoka Nihiyama to take Professional Admission Test|date=August 9, 2024|website=Japan Shogi Association|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240901044415/https://www.shogi.or.jp/news/2024/08/post_2455.html|archivedate=September 1, 2024|access-date=August 25, 2026}}</ref> Masegi was Nishiyama's opponent in Game 5 of the test played on January 22, 2025, at the JSA's [[Japan Shogi Association#Headquarters and other offices|Kansai Branch office]]. A win by Nishiyama would mean that she would become the first woman to be awarded regular professional status by the JSA, but Masegi won the game in 135 moves.<ref name= "SH">{{cite news|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line-->|url=https://hochi.news/articles/20250122-OHT1T51245.html?page=1|script-title=ja:西山朋佳女流三冠の悲願阻んだ柵木幹太四段 ｢負けてもおかしくないと思った局面も｣|title=Nishiyama Tomoka Joryū Sankan no Higan Habanda Masegi Kanta Yondan ｢Maketemo Okashikunai to Omotta Kyokumen mo｣|language=ja|trans-title=Kanta Masegi 4-dan who ended women's professional 3-crown Tomoka Nishiyama chance at obtaining regular professional status says "there were some positions where I thought I had a good chance to lose".|date=January 22, 2025|newspaper=[[Sports Hochi]]|access-date=August 25, 2026}}</ref> Masegi and Nishiyama faced each five times in apprentice professional 3-dan League play, with Masegi winning each game;<ref name= "SH" /> however, Masegi reviewed the game scores from those games as part of his preparation and found that he had gotten a bit lucky and could have easily lost each game.<ref name= "SH" /> He was impressed by how strong Nishiyama was in fighting back from disadvantageous positions.<ref name= "SH" /> At the post-game press conference, Masegi stated he felt some pressure and was nervous before the game started but settled down once the game began.<ref name= "SH" /> He also stated that moving first allowed him to steer the game into a long drawn out positional battle as he had planned, allowing to him to obtain an advantageous position in the early part of the game; however, he then made some bad moves and ended up in an endgame where both sides had chances to win.<ref name= "SH" /> Masegi told the ''[[Asahi Shimbun]]'' in January 2026 (almost a year after the game) that defeating Nishiyama in such an important game completely changed things for him as a shogi professional, and he began to play much better and achieve better results.<ref name="AS-1">{{cite news|last=Kitano|first=Arata|url=https://www.asahi.com/articles/ASV1L0VPKV1LUCVL008M.html?msockid=389e7311970d6e27315464a596466f59|url-access=subscription|script-title=ja:あの名局の記憶と名古屋大合格への勉強法 急伸の棋士 ‣ 柵木幹太四段|title=Ano Meikyoku no Kioku to Nagoya Dai Gōkau e no Benkyōhō Kyūshin no Kishi ‣ Masegi Kanta Yondan|language=ja|trans-title=Rising star Kanta Masegi: Memories of that one important game and the study habits used to get into Nagoya University|date=January 18, 2026|newspaper=[[Asahi Shimbun]]|access-date=August 25, 2026}}</ref>{{efn|Masegi had a winning percentage or around 0.500 prior to the Nishiyama game, but he had improved it to 0.735 by the time of the January 2026 ''Asahi Shimbun'' article.<ref name = "AS-1" /> By the end of July 2026, his winning percentage had improved to 0.769 (50 wins and 15 losses) since beating Nishiyama.<ref name = "AS-2" />}} 

Masegi was promoted to [[Meijin (shogi)#Qualifying|Class C2 of the Meijin Ranking League]] from the Free Class for the 85th Meijin League (April 2026{{sndash}}March 2027) in April 2025 after defeating [[Yoshikazu Minami (shogi)|Yoshikazu Minami]] in a [[Ryūō#Tournament structure|38th Ryūō Tournament Class 6 game]]. The win allowed Masegi to meet the criteria for promotion from the Free Class by posting a winning percentage of 0.650 or greater over a span of 30 games. Masegi's win over Minami was his twentieth win over a span of 30 games and gave him a winning percentage of 0.667.<ref>{{cite web|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line-->|url=https://www.shogi.or.jp/news/2025/04/post_2528.html|url-status=dead|script-title=ja:柵木幹太四段, フリークラスからC2組へ昇級|title=Masegi Kanta Yondan, Furīkurasu kara Shīnikumi e Shōkyū|language=ja|trans-title=Kanta Masegi 4-dan promoted to Class C2 from Free Class|date=April 28, 2025|website=Japan Shogi Association|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250501033902/https://www.shogi.or.jp/news/2025/04/post_2528.html|archive-date=May 1, 2025|access-date=August 25, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no-byline-->|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/general/nikkan/news/202504250001712.html|script-title=ja:柵木幹太四段 ｢ホッとしている｣ 引退の師匠の言葉を胸に順位戦C級2組へ昇級を決める|title=Masegi Kanta Yondan ｢Hottoshiteiru｣ Intai no Shishō no Kotoba wo Mune ni Jun'isen Shīkyū Nikumi e Shōkyū wo Kimeru|language=ja|trans-title=Kanta Masegi says he is relieved after being promoted to Class C2, remembering what his recently retired teacher [Yūji Masuda] once told him about becoming a professional shogi player.|date=April 25, 2025|newspaper=[[Nikkan Sports]]|access-date=August 25, 2026}}</ref><ref name="SN">{{cite news|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line-->|url=https://www.sponichi.co.jp/entertainment/news/2025/04/25/articles/20250425s000413F2358000c.html|script-title=ja:柵木四段 プロ2年でフリークラス卒業 名古屋大から初の順位戦へ 直近30局の勝率65％を満たす|title=Masegi Yondan Puro Ninen de Furīkurasu Sotsugyō Nagoya Dai kara Hatsu no Jun'isen e Chokkin Sanjūkyoku no Shōritsu Rokūjugo Pasento wo Mitasu|language=ja|trans-title= Second-year-pro Masegi 4-dan graduates from the Free Class, the Nagoya University graduate will enter Meijin Ranking League play for the first time due to achieving a winning precentage of 65% over a span of 30 games|date=April 25, 2025|newspaper=Sports Nippon|access-date=August 25, 2026}}</ref>

In October 2025, Masegi advanced to the finals of the 15th {{ill|Kakogawa Seiryū Tournament|ja|加古川青流戦}} against [[Ryūma Yoshiike]] but lost the best-of-three championship match 2 games to 1.<ref>{{cite news|last=Kobayashi|first=Shinya|url=https://www.kobe-np.co.jp/news/culture/202510/0019585295.shtml|script-title=ja:加古川青流戦, 20歳の吉池隆真四段が初優勝 柵木幹太四段を破り2年前の雪辱果たす|title=Kakogawa Seiryusen, Hatachi no Yoshiike Ryūma Yondan  ga Hatsuyūshō Masegi Kanta Yondan wo Yaburi Ninenmae no Setsujoku Hatasu|language=ja|trans-title=Kakogowa Seiryū Tournament:20-year-old Ryūma Yoshiike 4-dan defeats Kanta Masegi 4-dan to win his first tournament as a professional and ease the sting of losing in the finals of the same tournament two years ago.|date=October 13, 2025|newspaper=[[Kobe Shimbun]]|access-date=August 25, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Satō|first=Keiji|url=https://www.asahi.com/articles/ASTBM3F83TBMUCVL015M.html|url-access=subscription|script-title=ja:2年前2連敗の雪辱 将棋加古川青流戦, 20歳の吉池隆真四段が優勝|title=Ninenmae Nirenpai no Setsujoku Shōgi Kakogawa Seiryūsen, Hatachi no Yoshiike Ryūma Yondan ga Yūshō|language=ja|trans-title= Twenty-year-old Ryūma Yoshiike 4-dan wins Kakogawa Seiryū Tournament to "avenge" losing in the same finals two years earlier without winning even a single game.|date=October 10, 2025|newspaper=[[Asahi Shimbun]]|access-date=August 25, 2026}}</ref>

'''''Eduardo Rodrigo Fernandes Ribeiro''''', born {{Date|October 11, 1988}} in [[Capinzal]], is a [[biochemist]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Eduardo Rodrigo Fernandes Ribeiro |url=https://www.escavador.com/sobre/3829332/eduardo-rodrigo-fernandes-ribeiro |access-date=2026-06-23 |website=Escavador |language=pt-br}}</ref> businessman and a [[Brazil]]ian  [[politician]]. He is the current national president of the [[New Party (Brazil)|Partido Novo]] (NOVO).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Partido Novo |url=https://www.tre-ro.jus.br/partidos/partidos-politicos/partido-novo |access-date=2026-06-23 |website=Justiça Eleitoral |language=pt-br}}</ref>

==Political career==
Affiliated with the Partido Novo since its registration in 2015, Eduardo Ribeiro participated in building the party in the state of [[Santa Catarina (state)|Santa Catarina]], being elected its first president of the State Directorate in 2017. Under his leadership, the party participated in the 2018 elections, winning a seat in the Chamber of Deputies held by [[Gilson Marques]].

In 2019, he was elected national secretary of the Partido Novo, a position he held until March 2020, when he assumed the party presidency following the resignation of then president [[João Amoêdo]].

In April 2023, the party's National Convention reappointed Eduardo Ribeiro as president of [[New Party (Brazil)|NOVO]] for four additional years, with a term until 2027.<ref>{{Cite web |title=João Amoêdo deixa a presidência do Novo; Eduardo Ribeiro assume |url=https://www.estadao.com.br/politica/joao-amoedo-deixa-a-presidencia-do-novo-e-eduardo-ribeiro-assume/ |access-date=2026-06-23 |website=Estadão |language=pt-br}}</ref>

'''Conner Mooneyham''' (born 28 March 1996) is an American [[rugby union]] player who played for the [[Anthem Rugby Carolina|Anthem Carolina]] in [[Major League Rugby]] (MLR). His preferred position is [[Wing (rugby union)|wing]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ultimaterugby.com/conner-mooneyham|title=Conner Mooneyham|work=Ultimate Rugby|access-date=8 December 2025}}</ref>

==Early career==
Mooneyham is from [[Rocklin, California]] but grew up in [[Magnolia, Texas]] before attending [[Life University]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://goldcountrymedia.com/news/272699/conner-mooneyham-took-his-rugby-skills-from-the-sierra-foothills-rugby-club-to-the-international-level/|title=Conner Mooneyham took his rugby skills from the Sierra Foothills Rugby Club to the international level|work=Gold Country Media|date=29 March 2023|access-date=8 December 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.rugbypass.com/news/when-they-told-me-that-i-was-going-to-be-the-number-one-pick-i-didnt-expect-things-to-blow-up-as-much-as-they-did/|title='When they told me that I was going to be the number one pick, I didn't expect things to blow up as much as they did'|work=Rugby Pass|date=19 June 2020|access-date=8 December 2025}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Mooneyham was the first selection in the [[2020 MLR Draft]] for the [[Dallas Jackals]], however joined the [[Austin Gilgronis]] ahead of the [[2021 Major League Rugby season]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://goffrugbyreport.com/news/top-draft-pick-finds-new-home-austin|title=Top draft pick finds new home in Austin|work=Goff Rugby Report|date=2 December 2021|access-date=8 December 2025}}</ref> He remained with the team until it was disbanded at the end of the 2022 season, where he was picked up by [[Rugby ATL]] in the dispersal draft,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.americasrugbynews.com/2022/11/11/mlr-expansion-dispersal-draft-summary/|title=MLR expansion / dispersal draft summary|work=Americas Rugby News|date=11 November 2022|access-date=8 December 2025}}</ref> however chose to sign with the {{Rut|Seattle Seawolves}} instead.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.americasrugbynews.com/2022/11/29/seattle-acquires-rights-to-conner-mooneyham-from-atl/|title=Seattle Seawolves acquires rights to Conner Mooneyham from ATL|work=Americas Rugby News|date=29 November 2022|access-date=8 December 2025}}</ref> He would compete for Seattle in the 2023 and 2024 seasons, before being traded to [[Anthem Rugby Carolina|Anthem Carolina]] ahead of the 2025 season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.seawolves.rugby/news/seawolves-trade-conner-mooneyham-anthem-carolina|title=Seattle Seawolves trade Conner Mooneyham to Anthem Rugby Carolina|work=Seattle Seawolves|date=14 August 2024|access-date=8 December 2025}}</ref>

Mooneyham made his debut for the [[United States men's national rugby union team|United States]] national team in July 2024, debuting against Scotland.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://scottishrugby.org/news-and-features/match-report-usa-7-42-scotland/|title=Match Report: USA 7 – 42 Scotland|work=Scottish Rugby|date=13 July 2024|access-date=8 December 2025}}</ref> He scored his first tries against Canada in September.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://eagles.rugby/news/usa-defeat-canada-2815-on-home-soil-to-book-pacific-nations-cup-semifinal-spot-202491|title=USA defeat Canada 28-15 on home soil to book Pacific Nations Cup semifinal spot|work=USA Rugby|date=1 September 2024|access-date=8 December 2025}}</ref>

'''Jerrie Johnson''' is an American actress. She is best known for playing Tye Reynolds in the sitcom ''[[Harlem (TV series)|Harlem]]'' and Daphne in the comedy drama series ''[[Survival of the Thickest]]''.

==Early life==
Johnson is from [[Philadelphia]], Pennsylvania. Johnson graduated from [[Pennsylvania State University]] in 2016 with a bachelor of arts in theatre and a minor in African American studies. She earned a master of fine arts at the [[American Conservatory Theater]] in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Theatre alum Jerrie Johnson to talk career, new series on Nov. 29|url=https://www.psu.edu/news/arts-and-entertainment/story/theatre-alum-jerrie-johnson-talk-career-new-series-nov-29|access-date=January 13, 2026 |website=psu.edu}}</ref>

==Career==
Johnson made her acting debut on the drama series ''[[Good Trouble (TV series)|Good Trouble]]'' where she portrayed Tye.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tracy Oliver Amazon Series Casts Meagan Good, Grace Byers, Jerrie Johnson and Shoniqua Shandai|url=https://variety.com/2020/tv/news/tracy-oliver-amazon-series-cast-meagan-good-grace-byers-jerrie-johnson-and-shoniqua-shandai-1203466923/|access-date=January 13, 2026 |website=variety.com}}</ref> Her first big role came playing Tye Reynolds in the sitcom ''[[Harlem (TV series)|Harlem]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Harlem Season 3: Meagan Good & Jerrie Johnson Say Goodbye|url=https://www.thathashtagshow.com/interviews/harlem-season-3-meagan-good-jerrie-johnson-say-goodbye/|website=thehashtagshow.com|access-date=January 13, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=JERRIE JOHNSON ON ‘HARLEM,’ HUSTLE, AND HOLDING SPACE FOR BLACK QUEER STORIES|url=https://www.abookof.us/openbook/jerrie-johnson|website=abookof.us|access-date=January 13, 2026}}</ref> She had a recurring role as Daphne on the comedy drama series ''[[Survival of the Thickest]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Meet the 'Survival of the Thickest' Season 2 Cast|url=https://www.marieclaire.com/culture/tv-shows/survival-of-the-thickest-cast/|access-date=January 13, 2026|website=marieclaire.com}}</ref> On June 30th 2025 she took part in Soul Soirée’s Monologue Slam in [[Brooklyn]] alongside [[Dominique Thorne]] and [[Daniel J. Watts]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dominique Thorne, Jerrie Johnson, Daniel J. Watts, and Adrianna Mitchell Set to Take the Stage at Soul Soirée’s Summer Monologue Slam|url=https://blexmedia.com/soul-soirees-summer-monologue-slam/|access-date=January 13, 2026 |website=blexmedia.com}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Johnson is a lesbian and is married to art doula Dria Brown. They met at a post-show panel for the play Confederates by [[Dominique Morisseau]]. They started dating in 2022 before Johnson proposed to her in [[Montego Bay]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jerrie Johnson And Dria Brown: The Creative Power Couple Who Are Better Together|url=https://gomag.com/article/jerrie-johnson-and-dria-brown-the-creative-power-couple-who-are-better-together/|access-date=January 13, 2026 |website=gomag.com}}</ref>

'''Ryōsuke Takashima{{efn|{{langx|ja|高島 崚輔、たかしま　りょうすけ}},
officially {{lang|ja|髙島 崚輔}}|name=renamed_from_1_on_20260124174822|group=lower-alpha}}''' (born 4 February 1997)<ref>{{Cite web |title=髙島崚輔市長のページ |url=https://www.city.ashiya.lg.jp/hisho/shisei/shichou/index_2019.html |access-date=2023-05-04 |website=芦屋市 |language=ja}}</ref> is a Japanese politician who has served as mayor of [[Ashiya, Hyōgo|Ashiya, Hyogo Prefecture]] since April 2023.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=日本放送協会 |title=歴代最年少26歳で芦屋市長に 高島崚輔さんって？灘高からハーバード {{!}} NHK |url=https://www3.nhk.or.jp/news/html/20230424/k10014047281000.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230424042951/https://www3.nhk.or.jp/news/html/20230424/k10014047281000.html |archive-date=2023-04-24 |access-date=2023-04-27 |website=NHKニュース}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=史上最年少26歳・高島崚輔芦屋市長が初登庁「世界で一番住み続けたい芦屋を」朝食はいつも通り - 社会 : 日刊スポーツ |url=https://www.nikkansports.com/general/nikkan/news/202305010000250.html |access-date=2023-05-01 |website=nikkansports.com |language=ja}}</ref> He is known as the youngest elected mayor in Japan, being 26 years old at the time of the election on 23 April 2023.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=学生時代は「ノートの神様」…灘中・灘高・東大・ハーバード大学そして“史上最年少”市長へ 芦屋市長選”当選”の26歳・高島崚輔さん「世界でいちばん住み続けたい街にする」とカメラ目線でトーク {{!}} 特集 {{!}} ニュース {{!}} 関西テレビ放送 カンテレ |url=https://www.ktv.jp/news/feature/230424-ashiyatakashima/ |access-date=2025-10-09 |website=ニュース |language=ja}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Ryōsuke Takashima was born in [[Minoh]], [[Osaka Prefecture]].<ref name="yomiuri20220424">{{Cite news |date=2023-04-24 |title=史上最年少の芦屋市長、灘高・ハーバード卒でTikTokも駆使…草の根選挙展開 |url=https://www.yomiuri.co.jp/election/local/20230424-OYT1T50156/ |access-date=2023-04-24 |work=[[読売新聞]]}}</ref> He studied in [[Nada High School|Nada Junior and High School]], serving there as the student council leader. Takashima passed both exams for [[University of Tokyo]] and [[Harvard University]],<ref>{{Cite news |date=2016-03-06 |title=ハーバードにペーパーテストはない　求められるのは「人とつながる力」 |url=https://globe.asahi.com/article/11563048 |access-date=2023-04-24 |work=朝日新聞グローブ}}</ref> but because he already completed the enrollment procedure at Tokyo, he spent 4 months studying in Tokyo before dropping out for Harvard.<ref>{{Cite web |title=髙島崚輔市長のページ |url=https://www.city.ashiya.lg.jp/hisho/shisei/shichou/index_2019.html |access-date=2023-05-04 |website=芦屋市 |language=ja|date=2023-05-04}}</ref> There he first studied [[public policy]], but then switched to studying [[Environmental engineering|environmental]] [[energy engineering]]. In his first year, he visited the [[Tokyo Electric Power Company]]’s [[Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant]] together with colleagues from the [[Harvard Kennedy School|Kennedy School]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=学生時代は「ノートの神様」…灘中・灘高・東大・ハーバード大学そして“史上最年少”市長へ 芦屋市長選”当選”の26歳・高島崚輔さん「世界でいちばん住み続けたい街にする」とカメラ目線でトーク {{!}} 特集 {{!}} ニュース {{!}} 関西テレビ放送 カンテレ |url=https://www.ktv.jp/news/feature/230424-ashiyatakashima/ |access-date=2025-10-09 |website=ニュース |language=ja}}</ref><ref name="NewsPicks">{{Cite news |date=2023-04-23 |title=全国最年少の市長誕生へ／高島りょうすけ、ハーバード大を7年で卒業した日本人 |url=https://newspicks.com/topics/nogami/posts/118 |access-date=2023-04-24 |work=NewsPicks}}</ref> Later in 2016 he became a chairman of the board of the non-profit organisation ''Global Learning Community Study Abroad Fellowship'', officially dropping out of the Tokyo University in 2019.<ref> {{Facebook|takashimaryosuke2023|高島りょうすけ}}</ref> While receiving a scholarship from the Masayoshi Son Foundation and taking three [[Gap year|gap years]], he graduated from the [[Harvard John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences]] on 26 May 2022 with a Bachelor of Arts and Sciences degree.{{R|NewsPicks}}<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-05-13 |title=進学は「海外超難関大」という選択 経験者語る「海外進学塾」からハーバードへ |url=https://www.dailyshincho.jp/article/2018/05130802/?all=1&page=2 |access-date=2023-05-12 |publisher=[[週刊新潮]]}}</ref> In the summer of the same year he moved to Ashiya.<ref name="kobenp20230424">{{Cite news |date=2023-04-23 |title=全国の最年少市長記録を更新　26歳2カ月で芦屋市長選の高島氏　灘高、東大、ハーバードに「期待」 |url=https://www.kobe-np.co.jp/news/sougou/202304/0016276362.shtml |access-date=2023-04-24 |work=[[神戸新聞]]}}</ref>

===Elections===
On 14 April 2023 Takashima ran as an independent candidate in the Ashiya mayor elections, receiving 19,779 votes (46,66% of the total exit polls). Before Takashima's election, the youngest elected politician in Japan was {{Interlanguage link|Kesuke Ishida|ja|石田健佑}} at 27 years old.{{R|kobenp20230424}}<ref>{{Cite web |title=髙島崚輔市長のページ |url=https://www.city.ashiya.lg.jp/hisho/shisei/shichou/index_2019.html |access-date=2023-05-04 |website=芦屋市 |language=ja}}</ref> In 2025, Takashima was selected for ''Time'' magazine’s "100 Next" list as "unconventional in Japan’s gerontocratic politics".<ref>{{Cite web |title=学生時代は「ノートの神様」…灘中・灘高・東大・ハーバード大学そして“史上最年少”市長へ 芦屋市長選”当選”の26歳・高島崚輔さん「世界でいちばん住み続けたい街にする」とカメラ目線でトーク {{!}} 特集 {{!}} ニュース {{!}} 関西テレビ放送 カンテレ |url=https://www.ktv.jp/news/feature/230424-ashiyatakashima/ |access-date=2025-10-09 |website=ニュース |language=ja}}</ref>

== Mayor of Ashiya ==
On 1 December 2023, the Ashiya City Council rejected Takashima’s proposal to appoint former superintendent of education of [[Saitama (city)|Saitama City]] Mayumi Hosoda as the successor to Toshiko Uetsuki on the board of education at a plenary session. The proposal failed to gain a majority vote, which was the first time that a personnel-related bill had been rejected in Ashiya since 1999. The Ashiya Board of Education consists of four members, who are appointed by the mayor with the consent of the council. As the previous superintendent of education, Uetsuki’s term was to end in December, Takashima recommended Hosoda as her successor. Hosoda had served as superintendent of education in Saitama City for five years from June 2018 and has also been a lecturer at the [[Graduate School of Public Policy, University of Tokyo|University of Tokyo Graduate School of Public Policy]], with which Ashiya City concluded a partnership agreement in September of that year. In the plenary session, seven councillors from the [[Liberal Democratic Party (Japan)|LDP]] and [[Komeito]] parties voted in favour of the proposal, while ten councillors from the [[Japanese Communist Party]], [[Japan Innovation Party|Nippon Ishin no Kai]], Ashiya Citizens’ Future Party and independents voted against it; three members of the [[Sanseitō|Sanseito]] abstained. In opposing speeches, four councillors cited reasons such as concerns that living far away would make it difficult to attend twice-monthly committee meetings and local events, and doubts over whether Ashiya’s education would be prioritised given its many other roles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=髙島崚輔市長のページ |url=https://www.city.ashiya.lg.jp/hisho/shisei/shichou/index_2019.html |access-date=2023-05-04 |website=芦屋市 |language=ja}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=学生時代は「ノートの神様」…灘中・灘高・東大・ハーバード大学そして“史上最年少”市長へ 芦屋市長選”当選”の26歳・高島崚輔さん「世界でいちばん住み続けたい街にする」とカメラ目線でトーク {{!}} 特集 {{!}} ニュース {{!}} 関西テレビ放送 カンテレ |url=https://www.ktv.jp/news/feature/230424-ashiyatakashima/ |access-date=2025-10-09 |website=ニュース |language=ja}}</ref>

{{nihongo|'''Shingo Suzuki'''|鈴木 槙吾|Suzuki Shingo|born April 30, 1986}}<ref name=Pancrase>{{cite web |url=https://pancrase.co.jp/data/prfl2/suzukis.html |title=Shingo Suzuki |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240523164331/https://www.pancrase.co.jp/data/prfl2/suzukis.html |archive-date=May 23, 2024 |work=[[Pancrase]] |language=ja}}</ref><ref name=Sherdog>{{cite web |url=https://www.sherdog.com/fighter/Shingo-Suzuki-36613 |title=Shingo Suzuki |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250419044511/https://www.sherdog.com/fighter/Shingo-Suzuki-36613 |archive-date=April 19, 2025 | work=[[Sherdog]]}}</ref> is a Japanese [[Mixed martial arts|mixed martial artist]] and [[Professional wrestling|professional wrestler]]. He is signed to [[Pro Wrestling Zero1]], where he performs as the second incarnation of {{nihongo|'''Hayabusa'''|ハヤブサ||"Falcon"}}, a character formerly portrayed by [[Eiji Ezaki]] in [[Frontier Martial-Arts Wrestling]] (FMW) between 1994 and 2001. He also appears on the Japanese independent scene both as Hayabusa and under the [[mononymous]] [[ring name]] '''Shingo'''. As a martial artist, he previously competed for [[Pancrase]], [[Shooto]] and most recently for [[Deep (mixed martial arts)|Deep]]. He is a former [[List of Pancrase champions#Welterweight Championship|Welterweight King of Pancrase]] as well as a former [[List of Deep champions#Welterweight Championship|Deep Welterweight Champion]].

He made his professional wrestling debut in 2014 with a single appearance at a Hard Hit-branded [[DDT Pro-Wrestling]] event. He made his second debut in 2019 for [[Pro Wrestling Zero1]], where he went by the [[ring name]] '''Raicho''' (stylized in [[all caps]] as '''RAICHO''').

===Shooto (2017–2018)===
Upon joining [[Shooto]] in March 2017, Suzuki dropped to the [[Lightweight (MMA)|lightweight class]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 26, 2017 |title=[Shūto] Pankurasu kara Suzuki Shingo, ZST kara Katō Atsushi ga sansen |script-title=ja:【修斗】パンクラスから鈴木槙吾、ZSTから加藤惇が参戦 |trans-title=[Shooto] Shingo Suzuki from Pancrase and Atsushi Kato from ZST will compete |url=https://efight.jp/news-20170326_257639 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170703221832/http://efight.jp/news-20170326_257639 |archive-date=July 3, 2017 |website=eFight |language=ja}}</ref> On May 12, in his first Shooto fight, he faced Yuki Tencho Kawana and was knocked out in the first round.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 12, 2017 |title=[Shūto] "Doesu Kakutōka" Takahashi ga hissatsu fukurahagi rō de KO kachi |script-title=ja:【修斗】“ドS格闘家”高橋が必殺ふくらはぎローでKO勝ち |trans-title=[Shooto] "Sadistic Fighter" Takahashi Wins by KO with His Signature Low Kick to the Calf |url=http://efight.jp/result-20170512_260341/2 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170517130755/http://efight.jp/result-20170512_260341/2 |archive-date=May 17, 2017 |website=eFight |language=ja}}</ref> Suzuki then faced Yuki Okano on October 15. The fight ended in a 1–1 [[split draw]] decision.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 15, 2017 |title=[Shooto] Zen kyokumen de makkō shōbu no Okano Yūki vs Suzuki Shingo wa sanshasanyō no dorō |script-title=ja:【Shooto】全局面で真っ向勝負の岡野裕城vs鈴木槙吾は三者三様のドロー |trans-title=[Shooto] Yuki Okano vs. Shingo Suzuki: A head-to-head battle across all fronts ends in a split draw |url=https://mmaplanet.jp/72448 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211020031931/https://mmaplanet.jp/72448 |archive-date=October 20, 2021 |website=mmaplanet.jp |language=ja}}</ref> However, a post-fight investigation revealed judge Kyosuke Watanabe had mistakenly reversed the scores for Suzuki and Okano on his scorecard. Consequently, the decision was overturned to a 0–2 loss for Suzuki, and Watanabe was reprimanded for his mistake.<ref>{{Cite web |title=10-gatsu 15-nichi puro shūto Maihama taikai Dai go shiai Okano tai Suzuki no shiai kekka henkō ni tsuite |script-title=ja:10月15日 プロ修斗舞浜大会 第5試合 岡野対鈴木の試合結果変更について |trans-title=October 15th Pro Shooto Maihama Tournament Match 5: Okano vs. Suzuki Regarding the Change in Match Result |url=https://j-shooto.com/2017/10/20/post-0/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220701023031/https://j-shooto.com/2017/10/20/post-0/ |archive-date=July 1, 2022 |website=Japan Shooto Association |language=ja}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 26, 2017 |title=[Shooto] Maihama taikai, Okano × Suzuki no shiai kekka henkō nitaishi, Kōsaka Tsuyoshi-shi ga seimeibun "saihatsu no bōshi o" |script-title=ja:【Shooto】舞浜大会、岡野×鈴木の試合結果変更に対し、高阪剛氏が声明文「再発の防止を」 |trans-title=[Shooto] Regarding the change in the Okano vs. Suzuki match result at the Maihama event, Tsuyoshi Kosaka issues a statement: "Prevent recurrence" |url=https://mmaplanet.jp/72820 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241205090320/https://mmaplanet.jp/72820 |archive-date=December 5, 2024 |website=mmaplanet.jp |language=ja}}</ref>

On March 25, 2018, Suzuki faced former [[judo]] medalist Shutaro "Captain Africa" Debana and lost by submission in the first round.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 25, 2018 |title=[Shūto] Matsumoto Kōshi ga asshō bōei, Okano Yūki o 1R KO de kudasu |script-title=ja:【修斗】松本光史が圧勝防衛、岡野裕城を1RKOで下す |trans-title=[Shooto] Koshi Matsumoto Retains Title in Dominant Fashion, Defeats Yuki Okano via 1st-Round KO |url=https://efight.jp/result-20180325_282388/3 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220314140952/https://efight.jp/result-20180325_282388/3 |archive-date=March 14, 2022 |website=eFight |language=ja}}</ref> Following the match, he left the Alliance dojo and accepted [[Takuya Sugi]]'s invitation to transition from mixed martial arts to professional wrestling.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kameike |first=Shojiro |date=September 14, 2023 |title=[DEEP 115] Black Combat to no taikōsen, Suzuki Shingo 01 "sore ga kakutōgi deari, sore ga shōbu da" |script-title=ja:【DEEP115】Black Combatとの対抗戦へ、鈴木槙吾―01―「それが格闘技であり、それが勝負だ」 |trans-title=[Deep 115] Shingo Suzuki vs. Black Combat —01— "That is combat, and that is the contest" |url=https://mmaplanet.jp/152371 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250808010200/https://mmaplanet.jp/152371 |archive-date=August 8, 2025 |website=mmaplanet.jp |language=ja}}</ref>

===Deep (2022–2024)===
On August 21, 2022, at Deep 109 Impact, Suzuki faced Ryuichiro Sumimura in the welterweight division and won by technical knockout in the first round, marking his successful return to MMA after a four-year hiatus.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 21, 2022 |title=[DEEP] Moto Pankurasu ōja, Suzuki Shingo ga TKO shōri, 4-nen buri MMA-sen de moto ōja, Sumimura ni shōri |script-title=ja:【DEEP】元パンクラス王者・鈴木槙吾がTKO勝利、４年ぶりMMA戦で元王者・住村に勝利 |trans-title=[Deep] Former Pancrase champion Shingo Suzuki wins by TKO, defeating former champion Sumimura in his first MMA fight in four years |url=https://efight.jp/result_s-20220821_1291460 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230722041247/https://efight.jp/result_s-20220821_1291460 |archive-date=July 22, 2023 |website=eFight |language=ja}}</ref>

Suzuki fought [[Daichi Abe]] at Deep 112 Impact on February 11, 2023, and won the [[List of Deep champions#Welterweight Championship|Deep Welterweight Championship]] by submission in the second round.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 11, 2023 |title=[DEEP] Furai-kyū T junkesshō wa Honda Ryōsuke ga Itō Yūki ni shōri, Fukuda Ryūya to kesshō de taiketsu! Kanda Kōya ga Gomyō Hiroto o kudashite shin ōja ni |script-title=ja:【DEEP】フライ級T準決勝は本田良介が伊藤裕樹に勝利、福田龍彌と決勝で対決！神田コウヤが五明宏人を下して新王者に |trans-title=[Deep] Flyweight Tournament Semifinal: Ryosuke Honda defeats Yuki Ito, advancing to face Ryuya Fukuda in the final! Kouya Kanda defeats Hiroto Gomyo to become the new champion! |url=https://efight.jp/result-20230211_1347853/2 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260214102444/https://efight.jp/result-20230211_1347853/2 |archive-date=February 14, 2026 |website=eFight |language=ja}}</ref> He lost the title to Yoichiro Sato at Deep 120 Impact on July 14, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 14, 2024 |title=[DEEP] Satō Yōichirō, gōkai kauntā de Suzuki Shingo o KO shi werutā-kyū shin ōja ni! |script-title=ja:【DEEP】佐藤洋一郎、豪快カウンターで鈴木槙吾をKOしウェルター級新王者に！ |trans-title=[Deep] Yoichiro Sato Knocks Out Shingo Suzuki with a Powerful Counterpunch to Become the New Welterweight Champion! |url=https://efight.jp/result_s-20240714_1514376 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240714183954/https://efight.jp/result_s-20240714_1514376 |archive-date=July 14, 2024 |website=eFight |language=ja}}</ref>

Suzuki's final bout to date was at Deep Tokyo Impact 2024 6th Round on December 8, where he lost by submission to Ibuki Shimada.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 8, 2024 |title=DEEP TOKYO IMPACT 2024 6th ROUND |url=https://www.deep2001.com/deep-tokyo-impact-2024-6th-round/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251107090450/https://www.deep2001.com/deep-tokyo-impact-2024-6th-round/ |archive-date=November 7, 2025 |website=[[Deep (mixed martial arts)|Deep]] |language=ja}}</ref>

==Professional wrestling career==
===Early career (2014)===
Suzuki made his first professional wrestling appearance at Hard Hit: G-generation on August 23, 2014. This event was produced by [[DDT Pro-Wrestling]]'s MMA-oriented brand, Hard Hit, which was managed at the time by [[Hikaru Sato]] and heavily inspired by [[UWF International|UWF]] rules. At the event, Suzuki defeated [[Michael Nakazawa]] by submission.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 23, 2014 |title=Haado Hitto: G-generation |script-title=ja:ハードヒット〜G-generation〜 |trans-title=Hard Hit: G-generation |url=http://www.ddtpro.com/hardhit/13607/ |url-status=deviated |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150609063033/http://www.ddtpro.com/hardhit/13607/ |archive-date=June 9, 2015 |website=[[DDT Pro-Wrestling]] |language=ja}}</ref>

=== Japanese independent circuit (2021–present) ===
In early 2021, Sugi and Yuji Hino formed the stable Only We. They aimed to produce an independent charity event at the [[Active Advance Pro Wrestling]]'s 2AW Square dojo in [[Chiba (city)|Chiba]] on January 30. They were quickly joined by Suzuki, who changed his ring name to '''Shingo''', and [[Quiet Storm (wrestler)|Quiet Storm]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 16, 2021 |title=Hino Yuji & Sugi gōdō charitī jishū kōgyō |script-title=ja:火野裕士＆SUGI合同チャリティー自主興行 |trans-title=Yuji Hino & SUGI Joint Charity Independent Event |url=https://peraichi.com/landing_pages/view/hinosugi/ |url-status=deviated |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210125153049/https://peraichi.com/landing_pages/view/hinosugi/ |archive-date=January 25, 2021 |website=HINO-YUJI and SUGI |language=ja}}</ref> Titled Voyage vol.{{nbsp}}1, the event was pushed back twice: first to March 6 and then to May 23. In the main event, Only We (Hino, Sugi, Shingo and Quiet Storm) were defeated by Shogun Okamoto, [[Hoshitango Imachi|Hoshitango]], [[Akira Raijin]] and [[Masato Shibata]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 23, 2021 |title=VOYAGE vol.1 |url=https://wp.bbm-mobile.com/sp2/result/resultshow.asp?s=050980 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://megalodon.jp/2026-0222-2210-27/https://wp.bbm-mobile.com:443/sp2/result/resultshow.asp?s=050980 |archive-date=February 22, 2026 |website=Weekly Pro-Wrestling |publisher=Baseball Magazine Sha |language=ja}}</ref> Suzuki made his debut in [[Kazuhiro Tamura]]'s Pro-Wrestling Heat-Up promotion on July 10, 2021, where he faced [[Tetsuya Izuchi]] in a grappling [[sparring match]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 10, 2021 |title=Shichigatsu tōka (do) Fukkatsu! === All Japan Pro Wrestling (2021–2022) ===
On December 26, 2021, Suzuki reprised his role as Raicho and competed alongside Sugi in the [[Junior Tag Battle of Glory#2021|Jr. Tag Battle of Glory]] tournament, hosted by [[All Japan Pro Wrestling]] (AJPW). ==Professional wrestling persona==
While Zero1 is keeping the new Hayabusa's identity a secret, many believe that Suzuki is portraying him based on his physique and his schedule.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kreikenbohm |first=Philip |title=Hayabusa, Shingo |url=https://www.cagematch.net/?id=2&nr=24185 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260221224244/https://www.cagematch.net/?id=2&nr=24185 |archive-date=February 21, 2026 |website=Cagematch}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Hayabusa no shōtai o yosō shiyō! |script-title=ja:ハヤブサの正体を予想しよう！ |trans-title=Guess the identity of Hayabusa! |url=https://medaka.5ch.net/test/read.cgi/wres/1742805175/l50 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://megalodon.jp/2026-0222-2227-48/https://medaka.5ch.net:443/test/read.cgi/wres/1742805175/l50 |archive-date=February 22, 2026 |website=[[5ch]] |language=ja}}</ref>

Unlike promotions such as NJPW, which formally acknowledge successive incarnations of masked characters – for example recognizing [[Yoshihiro Yamazaki]] as the fourth generation [[Tiger Mask (professional wrestling)|Tiger Mask]] and styling him as {{nihongo|Fourth Generation Golden Tiger|黄金の虎4代目|Ōgon no Tora Yon-daime}}<ref>{{Cite web |title=Taigā Masuku |script-title=ja:タイガーマスク |trans-title=Tiger Mask |url=https://www.njpw.co.jp/profile/691 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://megalodon.jp/2026-0222-2228-14/https://www.njpw.co.jp:443/profile/691 |archive-date=February 22, 2026 |website=[[New Japan Pro-Wrestling]] |language=ja}}</ref> – and similar lineage-based gimmicks such as [[Ebessan]] in [[Osaka Pro Wrestling]], Pro Wrestling Zero1 has presented the 2025 return of Hayabusa as the revival of the same character rather than as a new generational successor. Although Suzuki is not the original wrestler, Eiji Ezaki, Zero1 has not designated the character with a numerical suffix (such as "Hayabusa II") nor officially framed it as a second-generation version. Nevertheless, some external websites and databases have referred to the revived character as Hayabusa II.<ref name=Himatsuri25andHayabusaII /> This designation is unofficial and potentially inaccurate, as the Hayabusa persona had previously been portrayed by other wrestlers, most notably [[Mr. Gannosuke]] during the period in which Ezaki performed under the H persona, and on a couple occasions by [[Genichiro Tenryu]]. As a result, while the current portrayal represents the first revival of the character since Ezaki's death, it is not necessarily the second chronological incarnation of the Hayabusa persona.

'''Juan Ignacio Saborido''' (born 25 April 1998) is an Argentine professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|centre-back]] for [[Club Atlético Platense|Platense]].

==Career==

===Villa San Carlos===
Saborido came through the youth program at [[Estudiantes de La Plata]]<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Juan Saborido y Nahuel Luna se acercan a San Carlos |url=https://www.eldia.com/nota/2019-7-4-19-37-0-juan-saborido-y-nahuel-luna-se-acercan-a-san-carlos-deportes |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=Diario El Dia de La Plata |language=es}}</ref> before joining [[Club Atlético Villa San Carlos|Villa San Carlos]], where he made his debut on 6 October 2019 in a 1–0 loss to [[Talleres de Remedios de Escalada|Talleres RdE]] in the [[Primera B Metropolitana]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-10-08 |title=El villero no pudo con Talleres – Club Atlético Villa San Carlos |url=https://villasancarlos.club/vsc/2019/10/el-villero-no-pudo-con-talleres/ |access-date=2026-03-02 |language=es-AR}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club in a 2–1 win against [[Club Atlético Colegiales (Argentina)|Colegiales]] on 22 February 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-02-23 |title=Volvió a enderezar el camino – Club Atlético Villa San Carlos |url=https://villasancarlos.club/vsc/2020/02/volvio-a-enderezar-el-camino/ |access-date=2026-03-02 |language=es-AR}}</ref>

====Loan to General Caballero JLM====
On December 17 2022, he was loaned to [[APF División de Honor|Paraguayan Primera División]] side [[Club General Caballero (Juan León Mallorquín)|General Caballero JLM]] for the 2023 season, after his contract at Villa San Carlos was extended until the end of 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Juan Ignacio Saborido, el sexto fichaje de General Caballero JLM - Fútbol - ABC Color |url=https://www.abc.com.py/deportes/futbol/2022/12/17/juan-ignacio-saborido-el-sexto-fichaje-de-general-caballero-jlm/ |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=www.abc.com.py |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Juan Ignacio Saborido renovó contrato con la Villa y se fue a Paraguay |url=https://www.berissociudad.com.ar/Juan-Ignacio-Saborido-renovo-contrato-con-la-Villa-y-se-fue-a-Paraguay-392479 |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=Berisso Ciudad |language=es-ES}}</ref> He featured 38 times for General Caballero in the league, scoring against [[Club Guaraní|Guaraní]] and [[Sportivo Ameliano]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2024-01-09 |title=Juan Ignacio Saborido se convirtió en jugador Calamar |url=https://cap.org.ar/2024/01/juan-ignacio-saborido-se-convirtio-en-jugador-calamar/ |access-date=2026-03-02 |language=es}}</ref>

===Platense===
On 9 January 2024, he signed permanently for [[AFA Liga Profesional de Fútbol|Liga Profesional]] club [[Club Atlético Platense|Platense]] until December 2026.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-01-11 |title=Saborido llega a Platense - TyC Sports |url=https://www.tycsports.com/liga-profesional-de-futbol/platense-copa-de-la-liga-refuerzos-id557602.html |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=www.tycsports.com |language=es-AR}}</ref> After initially receiving a lack of minutes, he established himself in the first team and started every game in the [[2025 AFA Liga Profesional de Fútbol|2025]] Apertura playoffs, where Platense won the title. He signed a new contract after the tournament on 23 September, signing until the end of 2027.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-09-23 |title=Juan Ignacio Saborido extendió su vínculo con el club |url=https://cap.org.ar/2025/09/juan-ignacio-saborido-extendio-su-vinculo-con-el-club/ |access-date=2026-03-02 |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-02 |title=Surgió de Estudiantes, pasó por la Villa y se consagró con Platense: "Es fruto de trabajo y perseverancia, hay que disfrutar" |url=https://www.laplata1.com/2025-06-02/surgio-de-estudiantes-paso-por-la-villa-y-se-consagro-con-platense-es-fruto-de-trabajo-y-perseverancia-hay-que-disfrutar-115305/ |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=www.laplata1.com |language=es}}</ref>
