'''Rodrigo Sebastián Castillo''' (born 26 February 1999) is an Argentine [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A]] side [[Fluminense FC|Fluminense]].

==Club career==
===Early career===
Born in [[Venado Tuerto]], [[Santa Fe Province|Santa Fe]], Castillo began his career with hometown side {{ill|Club Sportivo Bernardino Rivadavia|lt=Sportivo Rivadavia|es}} before joining the youth sides of [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]]. After playing for the reserve team in 2019, he moved to [[Unión de Santa Fe]] in the following year, also for the reserve squad.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tycsports.com/copa-sudamericana/river-plate-lanus-gimnasia-rodrigo-castillo-id695211.html|title=Quedó libre de River, se reinventó en Gimnasia y es la carta de Lanús en la Sudamericana: la historia de Rodrigo Castillo|trans-title=River let him leave on a free, he reinvented himself at Gimnasia and is Lanús' wildcard in the Sudamericana: the story of Rodrigo Castillo|publisher=[[TyC Sports]]|language=es|date=30 October 2025|accessdate=16 March 2026}}</ref>

On 18 February 2021, Castillo moved to [[Club de Gimnasia y Esgrima La Plata|Gimnasia La Plata]] on loan.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tycsports.com/liga-profesional-de-futbol/rodrigo-castillo-llega-a-gimnasia-id322320.html|title=Rodrigo Castillo llega a Gimnasia|trans-title=Rodrigo Castillo arrives at Gimnasia|publisher=[[TyC Sports]]|language=es|date=18 February 2021|accessdate=16 March 2026}}</ref> After impressing with the reserve side, he signed a permanent deal with the club for the 2022 season.

===Gimnasia La Plata===
====Loan to Deportivo Madryn====
On 10 January 2022, however, after being deemed surplus to requirements by manager [[Néstor Gorosito]], Castillo was loaned to [[Primera Nacional]] side [[Deportivo Madryn]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.laplata1.com/2022-01-10/sin-lugar-en-gimnasia-rodrigo-castillo-ya-encontro-club-68978/|title=Sin lugar en Gimnasia Rodrigo Castillo ya encontró club|trans-title=Without a place at Gimnasia, Rodrigo Castillo already found a club|publisher=La Plata 1|language=es|date=10 January 2022|accessdate=16 March 2026}}</ref> He made his professional debut on 12 February, coming on as a late [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] and scoring the winner in a 1–0 home success over [[Club Agropecuario Argentino|Agropecuario]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.diariojornada.com.ar/319620/deportes/Castillo_el_heroe_del_Aurinegro_en_su_historico_debut_|title=Castillo, el héroe del "Aurinegro" en su histórico debut|trans-title=Castillo, the yellow-and-black's hero in their historic debut|publisher=Diario Jornada|language=es|date=13 February 2022|accessdate=16 March 2026}}</ref> He impressed with the side during the season, scoring 12 goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eldia.com/nota/2022-11-11-3-24-42-rodrigo-castillo-el-delantero-que-sorprendio-en-madryn-y-debe-volver-deportes|title=Rodrigo Castillo, el delantero que sorprendió en Madryn y debe volver|trans-title=Rodrigo Castillo, the forward who impressed at Madryn and might return|publisher=DiarioEl Día de La Plata|language=es|date=11 November 2022|accessdate=16 March 2026}}</ref>

====Breakthrough====
Back to Gimnasia in January 2023, Castillo made his club – and [[Argentine Primera División|Primera División]] – debut on 30 January, starting in a 3–1 away loss to [[Club Atlético Vélez Sarsfield|Vélez Sarsfield]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://provinciaradio.com.ar/noticia.php?noti_id=14936|title=Rodrigo Castillo: “nos adaptamos rápido a la idea que propuso el cuerpo técnico”|trans-title=Rodrigo Castillo: "we adapted quickly to the idea proposed by the technical staff"|publisher=Radio Provincia AM 1270 / FM 97.UNE|language=es|date=27 May 2024|accessdate=16 March 2026}}</ref> He renewed his contract until December 2025 on 23 March,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gimnasia.org.ar/castillo-renovo-su-contrato-con-el-lobo/|title=¡Castillo renovó su contrato con el Lobo!|trans-title=Castillo renewed his contract with the ''Lobo''!|publisher=Club de Gimnasia y Esgrima La Plata|language=es|date=23 March 2023|accessdate=16 March 2026}}</ref> and scored his first goal in the top tier on 16 July, but in a 3–1 home loss to [[Boca Juniors]].

On 24 September 2024, after establishing himself as a first-choice, Castillo further extended his link until the end of 2026.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gimnasia.org.ar/rodrigo-castillo-renovo-con-el-lobo/|title=¡Rodrigo Castillo renovó con el Lobo!|trans-title=Castillo renewed his contract with the ''Lobo''!|publisher=Club de Gimnasia y Esgrima La Plata|language=es|date=24 September 2024|accessdate=16 March 2026}}</ref>

===Lanús===
On 7 July 2025, Castillo moved to fellow top-tier side [[Club Atlético Lanús|Lanús]] on a three-and-a-half-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clublanus.com/rodrigo-castillo-se-suma-al-club-atletico-lanus/|title=Rodrigo Castillo se suma al Club Atlético Lanús|trans-title=Rodrigo Castillo joins Club Atlético Lanús|publisher=Club Atlético Lanús|language=es|date=7 July 2025|accessdate=16 March 2026}}</ref> An immediate starter, he helped the side to reach the [[2025 Copa Sudamericana final]] by scoring all his side's three goals in the semifinals against [[Club Universidad de Chile|Universidad de Chile]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tycsports.com/copa-sudamericana/rodrigo-castillo-pelea-clasificacion-lanus-copa-sudamericana-universidad-de-chile-u-de-chile-final-id695723.html|title=Castillo, sobre la pelea tras la clasificación de Lanús en la Sudamericana: "Los de la U nos quisieron sacar jugadores para la final"|trans-title=Castillo, about the brawl after Lanús' qualification in the Sudamericana: "The ones from ''la U'' wanted to take players off the final"|publisher=[[TyC Sports]]|language=es|date=31 October 2025|accessdate=16 March 2026}}</ref>

===Fluminense===
On 3 March 2026, [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A]] side [[Fluminense FC|Fluminense]] announced the signing of Castillo on a five-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fluminense.com.br/noticia/fluminense-acerta-a-contratacao-de-rodrigo-castillo|title=Fluminense acerta a contratação de Rodrigo Castillo|trans-title=Fluminense agree the signing of Rodrigo Castillo|publisher=Fluminense FC|language=pt-BR|date=3 March 2026|accessdate=16 March 2026}}</ref>

'''Eirik Saunes''' (born 22 September 1998) is a Norwegian footballer who plays as a midfielder for [[KFUM-Kameratene Oslo|KFUM]].

==Personal life==
He was born in [[Bærum]]<ref>{{WorldFootball.net|new_id=pe937016}}</ref> as a son of football manager [[Hallstein Saunes]], who managed [[Lyn Fotball|Lyn]] in the mid-1990s.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.jbl.no/fjoraret-var-en-stor-opptur-for-far-og-sonn/s/5-103-1126091|title=Fjoråret var en stor opptur for far og sønn|date=1 March 2025|work=Jærbladet|language=sv|access-date=14 April 2026}}</ref> Hallstein Saunes became manager of [[IL Hødd]] in 1999, and Eirik Saunes grew up in [[Ulsteinvik]] where he enrolled in Hødd at the age of 6.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.smp.no/sport/n/75B7l8/heimeavla-hodd-hap|title=Heimeavla Hødd-håp|date=15 July 2017|work=Sunnmørsposten|language=nn|access-date=14 April 2026}}</ref>

He was participating in athletics as a child, and ran the [[half marathon]] in 1:21:18 shortly after his 16th birthday.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.vikebladet.no/sport/n/RyXLzW/beste-16-aring-i-oslo|title=Beste 16-åring i Oslo|date=25 September 2014|work=Vikebladet Vestposten|language=nn|access-date=14 April 2026}}</ref> He was involved in a charity project in Brazilian [[favela]]s called Karanba.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.vikebladet.no/sport/n/vOGJOw/dei-treng-det-mykje-meir-enn-eg-gjer|title=– Dei treng det mykje meir enn eg gjer|date=14 December 2017|work=Vikebladet Vestposten|language=nn|access-date=14 April 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.vikebladet.no/sport/n/EwXPl5/eirik-gav-50-000-til-favelaborn|title=Eirik gav 50.000 til favelaborn|date=18 January 2018|work=Vikebladet Vestposten|language=nn|access-date=14 April 2026}}</ref>

==Career==
Saunes made his first-team debut for Hødd in May 2017. He amassed 134 league games and 10 cup games in six seasons, all spent in the [[2. divisjon]].<ref name=nff>{{NFF|3457889}}</ref> Having helped Hødd win promotion to the [[2023 1. divisjon]], he nonetheless left the club to sign for another First Division club ahead of the 2023 season, [[Bryne FK]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nrk.no/mr/eirik-franke-saunes-ferdig-i-hodd-1.16219551|title=Eirik Franke Saunes ferdig i Hødd|date=13 December 2022|publisher=NRK|language=nn|access-date=14 April 2026}}</ref>

Bryne won promotion to the [[2025 Eliteserien]], and Saunes subsequently made his first-tier debut in April 2025 against Haugesund.<ref name=nff/> He expressed joy in playing for the club with its underdog and rural farming image.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.tv2.no/sport/fotball/eliteserien/saunes-pa-lamming-vi-er-ikke-en-gjeng-byaser/17630199/|title=Saunes på lamming: – Vi er ikke en gjeng «byaser»|date=19 April 2025|publisher=TV 2|language=no|access-date=14 April 2026}}</ref> His goal celebration was a [[reindeer]] imitation.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.jbl.no/ingen-elg-men-et-reinsdyr/s/5-103-1160257|title=Slik forklarer han feringen|date=1 June 2025|work=Jærbladet|language=no|access-date=14 April 2026}}</ref>

Following Bryne's instant relegation,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.smp.no/sport/n/M7gvn0/fortvilte-etter-nedrykket-det-er-blytungt|title=Bryne-spilleren Eirik Saunes fortvilte etter nedrykket|date=12 December 2025|work=Sunnmørsposten|language=no|access-date=14 April 2026}}</ref> he continued in the Eliteserien with [[KFUM-Kameratene Oslo|KFUM]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.vikebladet.no/sport/n/43qemq/gaar-fraa-bryne-til-kfum-oslo|title=Går frå Bryne til KFUM Oslo|date=3 January 2026|work=Vikebladet Vestposten|language=nn|access-date=14 April 2026}}</ref>

'''Joseba Ezkurdia Galarraga''', known professionally as '''Ezkurdia''', is a [[Basque pelota]] forward player. He is a three-time champion of the [[Cuatro y Medio Euskadi Championship]] (2018, 2019 and 2022), and also of the [[Bare-handed Pelota First League Doubles]] (2018, 2020 and 2025).

== Professional career ==

Ezkurdia made his professional debut on 28 December 2011 on the [[Beotibar fronton]], from [[Tolosa, Spain]]. He lost the game along with Íñigo Pascual to Mikel Idoate and Miguel Merino Soto (Merino I) for a final score of 21-22. The match was part of the Bare-handed Pelota Second League Doubles.<ref>{{cite news |author1=L. G. |title=La primera lección para Ezkurdia |url=https://www.diariodenavarra.es/noticias/deportes/pelota/la_primera_leccion_para_ezkurdia_61539_1053.html |access-date=17 April 2026 |work=Diario de Navarra |date=29 December 2011 |language=es}}</ref>

He continued to progress in his career until the 2018 season, in which he achieved a double by winning the ''txapela'' of the [[Bare-handed Pelota First League Doubles]] with José Javier Zabaleta;<ref>{{cite news |author1=Redacción |title=Ezkurdia y Zabaleta, campeones de Parejas 2018 |url=https://gasteizberri.com/2018/04/ezkurdia-y-zabaleta-campeones-de-parejas-2018/ |access-date=17 April 2026 |work=Gasteiz Berri |date=8 April 2018 |language=es}}</ref> and the [[Cuatro y Medio Euskadi Championship]], whose final was played for the first time in the new [[Navarra Arena]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Laquidain |first1=Javier |author2=EFE |title=Ezkurdia, campeón del 4 y medio |url=https://cadenaser.com/emisora/2018/11/18/radio_pamplona/1542574232_267030.html |access-date=17 April 2026 |work=Cadena Ser |date=18 November 2018 |language=es}}</ref>

The following season, 2019, he won the Cuatro y Medio Euskadi Championship again in the same venue and against the same opponent, Jokin Altuna (Altuna III).<ref>{{cite news |author1=EiTB |title=Ezkurdia rompe los pronósticos y revalida la txapela |url=https://kirolakeitb.eus/es/pelota/pelota-mano/cuatro-y-medio/2019/11/17/final-4-medio-2019-joseba-ezkurdia-gana-txapela-jokin-altuna-2216/ |access-date=17 April 2026 |work=Kirolak EiTB |date=17 November 2019 |language=es}}</ref>

In the 2020 season, he won the Bare-handed Pelota First League Doubles with Julen Martija,<ref>{{cite news |author1=RC |author2=EFE Bilbao |title=Ezkurdia y Martija, campeones del Parejas |url=https://www.noticiasdealava.eus/deportes/2020/12/08/ezkurdia-martija-campeones-parejas-1152443.html |access-date=17 April 2026 |work=Noticias de Alava |date=8 December 2020 |language=es}}</ref> but in the Cuatro y Medio Euskadi Championship he lost in the semi-finals against Erik Jaka.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ormazabal |first1=Jon |title=El momento de Erik Jaka hace descarrilar a Ezkurdia en un duelo frenético (22-16) |url=https://www.naiz.eus/eu/info/noticia/20201220/el-momento-de-erik-jaka-hace-descarrilar-a-ezkurdia-en-un-duelo-frenetico |access-date=17 April 2026 |date=20 December 2020 |language=es}}</ref>

In the 2021 season, he was left out of the competition in both tournaments in which he was already a two-time champion.

The following season, he won the Cuatro y Medio Euskadi Championship for a third time (again against Altuna III), and he managed to reach the final of the [[Bare-handed Pelota First League]], which he lost against Unai Laso.<ref>{{cite news |author1=NaTV |title=Ezkurdia gana a Altuna en una final para recordar |url=https://www.navarratelevision.es/noticia/ze53aa392-9757-673e-4d81b7de7cb0b6d1/202211/ezkurdia-gana-a-altuna-en-una-final-para-recordar |access-date=17 April 2026 |work=Navarra Television |date=20 November 2022 |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author1=Redacción |title=Unai Laso consigue su primera txapela profesional en el Navarra Arena de Pamplona |url=https://navarra.okdiario.com/articulo/pelota/cronica-final-pelota-manomanista-ezkurdia-laso-navarra-arena-pamplona/20220529165106411834.html |access-date=17 April 2026 |work=Navarra.com |date=29 May 2022 |language=es}}</ref>

He did not win another championship until the 2025 Bare-handed Pelota First League Doubles with Beñat Rezusta.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Morin |first1=Ubay |title=Ezkurdia y Rezusta campeones del parejas 2025 tras vencer 22-20 |url=https://21iguales.com/2025/03/31/ezkurdia-y-rezusta-campeones-del-parejas-2025-tras-vencer-22-20/ |access-date=17 April 2026 |work=21 Iguales |date=31 March 2025 |language=es}}</ref>

{{Short description|American abstract painter (born 1990)}} {{Infobox artist | name = Lucy Bull | birth_date = {{birth year and age|1990}} | birth_place = New York City, New York, U.S. | education = Rhode Island School of Design (attended);
[[School of the Art Institute of Chicago]], BFA, 2012 | known_for = Painting | movement = [[Abstract art|Abstraction]] | patrons = | awards = | website = {{URL|lucybull.com}} }} '''Lucy Bull''' (born 1990) is an American [[abstract art|abstract]] painter based in Los Angeles and New York. She is known for large-scale paintings that employ a variety of procedural strategies and bold colors to produce complex textural compositions. Her work is held in the permanent collections of major institutions including the [[Hirshhorn Museum and Sculpture Garden]], [[Los Angeles County Museum of Art]], and the [[Museum of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles]], among others. ==Early life and education== Bull was born in 1990 in New York. Both of her parents are artists. Her mother is a painter and multimedia artist. When Bull and her twin sister were growing up, she designed textiles. Her father is a documentary filmmaker and former teaching assistant to [[Manny Farber]], a painter and theorist.{{cite web |url=https://news.artnet.com/art-world/the-endurance-test-of-lucy-bulls-visceral-abstractions-2491066 |title=The Endurance Test of Lucy Bull's Visceral Abstractions |work=[[artnet]] |date=May 24, 2024}} She initially attended the [[Rhode Island School of Design]] before transferring in 2010 to the [[School of the Art Institute of Chicago]], where she earned a BFA in 2012. In Chicago, she developed an interest in curatorial practice, organizing her first exhibition project—a group show staged at a dim sum restaurant, organized around a lazy susan—while taking a class with artist Joseph Grigely based on his book ''Exhibition Prosthetics''.{{cite web |url=https://www.interviewmagazine.com/art/20-minutes-in-miami-with-artist-lucy-bull |title="I'm Obsessed With Ambiguity": 20 Minutes in Miami With Artist Lucy Bull |work=[[Interview (magazine)|Interview]] |date=December 10, 2024}} After college she moved briefly to New York before relocating to Los Angeles, where she has been based since. ==Career== Bull began exhibiting in Los Angeles as part of the city's independent gallery scene. In her words, this was when "things started to click".{{cite web |url=https://thecreativeindependent.com/people/painter-and-curator-lucy-bull-on-being-addicted-to-your-work/ |title=Painter and curator Lucy Bull on being addicted to your work |work=The Creative Independent |date=September 26, 2022}} Her first exhibition, ''Queens Way'' (2017), was staged at the RMS Queen Mary in [[Long Beach, California]], presented by the art-run platform Mother Culture.{{cite web |url=https://www.davidkordanskygallery.com/artist/lucy-bull |title=Lucy Bull |publisher=David Kordansky Gallery}} In 2018, Bull founded From the Desk of Lucy Bull, a table-top exhibition space she operated from her East Hollywood apartment. The project grew out of a period when a hand injury prevented her from painting; she invited artists to present small exhibitions on and around a six-foot steel desk. Artists who have presented projects through the series include Ficus Interfaith, Loren Kramar, Elizabeth Englander, Lauren Quin, Mathis Altmann, Isabelle Frances McGuire, Michael Bala, and Alexandra Metcalf.{{cite web |title=From the Desk of Lucy Bull |url=https://www.lucybull.com/from-the-desk-of-lucy-bull |website=lucybull.com |access-date=June 11, 2026}} The Desk has also hosted performance evenings, dinner gatherings, and group exhibitions, and has appeared in other contexts, including a presentation at the Los Angeles Art Book Fair and three editions of From the Xmas Tree of Lucy Bull. The project later relocated to the East Village in [[New York City]], where it remains active. In 2019, Bull had her first solo exhibitions concurrently at Smart Objects and the artist-run project space Queens, both in Los Angeles. The same year she presented ''The Damage'' at Human Resources in Los Angeles, a painted lightbox installed on the facade of the building, accompanied by a 24-hour movie marathon.{{cite web |title=Unveiling of The Damage + 24 Hour Movie Marathon |url=https://www.h-r.la/event/unveiling-of-the-damage-24-hour-movie-marathon/ |website=Human Resources |location=Los Angeles |date=2019 |access-date=June 11, 2026}} Bull went on to show with the gallery High Art, first in Paris in 2019 and again in Arles in 2020. It was during this time that her work became known to a wider audience.{{cite web |title=Why There's a Bull Market for Lucy Bull's Psychedelic Paintings |url=https://news.artnet.com/market/work-of-the-week-lucy-bull-2587814 |website=[[artnet]] |date=December 17, 2024 |access-date=June 11, 2026}} Bull joined David Kordansky Gallery and had her first exhibition with the gallery, ''Skunk Grove'', in Los Angeles in 2021, followed by ''Piper'' in 2022 at Kordansky's New York location, and ''Ash Tree'' in 2024. In conjunction with ''Ash Tree'', Bull curated a 24-hour marathon film screening at Lumiere Cinema in Los Angeles, her second such marathon after the 2019 screening at Human Resources.{{cite web |title=Lucy Bull: Ash Tree |url=https://www.davidkordanskygallery.com/exhibitions/lucy-bull |website=David Kordansky Gallery |date=2024 |access-date=June 11, 2026}} In 2023, she was the subject of solo presentations at The Warehouse in Dallas and the Long Museum West Bund in Shanghai. Her first U.S. museum solo exhibition, ''The Garden of Forking Paths'', was presented at the [[Institute of Contemporary Art, Miami]] from December 2024 through March 2025, comprising sixteen paintings made between 2019 and 2024 and organized by curator Gean Moreno.{{cite web |url=https://icamiami.org/exhibition/lucy-bull-the-garden-of-forking-paths/ |title=Lucy Bull: The Garden of Forking Paths |publisher=Institute of Contemporary Art, Miami |date=2024}} In parallel, the museum commissioned a 39-foot painting for its three-story stairwell, which debuted alongside the exhibition and remained on view through September 2025, beyond the run of the show. ==Artistic practice== Bull works primarily in oil on linen. Her paintings are characterized by densely layered, gestural compositions built up through repeated applications of paint.{{cite web |url=https://www.wmagazine.com/culture/lucy-bull-david-kordansky-studio-visit |title=In the Studio With Lucy Bull, the Painter Bringing Back Abstraction |website=[[W (magazine)|W Magazine]] |date=February 20, 2024}} Her process involves using brushes in unconventional ways, including dabbing, stabbing, twisting, and scraping.{{cite web |url=https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2024/05/17/lucy-bull-abstract-painter-art-market-demand |title=Collectors stampeding to Lucy Bull's 'visionary' abstractions |website=[[The Art Newspaper]] |date=May 17, 2024}} Bull has described the scratching in her process as a form of excavation in which older marks from beginning layers are pulled to the foreground, acting as a relief as subsequent layers are built up.{{cite web |title=Getting Lost in the Brushstrokes: Lucy Bull Interviewed |url=https://bombmagazine.org/articles/2021/04/26/getting-lost-in-the-brushstrokes-lucy-bull-interviewed/ |website=[[BOMB Magazine]] |date=April 26, 2021 |access-date=June 11, 2026}} The result has been described in synesthetic terms—evoking sonic or tactile sensations as much as visual ones. She has invoked the late British painter [[Howard Hodgkin]] to describe her approach, noting: "I am a representational painter, but not a painter of appearances. I paint representational pictures of emotional situations." Her work engages themes of perception, consciousness, projection, and the limits of cognition, with many paintings evoking altered or dream-like psychological states. Critics have noted the paintings' resistance to fixed interpretation, and Bull has described them as functioning like [[Rorschach inkblot test|Rorschach inkblots]] in which the viewer's response reveals as much about their own psychology as about the work. Elsewhere Bull has stated "I want to titillate the senses. I want to draw people closer. I think people aren’t used to paying much-prolonged attention to paintings on walls and I want to allow people to have more of a sensory experience. I want to draw them in so that there is the opportunity for things to open up and for them to wander."{{cite web |url=https://whitewall.art/art/getting-lost-in-the-enigmatic-paintings-of-lucy-bull/ |title=Getting Lost in the Enigmatic Paintings of Lucy Bull |work=[[Whitewall]] |date=November 18, 2021}} ==Selected exhibitions== ===Solo and two-person exhibitions=== *2024–2025: ''The Garden of '''{{Nihongo|Akane Yonezawa|米澤 茜|Yonezawa Akane|Born December 31, 1998|lead=yes}}''' is a Japanese rock/metal musician and [[Voice acting in Japan|voice actress]]. She was a member of Try Try Niiche and is currently the drummer for Japanese metal band [[Ave Mujica]].

== Biography ==
Born on December 31, 1998 in the [[Tottori Prefecture]], Yonezawa started taking drumming lessons while visiting the fourth year of elementary school. After she graduated from [[University]] she played drums in several bands as a hobby musician. To start a professional drumming career, Yonezawa moved to [[Tokyo]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.oricon.co.jp/news/2294611/full/ |title=Ave Mujica、謎に包まれたヘヴィサウンドの真実 才気あふれる5人が生み出すアンサンブルの実像【インタビュー前編】 |work=[[Oricon News]] |date=September 15, 2023 |language=ja |access-date=April 25, 2026}}</ref>

Between March 2019 and November 2020, Yonezawa was an active member in [[Try Try Niiche]], a Japanese pop-rock band where she played drums under the moniker ''Abanun''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://skream.jp/news/2019/03/try_try_niiche_reunite.php |title=TRY TRY NIICHE、新メンバー あばぬん（Dr）迎え活動再開。新曲「いつかの少年」MV公開。5/11自主企画開催＆会場限定シングル『いつかの少年 / 蕾』リリースも |work=Skream.jp |date=March 4, 2019 |language=ja |access-date=April 25, 2026}}</ref> In 2023, she was cast for the character role Nyamu Yūtenji and became the drummer of [[Ave Mujica]], a metal band belonging to the ''[[BanG Dream!]]'' media franchise.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://natalie.mu/comic/pp/mygo |title=「BanG Dream! It's MyGO!!!!!」これまでの「バンドリ！」とは一線を画す、キラキラじゃない感情がぶつかり合う迷子たちの物語 |work=[[Music Natalie]] |date=September 7, 2023 |language=ja |access-date=April 25, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.crunchyroll.com/news/latest/2024/10/18/bang-dream-ave-mujica-tv-anime-january-2-2025-premiere-trailer |title=BanG Dream! '''Cristián Marcelo Garay Reyes''' (born 8 April 1989<ref>{{Cite news |last=Cipriani |first=Oiti |date=30 May 2026 |title=Palmeiras 4×1 Junior Barranquilla: arbitragem de Cristian Garay |url=https://3vv.com.br/novo/palmeiras-4x1-junior-barranquilla-arbitragem-de-cristian-garay/ |access-date=9 June 2026 |work=3vv Brasil |language=pt-br}}</ref>) is a Chilean [[Referee (association football)|football referee]] who has been on the [[FIFA International Referees List|FIFA International List of Referees]] since 2019.

== Career ==
Born in April 1989 in [[Macul]], [[Chile]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Benedetti |first=Eliezer |date=26 March 2025 |title=¿Quién es Cristián Garay, el árbitro del Perú vs Venezuela?: el historial polémico del juez chileno que fue castigado en su país |url=https://www.infobae.com/peru/deportes/2025/03/26/quien-es-cristian-garay-el-arbitro-del-peru-vs-venezuela-el-historial-polemico-del-juez-chileno-con-decisiones-incorrectas-en-el-pasado/ |work=[[Infobae]] |language=es}}</ref> Garay ascended to the [[Liga de Primera]] in 2018 and received his [[FIFA]] badge one year later.<ref name=":0" /> He previously refereed in the [[Campeonato Nacional Primera B]], the second division of [[Chilean football]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |last=Muñóz |first=Felipe |date=7 March 2023 |title=El historial y la polémica más recordada de Cristián Garay, el árbitro que correría con ventaja para dirigir su primer Superclásico |url=https://www.emol.com/noticias/Deportes/2023/03/07/1088587/historial-polemicas-cristian-garay-arbitro.html |access-date=9 June 2026 |work=[[El Mercurio]] |language=es}}</ref> Garay is part of the "new generation" of Chilean referees who are mentored by [[Roberto Tobar]], a former referee himself.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |date=12 April 2023 |title=Las polémicas de Cristián Garay, el árbitro escogido para el duelo entre la UC y Colo Colo |url=https://www.latercera.com/el-deportivo/noticia/las-polemicas-de-cristian-garay-el-arbitro-escogido-para-el-duelo-entre-la-uc-y-colo-colo/JTIJIT337RAQ5HTFLJXWRGYU2A/ |access-date=9 June 2026 |work=[[La Tercera]] |language=es}}</ref><ref name=":1" />

Within [[Conmebol|CONMEBOL]], Garay has overseen matches at Copa Sudamericana and [[Copa Libertadores]], as well as qualification games for the [[FIFA World Cup]].<ref name=":0" /> He was also appointed as one of the two Chilean referees at the [[2024 Copa América]] in the United States, the other being [[Piero Maza]]. In the tournament, Garay refereed a group stage match between [[Ecuador national football team|Ecuador]] and [[Jamaica national football team|Jamaica]] at [[Allegiant Stadium]] in [[Paradise, Nevada]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=25 June 2024 |title=El historial del árbitro Cristian Garay dirigiendo a la Selección de Ecuador |url=https://www.ole.com.ar/ecuador/la-tri/historial-arbitro-cristian-garay-chileno-dirigiendo-seleccion-ecuador-jamaica-copa-america_0_KsFVKBU6e6.html |access-date=9 June 2026 |work=[[Olé (sports newspaper)|Olé]] |language=es}}</ref>

Garay has been involved in high-stakes matches as well as in some controversies,<ref name=":3">{{Cite news |last=Vázquez |first=Luis Guillermo |date=18 June 2025 |title=Así es Cristián Garay, el árbitro que dirigirá el partido de Inter Miami ante el Porto en el Mundial de Clubes 2025 |url=https://as.com/us/futbol/asi-es-cristian-garay-el-arbitro-que-dirigira-el-partido-de-inter-miami-ante-el-oporto-en-el-mundial-de-clubes-2025-n/ |url-status= |access-date=9 June 2026 |work=[[Diario AS]] |language=es}}</ref> including the request by [[Argentine]] international referee [[Javier Castrilli]] to dismiss him from Liga de Primera games. Castrilli had been chosen as the head of the Commission of Referees of Chile. That same year, Garay was heavily criticized by manager [[Francisco Meneghini]], who considered that he had made detrimental decisions against his team, [[Everton de Viña del Mar|Everton Viña del Mar]]. In 2025, Garay was selected for the [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup|FIFA Club World Cup]].<ref name=":3" />

Other controversies included one in a March 2026 match in the [[Saudi Pro League]] where he oversaw a game between [[Al Fateh SC]] and [[Al Hilal SFC|Al Hilal]], giving a [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty kick]] to Al Fateh in the 96th minute of the match; upon being called by the [[video assistant referee]], Garay retracted his decision.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Rebolar |first=Juan Pedro |date=16 March 2026 |title=Video: La gran polémica del árbitro chileno Cristián Garay en Arabia Saudita tras anular un penal con el VAR |url=https://www.emol.com/noticias/Deportes/2026/03/15/1194354/cristian-garay-arbitro-polemica-arabia.html |access-date=9 June 2026 |work=[[El Mercurio]] |language=es}}</ref>

In local football, Garay refereed [[Club Deportivo Universidad Católica|Universidad Católica]] and [[Colo-Colo]] in April 2023.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /> He was selected as a referee for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]], where his only appearance was in the [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group B#Canada vs Qatar|Group B match]] between co-hosts [[Canada men's national soccer team|Canada]] and [[Qatar national football team|Qatar]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Cerutti |first=Sebastián |date=7 June 2026 |title=Quién es Cristián Garay: árbitro del Mundial 2026 |url=https://www.dazn.com/es-MX/news/f%C3%BAtbol/quien-es-cristian-garay-arbitro/fvwt21ba3yzd1g3n2xkmoppb7 |access-date=9 June 2026 |work=[[DAZN]] |language=es}}</ref>

Árbitro Asistente FIFA {{!}} Comisión de Árbitros FMF |url=https://arbitraje.fmf.mx/ficha-arbitro/sandra-elizabeth-ramirez-aleman_56993_2_4 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240617174352/https://arbitraje.fmf.mx/ficha-arbitro/sandra-elizabeth-ramirez-aleman_56993_2_4 |archive-date=17 June 2024 |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=arbitraje.fmf.mx |language=en |url-status=live }}) is a Mexican football [[Assistant referee (association football)|assistant referee]] who has been listed on the [[FIFA International Referees List]] since 2019. == Career == Ramírez Alemán was born on 8 January 1989 in [[Guadalajara]], [[Jalisco]], and played football in her adolescence and early youth while she studied [[dentistry]] at the [[University of Guadalajara]]. She began her career in refereeing when one of her teammates at the university's football team asked her to relieve her in a match that she could not oversee because of other responsibilities.{{Cite news |last=Gamiño |first=Sonia G. |date=2026-04-25 |title=Sandra Ramírez árbitra asistente jalisciense hará historia en Mundial |url=https://www.milenio.com/futbol-internacional/mundial/sandra-ramirez-arbitra-asistente-jalisciense-hara-historia-en-mundial |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=Grupo Milenio |url-access=subscription|language=es}} After that game, Ramírez started studies into professional refereeing at the school of the [[Mexican Football Federation]]. At university, she also practiced [[Sport of athletics|athletics]] aside from football. Between 2010 and 2019, Ramírez alternated between her profession as a dentist and an assistant referee. She made her debut at the [[Ascenso MX]] in a match between [[Potros UAEM]] and [[Zacatepec F.C.]]{{Cite web |last=Coello | first=Luz |date=2026-05-29 |title=Katia Itzel García y Sandra Ramírez, las árbitras mexicanas que harán historia en el Mundial 2026 |url=https://www.infobae.com/mexico/deportes/2026/05/29/katia-itzel-garcia-y-sandra-ramirez-las-arbitras-mexicanas-que-haran-historia-en-el-mundial-2026/ |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=infobae |language=es-MX}} She continued ascending through local leagues, including the [[Liga Premier de México]] and youth competitions, until reaching [[Liga MX]] in both [[Liga MX Femenil|women's]] and men's tournaments. Outside Mexican leagues, Ramírez made her international debut at the [[2022 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup]] in [[Costa Rica]]. In 2023, she suffered from a [[fibular fracture]] as a consequence of [[Stress (biology)|stress]].{{Cite web |title=Sandra Ramírez, otra mexicana con historia en el Mundial |url=https://www.sinembargo.mx/4821409/sandra-ramirez-de-la-odontologia-a-hacer-historia-en-el-arbitraje-del-mundial-2026/ |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=SinEmbargo MX {{!}} Periodismo digital con rigor. |language=es}} After making a full recovery, Ramírez was selected for the [[2023 FIFA Women's World Cup]] in Australia and New Zealand, where she served as an assistant referee for Honduran referee [[Melissa Borjas]] in two group stage games: [[2023 FIFA Women's World Cup Group G#Italy vs Argentina|Italy vs Argentina]] and [[2023 FIFA Women's World Cup Group H#Germany vs Colombia|Germany vs Colombia]].{{Cite web |date=2026-06-14 |title=Quién es Katia Itzel García, la cuarta árbitra de Países Bajos vs. Japón en el Mundial 2026 |url=https://bolavip.com/mx/mundial/quien-es-katia-itzel-garcia-la-cuarta-arbitra-de-paises-bajos-vs-japon-en-el-mundial-2026 |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=Bolavip México |language=es-MX}} In 2024, Ramírez was called for games at the [[2024 CONCACAF Nations League Finals|CONCACAF Nations League Finals]], the [[2024 CONCACAF W Gold Cup]], and the [[2025 CONCACAF Gold Cup]], as well as qualification matches for the [[FIFA World Cup]] for CONCACAF. That same year, she took part in the [[2024 Summer Olympics]], serving under referee [[Katia Itzel García]] and along with fellow Mexican assistant referee Karen Díaz, overseeing the match between [[Football at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Women's tournament#Group B|Germany and Australia]].{{Cite web| title=Actuación histórica de la árbitra Katia Itzel García en París 2024 |url=https://www.foxdeportes.com/olimpiadas/nota/actuacion-historica-de-la-arbitra-katia-itzel-garcia-en-paris-2024 |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=www.foxdeportes.com |language=es}} In April 2026, Ramírez was appointed to the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]] in North America, serving again under [[Referee (association football)|pitch referee]] García.{{Cite news |last=Riviera Martínez |first=Xavier |date=10 April 2026 |title=Katia Itzel García y Sandra Ramírez harán historia como árbitras mexicanas en el Mundial 2026 |url=https://eldiariodesonora.com.mx/deportes/2026/04/10/katia-itzel-garcia-mundial-2026.html |work=El Diario de Sonora |language=es}}{{Cite web |last=García |first=Roger |date=2026-06-15 |title=Árbitras Katia Itzel García y Sandra Ramírez tienen nueva designación en el Mundial 2026 |url=https://lopezdoriga.com/deportes/arbitras-katia-itzel-garcia-sandra-ramirez-nueva-designacion-mundial-2026/ |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=López-Dóriga Digital |language=es}} == References == {{Reflist}} {{2026 FIFA World Cup referees}} {{2023 FIFA Women's World Cup referees}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Ramírez, Sandra}} [[Category:1989 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Mexican football referees]] [[Category:Association football assistant referees]] [[Category:21st-century Mexican sportswomen]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Guadalajara, Jalisco]] [[Category:University of Guadalajara alumni]] [[Category:Mexican dentists]] [[Category:2026 FIFA World Cup referees]]

'''Alice Gabrielle Affonso Carvalho''' (Natal, 15 June 1996) is a Brazilian actress, screenwriter, and singer. Most known for portraying Dinorah in [[Amazon Prime Video|Prime Video]]'s Brazilian drama series ''[[New Bandits]]'' (2023).<ref>{{Cite news |last=Marques |first=Patrícia |date=23 September 2023 |title=Dinorah em 'Cangaço Novo', Alice Carvalho precisou mudar completamente a rotina para viver heroína |trans-title=Dinorah in 'New Bandits', Alice Carvalho had to completely change her routine to play the heroine |url=https://www.itatiaia.com.br/editorias/entretenimento/2023/09/23/dinorah-em-cangaco-novo-alice-carvalho-precisou-mudar-completamente-a-rotina-para-viver-heroina |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231007060847/https://www.itatiaia.com.br/editorias/entretenimento/2023/09/23/dinorah-em-cangaco-novo-alice-carvalho-precisou-mudar-completamente-a-rotina-para-viver-heroina |archive-date=7 October 2023 |access-date=26 January 2026 |work=[[Rádio Itatiaia]] |language=pt-BR}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=22 September 2023 |title=Alice Carvalho: de R$ 600 por mês a Cangaço Novo |trans-title=Alice Carvalho: from R$ 600 per month to New Bandits |url=https://revistatrip.uol.com.br/trip-fm/alice-carvalho-de-r-600-por-mes-a-cangaco-novo |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230925062817/https://revistatrip.uol.com.br/trip-fm/alice-carvalho-de-r-600-por-mes-a-cangaco-novo |archive-date=25 September 2023 |access-date=26 July 2026 |work=Trip |language=pt-br}}</ref>

==Early life==
Alice Carvalho was born in the city of [[Natal, Rio Grande do Norte]], and raised in the city of [[Parnamirim]]. As a child, she first encountered theater as a form of therapy to alleviate [[hyperactivity]].<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
After several auditions and rejections as a teen, Carvalho experimented creating stories alongside other screenwriters and friends, starting with the web series ''SEPTO'' in 2016,<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Pinheiro |first=Malu |date=14 August 2023 |title='Amo tudo igual, sem dividir em caixas', revela Alice Carvalho sobre atuar, dirigir e escrever |trans-title='I love everything equally, without dividing it into boxes,' reveals Alice Carvalho about acting, directing, and writing |url=https://glamour.globo.com/entretenimento/filmes-e-series/noticia/2023/08/amo-tudo-igual-sem-dividir-em-caixas-revela-alice-carvalho-sobre-atuar-dirigir-e-escrever.ghtml |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231007060843/https://glamour.globo.com/entretenimento/filmes-e-series/noticia/2023/08/amo-tudo-igual-sem-dividir-em-caixas-revela-alice-carvalho-sobre-atuar-dirigir-e-escrever.ghtml |archive-date=7 October 2023 |access-date=26 July 2026 |work=[[Glamour (magazine)|Glamour]] |language=pt-BR}}</ref> which she portrayed Jéssica Borges, a young [[Triathlon|triathlete]] who tries to live her father's dream of competing in the [[Olympic Games]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=15 August 2018 |title=Entrevista com Alice Carvalho da websérie SEPTO |trans-title=Interview with Alice Carvalho from the web series SEPTO |url=https://lesbout.com.br/entrevista-com-alice-carvalho-da-webserie-septo/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231007060842/https://lesbout.com.br/entrevista-com-alice-carvalho-da-webserie-septo/ |archive-date=7 October 2023 |access-date=26 July 2026 |website=LesB Out! |language=pt-BR}}</ref>

'''Kim Seong-mi''' ([[Korean language|Korean]]: 김성미, born 2 April 1997) is a South Korean professional [[Football player|footballer]] who plays as a midfielder for [[WK League]] side [[Gangjin Swans WFC|Gangjin Swans]]. She played for South Korea at the [[2022 AFC Women's Asian Cup]].

== Club career ==
Kim was selected by [[Sejong Sportstoto WFC|Gumi Sportstoto]] in the first round of the [[2018 WK League]] new players draft.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cho |first=Hyun-hoo |date=27 December 2017 |title=2018 여자실업축구 신인선수 선발 드래프트 |trans-title=2018 women's works football new players draft |url=https://www.yna.co.kr/view/PYH20171227154000013 |access-date=17 September 2026 |website=[[Yonhap News Agency]] |language=ko}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Go |first=Mi-hye |date=27 December 2017 |title=홍혜지·손화연, WK리그 드래프트서 1·2순위로 신생 창녕WFC行 |trans-title=Hong Hye-ji, Son Hwa-yeon heading to Changnyeong WFC as first and second picks in WK League draft |url=https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20171227108100007 |access-date=17 September 2026 |website=[[Yonhap News Agency]] |language=ko}}</ref> After four years at Sportstoto, she transferred to Incheon Hyundai Steel Red Angels, making her debut appearance for the club in the first round of the [[2023 WK League]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jeon |first=Young-ji |date=24 March 2023 |title="이래서 절대1강" '최유정 멀티골'인천 현대제철,문경 상무에 3대0완승 |trans-title="That's why they're the best" Choi Yoo-jung scores brace as Incheon Hyundai Steel beat Mungyeong Sangmu 3-0 |url=https://www.sportschosun.com/football/2023-03-24/202303240100195890024178 |access-date=17 September 2026 |website=Sports Chosun |location=ko}}</ref> Kim signed with Gangjin Swans ahead of the [[2026 WK League]] season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=28 January 2026 |title=What we know so far about Gangjin Swans WFC |url=https://wkleaguenews.com/2026/01/28/about-gangjin-swans-wfc/ |access-date=17 September 2026 |website=WK League News}}</ref> She was named as one of the club's vice-captains.<ref>{{Cite web |date=31 March 2026 |title=2026 Preview: Gangjin Swans |url=https://wkleaguenews.com/2026/03/31/2026-preview-gangjin-swans/ |access-date=17 September 2026 |website=WK League News}}</ref>

== International career ==
Kim scored in a friendly against Australia while playing for South Korea's under-16 side, and later played for the country's [[South Korea women's national under-20 football team|under-20 team]], including at the [[2016 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kim |first=Hee-sun |date=12 May 2013 |title='김성미 선제골' U-16 女 대표팀, 친선경기서 호주와 1-1 |trans-title='Kim Seong-mi opening goal' women's U-16 national team draw 1-1 with Australia in friendly |url=https://sports.news.nate.com/view/20130512n13056 |access-date=17 September 2026 |website=OSEN |language=ko |via=Nate Sports}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kim |first=Kyung-yoon |date=2 November 2016 |title=U-20 여자축구대표팀 엔트리 확정…5일 출국 |trans-title=U-20 women's football team entry confirmed, set to leave country on 5th |url=https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20161102096500007 |access-date=17 September 2026 |website=[[Yonhap News Agency]] |language=ko}}</ref> She also played at the [[2017 Summer Universiade]], scoring a consolation goal in South Korea's final match against the United States as the team finished in sixth place.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hwang |first=Min-guk |date=30 August 2017 |title=女축구, 유니버시아드대회 6위로 마감 |trans-title=Women's football team finish Universiade in 6th |url=https://sports.khan.co.kr/article/201708300932003 |access-date=17 September 2026 |website=Sports Kyunghyang |language=ko}}</ref>

Kim received her first senior call-up for South Korea in 2021 under then-manager [[Colin Bell (footballer, born 1961)|Colin Bell]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kwon |first=Tae-kyung |date=11 June 2021 |title=송다희-김성미 "첫 발탁, 긴장되지만 즐겨야" |trans-title=Song Da-hee, Kim Seong-mi "First call-up: it's nervewracking but we have to enjoy it" |url=https://m.blog.naver.com/kfa_official_/223720347154 |access-date=17 September 2026 |publisher=[[Korea Football Association]] |language=ko |via=Naver Blog}}</ref> She was part of the squad for the [[2022 AFC Women's Asian Cup]], in which South Korea finished as runners-up.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jang |first=Bo-in |date=10 January 2022 |title=여자축구대표팀, 아시안컵 23명 확정…어희진·전은하 부상 낙마 |trans-title=Women's national team 23-strong squad for Asian Cup confirmed. Eo Hee-jin, Jeon Eun-ha out with injuries |url=https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20220110095100007 |access-date=17 September 2026 |website=[[Yonhap News Agency]] |language=ko}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Choi |first=Song-a |date=6 February 2022 |title=한국 여자축구, 아시안컵 준우승…결승전서 중국에 2-3 역전패 |trans-title=Korean women's football team runners-up in Asian Cup, lost 2-3 to China after going ahead in the final |url=https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20220206063300007 |access-date=17 September 2026 |website=[[Yonhap News Agency]] |language=ko}}</ref>

'''Emily Pendergast''' ({{nee|'''Sulenski'''}}; born February 25, 1987) is an American actress. She has appeared on TV series such as ''[[Veep]]'', ''[[Common Side Effects]]'', and ''[[Jury Duty Presents: Company Retreat]]''. She is a longtime member of [[the Groundlings]] improvisational comedy troupe.

==Early life==

Pendergast grew up in [[Canfield, Ohio]].<ref name="VA19">{{cite news|url=https://www.vindy.com/news/2019/may/25/actress-pendergast-canfield-seeks-more-after-veep-/|title=Actress Pendergast of Canfield seeks more after ‘Veep’ role|last=D'Astolfo|first=Guy|date=2019-05-25|newspaper=[[The Vindicator (Ohio newspaper)|The Vindicator]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190526024229/https://www.vindy.com/news/2019/may/25/actress-pendergast-canfield-seeks-more-after-veep-/|archive-date=2019-05-26}}</ref> She was a big fan of ''[[Saturday Night Live]]'' growing up, sometimes reenacting [[Dana Carvey]] or [[Adam Sandler]] sketches in home videos.<ref name="VA19"/> She graduated from [[Canfield High School]] in 2005, where she played [[association football|soccer]] as a [[letterwinner]] all four years.<ref name="VA19"/> She also sang in the choir and had small roles in theater.<ref name="VA19"/> She majored in psychology at [[Ohio University]], graduating in 2009.<ref name="VA19"/>

==Career==

Pendergast moved to Los Angeles after college to pursue an acting career.<ref name="VA19"/> She began working as a waitress and took classes with [[the Groundlings]] improvisational and sketch comedy group.<ref name="VA19"/> She said she had "looked up my comedic north stars and realized that Groundlings was the common denominator of several of them".<ref name="BW22">{{cite news|url=https://www.broadwayworld.com/los-angeles/article/Interview-Emily-Pendergasts-Happy-to-SUPPORT-Her-Groundlings-GROUP-20220826|title= Interview: Emily Pendergast's Happy to SUPPORT Her Groundlings' GROUP|last=Kaan|first=Gil|date=2022-02-26|website=[[BroadwayWorld]]|access-date=2026-09-17}}</ref> She immediately discovered that the Groundlings "felt like home" and was eventually promoted to the main company in 2017.<ref name="WF26">{{cite news|url=https://www.wfmj.com/video/news/canfield-native-takes-improv-to-the-next-level-in-company-retreat-part-i/video_2f54e146-a363-542e-b811-02a17603c872.html|title= Canfield native takes improv to the next level in "Company Retreat": Part I |date=2026-06-16|publisher=[[WFMJ-TV]]|access-date=2026-09-17|at=5:00}}</ref>

In 2019, she played the recurring role of [[Beth Ryan]], wife of presidential candidate [[Jonah Ryan|Jonah]], on the [[Veep season 7|last season]] of the [[HBO]] political satire ''[[Veep]]''.<ref name="VA19"/>

In 2025, she voiced the main role of Frances on the [[Netflix]] adult animated series ''[[Common Side Effects]]'', reuniting with former ''Veep'' writer [[Steve Hely]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.televisionacademy.com/features/online-originals/common-side-effects-adult-swim-interview|title=Common Side Effects Creators on Working With Mike Judge and Season 2 Hopes|last=Reinstein|first=Mara|date=2025-02-21|publisher=[[Academy of Television Arts & Sciences]]|access-date=2026-09-17}}</ref>

In 2026, she played the main role of Amy on the [[Amazon Prime Video]] series ''[[Jury Duty Presents: Company Retreat]]''.<ref name="WF26"/>

==Personal life==

She married Cory Pendergast on September 8, 2012.<ref>{{cite Instagram|postid=PnvBIXNoRI|title=Oh hello, happy week anniversary.|user=ependergast|date=2012-09-15|last=Pendergast|first=Emily|access-date=2026-09-17}}</ref>

'''Håkan Carl-Wiktor Charlie Svensson''' (born 11 January 1990) is a Swedish politician from the [[Christian Democrats (Sweden)|Christian Democrats]]. Svensson has been a regional councilor in [[Region Kalmar County]] since 2022.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2026-01-07 |language=sv |title=Regionråd |url=https://regionkalmar.se/politik-och-demokrati/politisk-organisation/sa-styrs-region-kalmar-lan/regionrad/ |work=regionkalmar.se}}<!-- auto-translated from Swedish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref><ref name=":1">{{cite web|access-date=2026-09-10 |language=sv |title=Företrädare – Högsby |url=https://kristdemokraterna.se/vart-parti/foretradare/foretradare/foretradare |work=kristdemokraterna.se}}<!-- auto-translated from Swedish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> Svensson previously represented the [[Moderate Party]], 2018–2022 as a non-serving deputy in the [[Riksdag]]. He has been First Deputy Chairman of the Municipal Council of [[Högsby Municipality|Högsby]] since 2022.

'''Seiya Takano''' ({{langx|ja|髙野 征也}}; born 9 January 1989) is a Japanese [[sepak takraw]] player who plays as a tosā (setter). He represents Japan internationally and has competed at multiple editions of the [[Asian Games]].<ref name="JSTAF">{{cite web
|title=男子強化指定選手
|url=https://jstaf.jp/japan/team-man
|publisher=Japan Sepaktakraw Association
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref>

== Career ==
Takano was born in [[Hiroshima]] and attended Sanyo High School before studying at [[Takushoku University]]. He began playing sepak takraw while at university after initially planning to continue playing football. He was selected for Japan's development squad within his first year of taking up the sport and subsequently concentrated on sepak takraw.<ref name="Withnews">{{cite news
|title=「日本代表になりたい....」セパタクローに転向「それぞれの理由」
|url=https://withnews.jp/article/f0190327002qq000000000000000W09n10301qq000018953A
|work=withnews
|date=27 March 2019
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref><ref name="JSTAF">{{cite web
|title=男子強化指定選手
|url=https://jstaf.jp/japan/team-man
|publisher=Japan Sepaktakraw Association
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref>

Takano represented Japan at the [[2010 Asian Games]] in Guangzhou, where he won a bronze medal in the men's team event. At the [[2014 Asian Games]] in Incheon, he won another bronze medal in the men's doubles event.<ref name="AiR">{{cite web
|title=髙野 征也（セパタクロー）
|url=https://www.airsleep.jp/asp/318.html
|publisher=AiR Athlete Support Program
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref>

At the 2016 All Japan Sepaktakraw Open Championship, Takano won the men's title. He also won the 2017 All Japan Sepaktakraw Championship.<ref name="AiR"/>

At the [[2018 Asian Games]] in Jakarta and Palembang, Takano won the silver medal in the men's quadrant event and the bronze medal in the men's team doubles event. He also won a bronze medal in men's doubles at the 2018 World Sepaktakraw Championships.<ref name="AiR"/><ref name="TakanoProfile">{{cite web
|title=髙野 征也（セパタクロー）
|url=https://www.airsleep.jp/asp/318.html
|publisher=AiR Athlete Support Program
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref>

In 2019, Takano was part of SC TOKYO, which finished second in the men's division of the All Japan Sepaktakraw Team Championship.<ref name="Athkatsu">{{cite web
|title=第６回全日本セパタクロー団体対抗戦で注目のSC TOKYOが準優勝！
|url=https://athkatsu.com/sports-events/5504/
|publisher=アスカツ
|date=2019
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref>

Takano represented Japan at the [[2022 Asian Games]] in Hangzhou in the men's quadrant and team regu events.<ref name="JOC2022">{{cite web
|title=髙野 征也
|url=https://www.joc.or.jp/games/asia/2022/japan/sepaktakraw/team/takanoseiya.html
|publisher=[[Japanese Olympic Committee]]
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref><ref name="JOCteam2022">{{cite web
|title=セパタクローのTEAM JAPAN
|url=https://www.joc.or.jp/games/asia/2022/japan/sepaktakraw/team/
|publisher=[[Japanese Olympic Committee]]
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref> Japan won the bronze medal in the men's quadrant event; Takano was among the Japanese players listed for the event.<ref name="TBS2023">{{cite news
|title=【アジア大会】大会10日目は男子4×100ｍリレーなど陸上で3個のメダル
|url=https://newsdig.tbs.co.jp/articles/-/756251?display=1
|work=TBS NEWS DIG
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref>

In January 2026, Takano was named a C-ranked tosā in the Japan Sepaktakraw Association's men's national-team strengthening squad for the first half of the year.<ref name="JSTAF2026">{{cite web
|title=2026年前期男女強化指定選手発表
|url=https://jstaf.jp/news/2026%E5%B9%B4%E5%89%8D%E6%9C%9F
|publisher=Japan Sepaktakraw Association
|date=11 January 2026
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref> In April, he was part of SC TOKYO's team that won the men's division of the seventh All Japan Quadrant Championship.<ref name="JSTAFquad2026">{{cite web
|title=結果報告 パル薬局 presents 第7回全日本クワッド選手権大会
|url=https://jstaf.jp/news/kekka-presents-7
|publisher=Japan Sepaktakraw Association
|date=12 April 2026
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref>

Takano was selected for Japan's men's sepak takraw team at the [[Sepak takraw at the 2026 Asian Games|2026 Asian Games]] in Aichi-Nagoya. He was listed among the Japanese representatives as a tosā and represented SC TOKYO.<ref name="TBS2026">{{cite news
|title=【選手一覧】セパタクロー 内藤利貴･髙野征也など 日本代表選手【アジア大会 愛知･名古屋 2026】
|url=https://newsdig.tbs.co.jp/articles/-/2867356?display=1
|work=TBS NEWS DIG
|date=16 September 2026
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref><ref name="SVOLME">{{cite web
|title=SEPAKTAKRAW JAPAN 2026–2029
|url=https://shop.svolme.net/view/page/sepak_takraw_japan_2026
|publisher=SVOLME
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref>

In the men's quadrant final on 3 October 2026, Japan faced Indonesia. Japan defeated Indonesia 2–1 to win the gold medal. Takano was part of the Japanese squad that secured the victory, which gave Japan its first Asian Games gold medal in sepak takraw since the sport was introduced to the Games in 1990. Japan also won the bronze medal in the men's team regu event at the Games.<ref name="JOC2026">{{cite news
|title=セパタクロー男子日本代表が歴史的快挙！ 強豪インドネシアを破りアジア大会史上初の金メダル獲得
|url=https://joc.or.jp/news/20261004_01.html
|publisher=[[Japanese Olympic Committee]]
|date=4 October 2026
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref><ref name="Bernama2026">{{cite news
|title=Asian Games 2026: Japan Defeats Indonesia For First Sepak Takraw Gold
|url=https://www.bernama.com/en/news.php?id=2615001
|work=Bernama
|date=3 October 2026
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref><ref name="ANTARA2026">{{cite news
|title=Perjuangan kuadran putra berakhir dengan perak sepak takraw
|url=https://www.antaranews.com/berita/5769697/perjuangan-kuadran-putra-berakhir-dengan-perak-sepak-takraw
|work=ANTARA News
|date=3 October 2026
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref><ref name="JOCmedals2026">{{cite web
|title=メダル・入賞者一覧
|url=https://www.joc.or.jp/games/asia/2026/japan/winnerslist/index_3.html
|publisher=[[Japanese Olympic Committee]]
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref>

In August 2026, Takano also competed in the men's quadrant at the [[King's Cup World Championships]]. Japan finished with the bronze medal after losing its semi-final to Myanmar.<ref name="KingCup2026">{{cite web
|title=第39回 King's Cup 世界選手権大会 全試合結果
|url=https://jstaf.jp/news/SGUnOr00
|publisher=Japan Sepaktakraw Association
|date=14 August 2026
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref><ref name="BunkaShutter">{{cite web
|title=「セパタクロー」と「VIVANT」がコラボ!?〖セパノート〗

}}</ref>
